parties:
Md. Baker Miah and others ------ Appellants
Vs.
Shamsun Nahar Begum ------ Respondent
full_judgment:
Md. Ruhul Amin J: The appeal, by leave, is by the defendant Nos. 3 and 4 against the judgment dated August 21, 2001 of a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 4139 of 1999 discharging the Rule obtained against the judgment and decree dated September 26, 1999 of the 8th Court of Additional District Judge, Dhaka in Title Appeal No. 301 of 1999 dismissing the same. The appeal was filed against the judgment and decree dated May 9, 1999 of the 2nd Additional Court of Assistant Judge, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 26 of 1998 decreeing the same. 

 3. The suit was contested by the defendant Nos.3 and 4 by filing written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint and stating, inter alia, that Zeon Bibi while owning and possessing the land her son Awlad Hossain died and as such Awlad Hossain did not inherit any property from Zeon Bibi and consequent thereupon Awlad Hossain's son Taleb Hossain and Monir Hossain did not acquire any interest in the land owned by Zeon Bibi, that on the death of Zeon Bibi her brother Abdul Hamid inherited the property left by Zeon Bibi, that he sold the land in suit to Kamaruddin on February 8, 1950, that to avoid future complications Kamaruddin obtained kabala from Taleb Hossain, father of the plaintiff on September 6, 1950 and thus became the owner of the land in suit and accordingly got the S.A. record prepared in his name, that Kamaruddin died leaving 6 daughters by name Shahida, Rashida, Shakila, Rina, Falani and Swriti and two brothers by name Zamiruddin and Alimuddin, that upon amicable arrangement between the co-sharers Zamiruddin got the land in suit and possessed the same, that after death of Zamiruddin the defendants got the land in suit by amicable settlement amongst the heirs and are possessing the land in suit, that plaintiff has no right, title and interest and possession in the land in suit, that the plaintiff has filed the suit making untrue statements and as such the same is liable to be dismissed. 

 4. The trial Court decreed the suit on the findings that the suit is maintainable and not barred by limitation, that the kabala dated September 6, 1950 by which Kamaruddin said to have purchased the land in suit from Taleb Hossain has not 1 been proved and as such by the said kabala Taleb Hossain's right in the land in suit was not affected, that there is no dispute that plaintiff is the daughter of Taleb Hossain and that defendant's contention that Taleb Hossain's father Awlad Hossain died before her mother Zeon Bibi has not been established and as such plaintiff has right, title and interest in the land in suit, that the plaintiff by reliable evidence, both oral and documentary, has established her possession in the land in suit and the papers filed by the defendants in support of their claim of possession in the land in suit are not related to the holding number of the land in suit, that plaintiffs suit is not bad for defect of party, that the plaintiff has been able to prove his case and as such entitled to the relief prayed for. 

 5. The contesting defendants went on appeal. The appellate Court on independent   discussions of the evidence, both oral and documentary, concurred with the findings and decisions of the trial Court and thereupon dismissed the appeal Thereupon the defendants moved the High Court Division in revisional jurisdiction and obtained the Rule. The High Court Division discharged the Rule on the findings that although defendants contended that plaintiffs father Awlad Hossain died before her mother Zeon Bibi but they failed to prove the said fact and the finding arrived at by the courts below that Zeon Bibi died leaving her son Awlad Hossain who died leaving sons Taleb Hossain and Monir Hossain is based on evidence, that kabala dated September 6, 1950 by which Kamaruddin said to have purchased the land from Taleb Hossain having not been proved the same has not affect the title of Taleb Hossain and consequently has also not affected the title of the plaintiff in the property of Taleb Hossain, that finding of the courts below as regard the possession of the Plaintiff is based on evidence and the said finding of the courts below does not suffer from misreading and non-consideration of the evidence on record, that the trial Court as well as the appellate Court on consideration of the evidence of P.W.2 in its entirety has correctly held that the said witness has stated that plaintiff is in possession of the land in suit, that plaintiffs possession in the land in suit is supported by the evidence of other P.Ws. as well as by the documentary evidence. 

 6. Leave was granted to consider the submissions that plaintiff although claimed possession through the tenants but none of such of the tenants was examined to prove plaintiffs possession in the land in suit, whereas the defendants by the evidence of D.Ws.4, 5 and 6 who are tenants in the land in suit proved possession of the defendants but the trial Court as well as the appellate Court without discussing and considering the evidence of P.WS. and on the weakness of the case of the defendants decreed the suit, the High Court Division did not consider this aspect of the case and thus committed error of law in discharging the Rule without considering that none of the courts below recorded any finding as to the proof of title by the plaintiff but decreed the suit on the alleged failure of the defendants to prove their title, that having regard to the pleadings of the plaintiff in that at the first instance it was the case of the plaintiff that plaintiffs predecessor died before her mother leaving sons Taleb Hossain and Monir Hossain but by amendment the plaintiff introduced a new story that Zeon Bibi died leaving son Awlad who died leaving sons Taleb Hossain and Monir Hossain and that on the death of Taleb Hossain plaintiff got 4 annas share in the property of Taleb Hossain and as such the courts below were in error in decreeing the suit on the afore-said assertion of the facts and on the untenable plea and on the untenable ground that defendants were required to prove the same and thus wrongly shifted the onus on the defendants and thereby caused failure of justice, that because of the contradictory nature of pleading of the plaintiff as to death of Zeon Bibi preceding her son Awlad Hossain the High Court Division as well as the courts below were in error in presuming that the plaintiff has acquired title through devolution without any evidence produced by the plaintiff to that end and as to her dealing with the property in any manner whatsoever and without prove of fact of death of Awlad Hossain after the death of her mother Zeon Bibi, that defendants produced the original document of title from their custody namely registered deed dated 8.2.1950 and 6.9.1950 which are being document of over 30 years the High Court Division was in error in holding that the courts below on proper consideration of the evidence correctly held that the kabala of the contesting defendants said to have been executed and registered by Taleb Hossain was not established as genuine and thereby committed serious error affecting the judgment. 

 7. The learned Counsel for the appellants in support of the appeal upon reiterating the contentions for the consideration whereof leave was obtained by the appellants also submitted that finding as to title and possession by the High Court Division as well as the courts below were arrived at without discussing evidence and the findings that defendants' documents on the basis whereof they are claiming title and possession were not proved by them is contrary to the materials on record or in other words the Court was not correct in holding that defendants failed to prove their documents on the basis whereof they claimed title in the land in suit and the courts below have decreed the suit of the plaintiff on the defendants' failure to prove their case. 

 8. As against that it has been submitted on behalf of the Respondent that the High Court Division as well as the Courts below upon due consideration and appreciation of the evidence correctly held that plaintiff has right, title, interest and possession in the land in suit. The teamed Counsel has also submitted that plaintiff by reliable evidence has established that her grandfather Awlad was alive when Zeon Bibi, mother of Awlad Hossain died. It has also been submitted on behalf of the Respondent that holding number of the suit land is 53, but the papers filed by the defendants in support of the claim of title and possession in the land in suit are of holding No.53/1. Lastly it has been submitted that as the plaintiff was successful in preying her right, title, interest and possession in the land in suit the case put forward from defendants' side that on the death of Zeon Bibi his brother Abdul Hamid inherited the property in suit and lie sold the same to Kamaruddin and that to avoid complications Kamaruddin obtained document from Taleb Hossain in respect of the land in suit and that Kamaruddin possessed the land and after him his successors-in-interest including the defendants possessed the land in suit has rightly been held by the High Court Division as well as the courts below is not correct. 

 10. It was the case of the defendants that Zeon Bibi had a son Awlad Hossain who had two sons Taleb Hossain and Monir Hossain and Awlad Hossain died before his mother Zeon Bibi and as such Awlad Hossain's heirs Taleb Hossain and Monir Hossain did not inherit the property of Zeon Bibi since he was survived by her brother Abdul Hamid and on the death of Zeon Bibi her property devolved upon Zeon Bibi's brother Abdul Hamid. It may be mentioned plaintiff is claiming the property in suit as daughter of Taleb Hossain. Since defendants urged upon the Court to accept their contention that Zeon Bibi's son Awlad was not alive when Zeon Bibi died and as such Awlad's sons Taleb Hossain and Monir Hossain did not inherit the property of Zeon Bibi the defendants under the provision of the Evidence Act was required to establish that fact but from the defendants' side no reliable evidence Was brought on record for the establishment of the said fact. This baiting the position in our view trial Court as well as the lower appellate Court and lastly the High Court Division was quite correct in holding that plaintiff inherited the property of her father Taleb who as son of Awlad Hossain had interest in the land in suit. The plaintiff in support of her case that Zeon Bibi died leaving her son Awlad Hossain deposed as P.W.1 and that fact indirectly has been established through the evidence of P.Ws.2-5 who have stated that plaintiff got the property as heir of Taleb Hossain. As stated hereinbefore Taleb Hossain is the son of Awlad Hossain who got the property in suit from her mother Zeon Bibi. As against the said evidence of the P.Ws. from the defendants' side no evidence was brought on record to show that the evidence of the P.Ws. is not correct or in other words to establish that plaintiff's predecessor Awlad Hossain son of Zeon Bibi died before Zeon Bibi. It has also been submitted by the learned Counsel for the appellants that plaintiff initially stated in her plaint that Zeon Bibi died leaving her grandsons Taleb Hossain and Monir Hossain through her son Awlad Hossain but lateron the plaintiff upon amendment introduced a quite different story to the effect that Abdul Barek, Hayatunnessa, Daulat Bi, Mohor Bi and Ratan Bi by the kabala dated April 4, 1940 sold the land left by Yousuf Ali to Zeon Bibi and she died leaving only son Awlad Hossain and he died leaving sons Taleb Hossain and Monir Hossain and Taleb Hossain died leaving plaintiff and his brother Monir Hossain and thus plaintiff inherited .0575 arzutangsha or in other words .5¾ decimals of land and the same is the land in suit and as such the Court was in error in accepting the story so introduced by amendment and lateron in allowing to lead evidence in support thereof. The submission so made merits no consideration since no material is on record to show that amendment so sought by the plaintiff and allowed by the Court was challenged from the defendants' side, rather it is seen that defendants upon accepting the amendment made by the plaintiff contested the suit. It may be mentioned it was the case of the defendants that Zeon Bibi's property was inherited by her brother Abdul Hamid and he sold the property so inherited by him from Zeon Bibi to Kamaruddin by the kabala dated 8.2.1950 and that Kamaruddin to avoid future complications obtained a kabala on September 6, 1950 from Taleb Hossain as regard the property left by Zeon Bibi and that Kamaniddin while owning and possessing the property so purchased from Abdul Hamid and Taleb Hossain died leaving two brothers and six daughters and that upon amicable partition Kamaruddin's brother Zamiruddin got the property in suit and said Zamiruddin died leaving 5 daughters and upon amicable partition amongst the said heirs of Zamiruddin defendant Nos.1 and 2 got the land in suit. As stated herein before from the defendants' side no evidence was brought on record that Zeon Bibi's son Awlad Hossain died before her. The said fact having not been established there, was no question of inheriting Zeon Bibi's property by Abdul Hamid and as such Kamamddin by purchase from Abdul Hamid did not acquire any interest in the land in suit and consequent thereupon on Kamaruddin's death his heirs or successors-in-interest including the defendants did not acquire any interest in the land in suit. It was contended from the defendants' side that the High Court Division as well as the courts below were not correct in holding that defendants' document on the basis of which they are claiming right, title, interest and possession in the land in suit were not proved. It has already been held by its that Abdul Humid did not inherit any property from his sister Zeon Bibi and as such by purchase from Abdul Hamid, Kamaruddin did not acquire any interest in the land of Zeon Bibi. It was the case of the defendants that Kamaruddin also made purchase from Taleb Hossain son of Awlad Hossain who got the property from his mother Zeon Bibi. The defendants to prove the document which said to have been executed and registered by Taleb Hossain on September 6, 1950 in respect of the property he inherited from his father Awlad Hossain who inherited the property of Zeon Bibi have not examined any witness i.e. the attesting witness of the kabala nor the scribe of the kabala. In that state of the matter we are of the view High Court Division as well as the courts below were quite correct in holding that defendants did not prove their documents on the basis of which they are claiming the land in suit. It was submitted by the learned Counsel for the appellants that defendants proved their claim of possession in the land in suit through the evidence of D.Ws. 4, 5 and 6. It may be mentioned the admitted fact is that holding number of the land in suit is 53 and that fact finds place in the evidence of D.Ws.1, 2, 3 and 5. It is in the evidence of D.W.4 that he does not know who filed the suit against whom. D.W.5 has deposed that the number of the suit holding is 53 and D.W.6 has stated that his son is the tenant of the defendants. This being the evidence of the said witnesses as regard the possession as claimed by the defendants in respect of the land in suit the High Court Division and the courts below have quite correctly discarded the evidence of the said witnesses through whom defendants tried to prove their claim of possession in the land in suit.

lawyer:
Syed Mojizur Rahman for AH Md Shahadat Ali Khan, Advocate------For the Petitioner.

parties:
Abdur Rahim Chowkrder @ Abdur Rahman Sheikh since deceased ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Raji Haider and others ------ .Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
Md Abdur Rashid J: Defendant No. 1 obtained the Rule upon making a revision application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure against judgment and decree dated 18-2-1990 passed by District Judge at Pirojpur in Title Appeal No. 8 of 1989 affirming those dated 31-12-1988 passed by Assistant Judge at Sadar in Pirojpur in Title Suit No. 50 of 1988, which decreed the suit in its entirety. 

 (b) the plaintiffs have got title in the suit land; and 

 4. Plaint case, in short, is that land of RS Khatian Nos. 197, 261 and 783 as described in schedule 'Ka' originally belonged to Nani Bala, who transferred said land to Bimal Krishna Debnath. Bimal Debnath then transferred the land to Ishaque Ali Miah, predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiffs by a registered 'Kabala' dated 12-4-1973. 

 5. Defendant No. 4 on 13-12-1973 got a decree in Title Suit No. 56 of 1972 of Second Court of Subordinate Judge at Barishal in respect of 1.11 acres of the suit land on the basis of 'Pattan' claimed to have been obtained by his mother. When the predecessor of the plaintiffs challenged the decree by instituting a suit, defendant No.4, on compromise, transferred 53.75 decimals of the suit land by a 'Kabala' dated 15-8-1987 to plaintiff Nos. 1 to 7. 

 7. Thus, Ishaque Ali, said predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiffs, acquired good title and possession in the entire land of schedule 'ka'. Then, he died leaving the plaintiffs as his only heirs and legal representatives. The plaintiffs possessed those lands through 'Bargaders'. 

 8. In 1394 BS, the suit land was given to defendant No. 1 for 'Borga' cultivation. When defendant No. 1 refused to give 'Borga' share to the plaintiffs, they started CR Case being No. 17 of 1988 in the local Upazila Magistrate Court. During the prosecution of the case defendant No. 1 declared that he had title and possession in the suit land, which was recorded in the record of rights in the name of his father Hashem Ali. The plaintiffs also came to know that Hashem Ali obtained an ex parte decree in Title Suit No. 49 of 1957 and got the record corrected in his name on the basis of the decree. 

 9. Further case of the plaintiffs is that defendant No. 2 in collusion with defendant No. 1 refused to execute a deed relinquishing all claims in the suit land in their favour. They claimed to be in possession of the entire suit land for more than twelve years and defendants had no title or possession in the suit land. 

 10. Defendant No. 1 alone contested the suit by filing a written statement. His case in short, is that his father Hashem Ali Sheikh got the suit land by way of 'Pattan'. When he was thus owner in possession of the suit land, the suit land was wrongly recorded in the names of original owners in the survey under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. Hashem Ali was then constrained to institute Title Suit No. 49 of 1957 against original tenants including those the plaintiffs claimed to have acquired title for declaration of title practically for correction of the record of rights and got a decree on 28-10-1957. On the basis of the decree, Hashem Ali made an application being Miscellaneous Case No. 4222/60-61 under section 54 for correction of the record and got an order on 28-3-1961. Then, the record was finally corrected in Mutation Case No. 9P/87-88 and the suit land was recorded in his name. Hashem Ali possessed 5.02 acres including the suit land until his death and after him defendant No. 1 continued possessing said land as his sole heir for more than 12 years by making a dwelling and living therein; and also by cultivation. 

 11. The plaintiffs started a false criminal case under sections 406 and 420 and destroyed by setting fire the huts of defendant No. 1 on the suit land and looted away his belongings by hired goons. The defendant filed a criminal case being GR Case No. 33 of 1988 in the Court of the Upazila Magistrate against the plaintiffs over trespass and looting, which was pending. Having found that they had no hope in their criminal case, the plaintiffs instituted instant suit on false allegations. They got no title or possession in the suit land. 

 (e) Had the plaintiffs any right, title, interest or possession in the suit land? 

 (f) Whether the order dated 14-1-1988 passed in Mutation Case No. 9P/87-88 was binding upon the plaintiffs? and (g) What relief or reliefs the plaintiffs were entitled to? 

 15. In the absence of any declaration sought for against the decree dated 28-10-1957 passed in Title Suit No. 49 of 1957 and order dated 28-3-1961 passed in Case No. 4222/60-61 for correction of the record of rights, he submits, the plaintiffs are not entitled to any decree. 

 24. As stated at the outset, the plaintiffs instituted the suit for declarations that they have got title in the suit land, that defendant No.2 Ramendra Nath was 'Benamdar' of their father Ishaque Aii in respect of sale deeds dated 28-12-1972 and 1-4- 1974 and that the order dated 14-1-1988 passed in Mutation Case No. 9P/87-88 was illegal, void and not binding upon them. 

 25. Needless to say that in order to succeed in the suit the plaintiffs would have first to establish their title and then, possession in the suit land. It is the case of the plaintiffs that their predecessor-in- interest, Ishaque Ali acquired title by way of purchase in the name of defendant No.2 Ramendra Nath by two registered sale deeds dated 18-12-1972 and 1-4-1974 and defendant No. 4 Abdul Salek transferred 53.75 decimals by a registered sale deed dated 15-8-1987 to the plaintiff Nos. 1 to 7 on the basis of a compromise in the suit brought by him. 

 26. In support, the plaintiffs adduced five 'kabalas' dated 12-4-1973, 28-12-1972, 15-8-1987, 29-12-1972 and 1-4-1974, which were marked as Exhibits 1 to 1(d). All the deeds were produced in original. 

 32. But upon such application that Ishaque Ali paid the consideration, that defendant No. 2 admitted to be a 'Benamdar' of Ishaque Ali, and the fact that the deeds dated 29-12-1972 and 1-4-1974 in original, Exhibit 1 (c) and Exhibit 1 (d), were produced from the custody of the plaintiffs, the trial Court held that Ishaque Ali purchased said 1.40 acre of land in the 'Benami' of defendant No. 2 Ramendra Nath. Appellate Court just dittoed such finding of the trial Court. 

 44. On the other hand, defendant No.2 deposed as DW 1 that his father took 'Pattan' of the suit land along with other land from recorded tenants Indobhushan, Nani Bala, Rebuti Ranjan, Subhasini and Sarala Bala long ago. He could not say how his father took 'Pattan'. His father used to possess the land on the basis of 'Pattan'. His father obtained a decree in Title Suit No. 47 of 1957 in respect of the suit land. In 1968, his father died leaving him as one son and one daughter. He started cultivating the suit land since the death of his father and living in the huts raised. He got the land mutated on the basis of the decree. He paid 'Chowkidari' tax. 

 50. In support of his case, defendant No.1 also adduced a certified copy of the plaint in Title Suit No. 49 of 1957 filed on 4-2-1957, order dated 28-10-1957 decreeing the suit ex parte and decree drawn. They were marked as Exhibit-A, A (1) and A(3). Certified copies were obtained on 13-3-1980. No doubt could be cast on the authenticity of the certified copies. But the Courts below found that the certified copies were created for the suit. 

 51. Had genuineness of any of the copies struck the eyes in any way, then who prevented them to verify the copies with the originals which were not far away from them. Moreover, there was no evidence adduced to create any doubt. Rather, it was the case of the plaintiffs that they came to know that the defendant No. 1's father obtained a decree in respect of the suit land. As Corts of fact, lower Courts are required to give decision on proof, not doubt. Any decision based on doubt cannot be binding and/or sustained in revision. 

 54. It may again be remembered that in a suit for declaration of title only production of deeds of purchase without proof of title and possession of their previous owners within twelve years of the suit would not entitle the plaintiff(s) to any decree. The suit would be doomed to fail. 

 55. But the trial Court appears to have been swayed away when the defendant No. 1 could not say definitely on the 'Pattan' obtained by his father. It reasoned that defendant No. 1 then failed to prove his title. Possession follows title. It forgot to place the burden of proof on right side. 

 56. The defendant No. 1 did not seek any declaration of title in the suit land. It is the plaintiffs who instituted the suit for declaration of their title in the suit land. Burden was therefore, on them to prove their title. Defendant No. 1 just took the defence that he had title in the suit land on the basis of the decree obtained by his father. 

 57. In support of the decree, defendant No.1 adduced certified copy of the plaint of Title Suit No. 49 of 1957, entire order sheet of said suit and the decree passed therein. Besides, certified copy' of order sheet of Case No. 4222/1960-61 and Mutation Case No. 9p/1987-88. Decree was passed against Indobhushan, Saralabala, Rabuti Ranjan, Nagendra Nath and others from whom the plaintiffs and their predecessor-in-interest Ishaque Ali claimed title. Such decree was though passed ex parte yet binding upon not only the judgment debtors but also any of their successors-in-interest. 

 58. The plaintiffs however, did not seek any relief against the decree. Nor did they challenge the decree in the suit. In the context of such suit, the defendant No.1 was not required to prove 'Pattan'. The Courts below therefore fell in serious error in holding against the defendant No.1 for his failure in not adducing evidence on 'Pattan'. Moreover, it must be remembered that long continuous possession for more than statutory period of twelve years has perfected any defect that may be found in the title of defendant No.1 in the suit land and other land possessed by him. 

 59. For foregoing reasons, the plaintiffs must be held to have failed to prove title and/or possession in the suit land. Finding on possession, however concurrent by the Courts below, being not based on the evidence oral and documentary and law, cannot be binding in revision. The case is very old. So, I had to take pain to find afresh the issues the parties are found to be in variance on the basis of the evidence on record and law.

lawyer:
Mr. Kazi Mozzammelul Huq with Mr. M. A. Gaffar ------- for the petitioners. 
Mr. M. A. Samad with, Mr. M.G.H. Ruhullah ------- for the opposite parties.
parties:
Fazlur Rahman and others
Vs.
Anjab Khan being dead his heirs Haji Md. Manir Khan & Ors.
full_judgment:
Md. Mizanur Rahman Bhuiyan, J: This Rule was issued directing against the judgment and decree dated 13.8.1998 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Anti Smugling Tribunal, Sylhet in Title Appeal No. 103 of 1979 affirming those dated 19.02.1979 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 2nd Additional Court, Sylhet in Title Suit No. 8 of 1978 decreeing the suit. 

 The predecessor of the opposite parties as plaintiff filed on 12.09.1973 title Suit No. 233 of 1973 (renumbered at Title Suit No. 8 of 1978) before the learned Sub-ordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Sylhet for declaration of Title in schedule-1 and confirmation of possession in respect of land described in Schedule-11 and for recovery of khas possession in respect of lands described in Schedule-111. The case of the plaintiff opposite parties in brief was that, the suit land originally belonged to Romesh Chandra Chowdhury amongst them Romesh Chandra Chowdhury died, leaving behind Ratish Chowdhury and Suresh Chandra Chowdhury died leaving behind only son Sankar Prasad Chowdhury, the proforma defendants No. 13 and 14 respectively. That the Proforma defendants Nos. 13 and 14 entered into an agreement for sale with the plaintiff for the suit land with a consideration of Tk. 15,000/- and executed a Bainapatra on 14.4.1969 in favour of the plaintiff on receipt of Tk. 13,000/- and delivered possession thereof and they agreed to execute the requisite kabala within three months on receipt of balance consideration, but on being refused the original plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 202 of 1969 for specific performance of Contract against the proforma defendant Nos. 13 and 14 and got decree on 26.01.70 and also the requisite kabala on 11.02.72 through court vide Title execution case No. 5 of 1970. That defendant Nos. 1-3, 9-12 and predecessor of defendant Nos. 4-8 created some false, fraud, fraudulent collusive and anti-dated documents by false personification, The aforesaid defendants wrongfully and forcefully dispossessed the plaintiffs on 06.9.1972 from the suit 3rd Schedule land and also threatened to dispossess from the suit 2nd schedule land and hence the suit. 

 3. Defendant No. I contested the suit by filing written statements and contended inter alia that, the suit was barred by limitation and bad for defect of parties and also stated that, the proforma defendant Nos. 13 and 14 never executed any Bainapatra or delivered possession of the suit land, that Suresh had no son in the name of Sankar (Proforma opposite party No. 14), but died leaving behind two sons namely Subrata and Shuhendu; that Ratish Chowdhury proforma defendant No. 13 sold Dag No. 2569 of the 2nd schedule comprising an area of 2.16 acres to this defendant by, registered kabala dated 03.06.1972 and delivered possession thereof and since then this defendant was possessing the same. The further case of the defendant petitioner was that Subrata and Shubendu sons of Suresh Chowdhury contracted to sell Dag No. 2283 of the 2nd schedule land with defendant Nos. 1 and 2 on 10.04.1964 and delivered possession thereof. That the defendant took settlement in 1358 B.S. of the suit 3rd scheduled land from the zamindar Romesh Chandra Chowdhury and Suresh Chandra Chowdhury and since then was possessing the same as residence and living there with their family. That as the record of right wrongly prepared in the name of Ex-land Lord, this defendant filed Title Suit No. 150 of 1969 in the first court of Munsif Sylhet for correction of the record of rights; that the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No. 202 of 19769 was not binding upon this defendant as he was not a party to the suit and that the plaintiff had no right title or interest over the suit land and hence prayed for dismissal of the suit. 

 4. The trial court on hearing the suit de-creed the same by his judgment and decree dated 13.8.1998 and against the aforesaid judgment and decree the petitioner preferred Title Appeal No. 103 of 1979 before the learned District Judge, Sylhet, which on transfer was heard by the learned Additional District Judge, 2nd court, Sylhet who sent the case back on remand by his judgment and decree dated 31.12.1981. A Civil Revision No. 262 of 1982 against the aforesaid Judgment and decree was preferred by the plaintiff before the High Court Division and the rule was made absolute on 29.04.1993. Thereafter the learned Additional District Judge, Sylhet, heard the matter afresh and dismissed the appeal 13.8.1998. 

 6. Mr. Kazi Mozzammelul Huq with, Mr. M.A. Gaffer, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submitted that both the courts below committed serious error of law in passing their judgments and decrees in not appreciating the settled principle of law that the plaintiff was to succeed on the basis of his own evidence and not on the witnesses of the other side if any., He further, submitted that both the Courts on misreading and non-reading the oral and documentary evidence disbelieved the case of the defendant No. 1. He further argued that both the courts below failed to appreciate the proof of defendants title by of pattan, kabala, Bainapatra and all the evidence on his side proved the said facts and also the possession of defendant No.1. Both the courts below misdirected themselves in holding a ground that the plaintiff failed to state specifying the suit land and further the failed to appreciate the provision as laid town in section 30 of State Acquisition of Tenancy Act of 1950. He finally argued that the plain-tiffs opposite party completely failed to prove possession followed by dispossession by any sufficient oral and documentary evidence. In support of his contention he referred the case of Imanuddin Barbi vs. Lilabati Das, reported in 32 DLR-75, Sultan Ahmed vs. Md. Waziullah and others, reported in 7 BLD-235, Munshi Dudhu in and others vs. Rahimuddin and others, reported in 16 DLR 56, Barada Prasanna Lod and others, vs. Kobbad Mia, reported in 13 DLR-765, The Crown vs. Mongal Khan, reported in 6 DLR-490. 

 7. Mr. M. A. Samid with, Mr. M.G.H. Ruhullah, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite parties submitted that both the courts below acted legally and com-mitted no mistake in passing their judgments and decrees. He further argued that the trial court rightly observed that Suresh had only one son which was evident from the fact that the defendant in Title Suit No. 150 of 1969 for correction of record of right made Subrata Chowdhury son of late Suresh Chowdhury as defendant No. 2 and none else and this clearly showed that Suresh had only one son and it also got strength from the certified copy of the petition filed by defendant in Title Execution Case No. 5 of 1970. In the said petition Sunkar was admitted by the defendant as only son of Suresh and from this evidence it was clear that Suresh had only one son namely Sankar and not Subrata. He also submitted that the lower appellate court had rightly observed that Ext.-C হইতেছে দেওয়ানী ১৫০/১৯৬৯ নং মোকদ্দমার ডিক্রীর সই মুহুরী নকল। উক্ত দেওয়ানী ১৫০/১৯৬৯ নং মোকদ্দমাটি বাদী ইন্তাজ আলী দায়ের করেন রেকর্ড সংশোধনের মোকদ্দমা এবং উক্ত মোকদ্দমার ২নং বিবাদী হিসাবে সুব্রত চন্দ্র চৌধুরী পিল মৃত সুরেশ চন্দ্র চৌধুরীকে একমাত্র ছেলে হিসাবে দেখানো হয়েছে। পি.ডব্লিউ-১ অঞ্জন খা তাহার জবান বন্দীতে বলেন ১৪নং বিবাদী শংকর প্রসাদ চৌধুরী সুরেশ চন্দ্র এর একমাত্র ছেলে। --------   and on this score the lower appellate court had observed that though the defendant No. 1, dismissed the decree of the Title Suit No. 202 of 1969 and also Title Execution No. 5 of 1970 but the defendant did not file any suit challenging the legality of Title Suit No. 202 of 1969 and Title execution Case No. 5 of 1970 and as such the judgment and decree passed by the learned trial court in Title Suit No. 202 of 1969 was valid in the eye of law. He finally argued that the petitioner never was in possession of the suit property since he neither mentioned his possession any where in written statement or memo appeal or Revisional application. In support of his argument he referred the cases of Zamir Uddin Ahmed Vs. Ziaul Huq and others, reported in 49 DLR622 and Md. Shah Alam Vs. Musammat Panda Begum, reported in 17BLD(AD)145.

caseno:
Appeal from Original Order (FMA) No. 34 of 2004 
with Civil Rule No. 736 (FM) of 2003.
parties:
Arab Bangladesh Bank Ltd ------ Appellant
Vs. 
Janata Bank and ors ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
2. It appears from the record that AB Bank instituted Title Suit No. 125 of 1992 in the Third Artha Rin Adalat at Dhaka and obtained a preliminary decree on 29-7-99 for Taka 87,79,388 as was due on 30-6-92. The decree was made final on 14-8-2000. Then, on 25-3-2001, AB Bank levied the decree in Title Execution Case No. 38 of 2001 in the same Artha Rin Adalat for realisation of Taka 4,18,65,415. 

 4. Respondent No. 1 Janata Bank also instituted Title Suit 217 of 1933 in the Fourth Artha Rin Adalat at Dhaka and obtained a preliminary decree on 5-9-99 for Taka 1,14,65,356 as was due on 30-9-93. On 17-7-2000 the decree was made final. Then, Janata Bank on 23-11-2000 started Title Execution Case No.150 of 2000 for realisation of Taka 2,59,49,528. In execution, Janata Bank also got attached very same property which was already mortgaged to it. The execution case was then renumbered as Title Execution Case No. 1210 of 2003. 

 5. Having come to know of such execution, on 19-11-2003. AB Bank made an application under Order XXII, rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure in Title Execution Case No. 1210 of 2003 for release of the property from attachment and said application was registered as Miscellaneous Case No. 41 of 2003. The Fourth Artha Rin Adalat ultimately, fixed 1-12-03 for hearing on maintainability of the application. On the date, AB Bank also filed an application for an order for analogous hearing of the miscellaneous case with that of the Third Artha Rin Adalat. 

 8. He however submitted that on the very same date, 1-12-2003, AB Bank made an application under section 27(1) read with section of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 (Act VIII of 2003), hereinafter referred as the Ain, in Title Execution Case No. 38 of 2001 of Third Artha Rin Adalat for sending its decree to the Fourth Artha Rin Adalat for execution. But Third Artha Rin Adalat rejected the application by an order passed on the same date. 

 10. Mr Shamim Khaled Ahmed, learned Advocate for the respondent No.1, submitted that the attached property was already mortgaged to Janata Bank by a registered deed of mortgages dated 31-5-84 being No. 19664. Said judgment-debtor deposited the Title deeds in original, which were kept in the custody of Janata Bank. After repeated attempts for sale of the property in auction, Fourth Artha Rin Adalat found the bid of respondent No. 15 for Taka 6,07,00,000 best available market price and accepted the bid. 

 20. Fourth Artha Rin Adalat also appears to be not at all aware of rule 62 of Order XXI of the Code of Civil Procedure and consequence of summary rejection of an application made under Order XXI, rule 58 under the rule. In India and Pakistan, in order to obviate the legal effect, rule 62 is amended and now, all questions relating to right, title and interest of the claimant or objector in the attached property shall have to be adjudicated upon and determined by the executing Court; and no separate suit shall lie to establish such title, right or interest. 

 22. In the result, the appeal is disposed of without however any order as to cost. Third Artha Rin Adalat is directed to send the decree dated 29-7-99 passed by it in Title Suit No. 125 of 1992 to the Fourth Artha Rin Adalat for execution and Fourth Artha Rin Adalat is directed to execute both the decrees in accordance with law.
