parties:
Wahida Bewa and others ------- Plaintiffs-Respondents-Petitioners
VS
Champa Bewa and others ------- Defendant Nos. 1- 1 10/13-17/19-26-Appellants -Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
At the instance of the plaintiffs-respondents-petitioners, a Rule was issued calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and order dated 10-3-2022 passed by learned Additional District Judge, First Court, Bogura, in Miscellaneous Appeal No.63 of 2021 reversing the order dated 24-2-2021 passed by learned Joint District Judge, First Court, Bogura, in Title Suit No. 308 of 2020 should not be set-aside and/or such other or further order or orders be passed as to this court may deem fit and proper. 

 3. Short facts leading to the under-standing of this revisional application are that these plaintiffs-respondents-petitioners instituted Title Suit No.308 of 2020 in the court of learned Joint District Judge, First Court, Bogura for declaration of title simpliciter wherein an application for temporary injunction was filed by them seeking restraint order against defendant Nos. 1, 2, 6 not to interfere with petitioners' peaceful possession in and enjoyment of the suit land. 

 4. It was also stated in the application that the suit property originally belonged to Ainullah Sarker, a CS recorded tenant, who declined paying rent to the superior landlord. This generated Rent Suit No.1203 of 1929 in the then Munsif Court, Bogura and Pabna against the defaulter tenant. The suit was decreed and the decree was put into execution. Norohori Shaha purchased the suit land and others in auction. The wife of Norohori Saha used to have certain other lands. Both of them executed a power of attorney to the Deputy Commissioner, Bogura to execute an exchange deed regarding the suit land and other in favour of Khajer Muhammad Shah, Md. Ruhul Amin Shah, Md. Yakub Ali Shah and Khatem Shah. They, however, obtained the properties vide exchange deed dated 6-1-1975. After the death of Khajer Muhammad Shah, his heirs Bibiran, the wife, Ruhul Amin and Yakub Ali Shah, the sons, Fatema and 5 others, the daughters, became the owner of the properties left by Khajer Muhammad Shah. By means of consecutive transfer, Md. Ruhul Amin, the son of Khajer Muhammad Shah acquired 3.32 acres of land being the suit land. While possessing the land, he died leaving behind the plaintiffs-respondents-petitioners who acquired title to the suit land and have been possessing therein by way of paying rent to the government. The defendants-appellants-opposite parties concerned without having any little title to and possession in that amount of land threatened to dispose these petitioners which resulted in filing by them the temporary injunction petition. 

 5. The trial court upon examination of the chain of title of the petitioners and perusing the documents of possession was pleased to allow the temporary injunction petition vide order No. 24-2-2021. 

 9.2 Mr. Abdul Momin further submits that a clear case of title is manifest on documents and inspite of producing sufficient essential documents of possession, the learned appellate court erroneously set-aside the temporary injunction order passed appropriately by learned Joint District Judge. 

 10. I have gone through at length the averments made in the application for revision and the grounds suggested therein. I've examined the original order of granting temporary injunction by learned Joint District Judge and also the impugned judgment and order along with observations focused therein. Documents and materials relevant for the purpose of disposal of the temporary injunction petition and the propriety of the impugned order have further been examined by me. 

 11. It, however, transpires from the order of learned Joint District Judge granting temporary injunction that he has taken into consideration the chain of title enunciated in the original suit and documents of possession of the adversaries. Upon appreciation of the documents of title between the parties, the learned Joint District Judge found prima facie arguable case in the suit and he, however, concluded affirmative decision in favour of the plaintiffs-respondent-petitioners in awarding the order of temporary injunction in order to protect the subject matter of the suit till finality thereof. But the impugned judgment, as is evident therefrom, is quite silent about the interpretation and decision as to what is an arguable prima facie case. The appellate court in a slipshod manner decided the plaintiffs-respondents-petitioners to have prima facie arguable case in the suit. 

 12. In the absence of any definition of 'prima fade' in the Civil Procedure Code, judicial pronouncements have been developed in the matter. Prima facie arguable case means a case in support of which there are arguments which can be taken into consideration and decision is to be taken at the time of trial. A prima facie case is not a case of full title but prima facie case means where the plaintiff has a case at first sight upon which there is scope of argument by the parties. In the instant circumstances, it appears that the plaintiffs-respondents-petitioners have submitted different documents supporting their chain of title. The genuineness of the documents is subject to trial on evidence and no conclusive determination of title is possible at this premature and pre-trial stage. 

 14. Order XLI, rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure lays down the contents of a judgment to be passed by appellate court wherein the appellate court is obliged to determine the points for determination and to decide those points with specific reasons therefor. In the impugned judgment, we are unable to find that the learned appellate court has ever reversed the findings of the learned trial court with specific findings of its own. The learned Joint District Judge has organised findings upon title and possession of the plaintiffs to the suit land on perusal of the documents submitted in the suit, whereas, the impugned judgment does not have any such clarity of possession and prima facie arguable case being the paramount consideration in granting or, rejecting an application for temporary injunction. 

 17. The impugned judgment and order dated 10-3-2022 passed by learned Additional District Judge, First Court, Bogura, in Miscellaneous Appeal No.63 of 2021 is set aside. The order of granting temporary injunction passed by learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Bogura in Title Suit No.380 of 2020 is hereby restored.

caseno: First Appeal No. 195 of 2018 with Civil Revision No. 1594 of 2019.
parties:
Rafiqul Islam and others --------- Appellants
vs
Shahanara Begum and others ---------- Respondents
full_judgment:
Md Ali Reza, J.: At the time of delivery of judgment the opposite party has come with an application for inclusion of certain words “স্বত্ত্ব সাব্যস্ত পূর্বক” as declaration of title in the prayer portion of the plaint which will be considered in the body of the judgment. 

 3. In civil revision Rule at the instance of defendant 6 was issued calling upon the opposite parties 1-8 to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 13-2-2019 passed by the Additional District Judge, Court No. 2, Dhaka in Title Appeal 38 of 2018 dismissing the appeal thereby affirming the judgment and decree dated 31-10-2017 passed by the Joint District Judge, Court No. 2, Dhaka in Title Suit 591 of 2015 decreeing the suit. 

 4. The heirs of defendant 6 in civil revision has preferred the instant appeal challenging the judgment and decree dated 31-10-2017 passed by the Joint District Judge Court No. 2, Dhaka in Title Suit 432 of 2015 dismissing the suit. 

 6. Plaintiff filed Title Suit 127 of 1957 in the Court of Sadar 3rd Munsif, Dhaka on 24-8-1957 for declaration of title and recovery of possession in respect of 'Kha' schedule land under schedule 'Ka' to the plaint contending that the 4Ka' schedule land belonged to Subodh Chandra Ghosh and Shrish Chandra Ghosh, They sold the land to as many as eight persons including the vendor of the plaintiff named Mir Mabtab Uddin with demarcation and division of different plots by hahala dated 2-1-1953. Mahtab acquired ownership with possession in D marked plot mentioned in the map of the kabala. He sold 

 8. Defendants 2 and 4 filed separate written statements on 13-2-1958 and 28-12-1957 respectively. Court framed 5(five) issues on 13-3- 1958. Plaintiff filed an application on 15-5-1958 for appointment of pleader commissioner to hold local investigation and the application was allowed and the report was submitted on 5-9- 1959. After filing of written statement on 20-8-1963 defendant 6 filed objection against commissioner's report on 16-4-1965. Defendant 2 filed objection on 26-5-1965. Report was accepted on 23-4-1969. Mominullah (sole plaintiff) died in 1973 and his heirs were substituted on 3-11-1974. Mesbaul Alam one of the sons of Mominullah deposed as PW .1 on 14-1-1999 after 42(forty two) years of filing of the suit and the suit was decreed ex-parte on the same day and Execution Case 13 of 1999 started. Abdul Aziz Khan (defendant 6) died in 2002 and his heirs started Miscellaneous Case 95 of 2004 for setting aside the ex-parte decree. The case was allowed and affirmed in Civil Revision 184 of 2005 filed before District Judge and in Civil Revision 1608 of 2006 filed before this Court on 15-10-2008. Suit was restored and the date for peremptory hearing was fixed on 7-6-2009 when another son of Mominullah named ANMA Hye deposed as PW 1 and plaintiff's evidence was over on 30-3-2011 after PW 4 was examined. After closing of examining witnesses plaintiff amended plaint on 24-4-2011 claiming Salve) katha instead of 3(three) katha and the amendment was allowed on 9-2-2016. Meanwhile defendant 6 filed Title Suit 218 of 2010 on 8- 9-2010 for declaration of title and correction of record and recovery of possession in respect of schedule land. These two suits were ordered to be heard analogously on 30-10-2011 upon consent of both parties. 

 9. In Title Suit 218 of 2010 the case of defendant 6 is that admittedly Mahtab Uddin was owner in possession in D marked plot measuring 10(ten) katha. He sold 5(five) katha of D plot from the smith to defendant 6 and the rest 5(five) katha of north side was sold to plaintiff. Defendant 6 erected homestead. Five katha is equivalent to 0.0828 acres. But in the city survey khatian 456 only 0.0722 acres were recorded and the remaining 0.0103 acres were wrongly recorded in the name of the plaintiff in city survey khatians 3504 and 650. Defendant 6 left 285 sq. ft. from his northern portion amicably for convenience of movement on the understanding that plaintiff would not enter into such left out land at the time of construction. But on 28-8- 20.10 plaintiff amalgamated such left out land with his land. The city survey khatians 3504 and 650 were also wrongly prepared in the name of plaintiff by inserting that 285 sq. ft. equivalent to 0.0103 acres. Hence the suit was filed for recovering 0.0103 acres and correction of record. 

 10. In Title Suit 218 of 2010 the case of plaintiff is that admittedly plaintiff purchased 5(five) katha of D block from the north side and defendant 6 purchased 5(five) katha from south by consecutive documents on 11-11-1953. Plaintiff had been living by erecting tin made house till his dispossession in November, 1954 done by defendant 6 along with some other persons. Plaintiff filed Title Suit 127 of 1957 to recover his possession. Mir Mahbub is owner of the land adjacent to the north of plaintiff's land and Ruhunnessa wife of plaintiff is owner of 6½ katha of land adjacent east to the land of Mahbub. Ruhunnessa upon payment of all utility bills have been residing therein with her family and after her death her heirs have been in possession and they used a pathway by the north side of the land covered by kabala dated 11-11-1953. The pathway claimed by plaintiff is described before the verification (satyapath) made in the plaint in earlier suit. The suit is false and liable to be dismissed. 

 11. In Title Suit 218 of 2010, 3(three) PWs were examined and documents were marked as Exhibits 1-10. On the other hand in Title Suit 706 of 1985 (127 of 1957) 4(four) PW and 2(two) PWs were examined and both parties adduced documentary evidence. 

 12. In Title Suit 591 of 2015 (706 of 1985 or 127 of 1957) defendant 6 is the only contesting defendant. On the other hand defendant 6 filed Title Suit 218 of 2010 against plaintiff for the same subject matter. The matter in issue is co-related thus same in both the suits. Title Suit 591 of 2015 was filed in 1957 and during pendency of the suit Title Suit 218 of 2010 was filed by defendant 6 thus evidence of both suits is relevant for each one and can be used in both suits. 

 14. The Joint District Judge decreed Title Suit 591 of 2015 mainly on the finding that the pleader commissioner has identified the land wherefrom plaintiff was dispossessed and defendant 6 did not deny the statement made in the last lines of schedule to the plaint that plaintiff has been in possession in three feet road marked as Ga to Una for movement. In Title Suit 21.8 of 2010 Court found that since the commissioner's report is accepted in Title Suit 591 of 2015 defendant 6 has failed to prove title, interest and fact of dispossession and thus the suit was dismissed. 

 15. Against judgment and decree passed in Title Suit 591 of 2015 defendant 6 preferred Title Appeal 38 of 2018 and the appeal was dismissed by Additional District Judge, Court No. 2, Dhaka on the finding that possession followed by dispossession as claimed by plaintiff is proved by both oral and documentary evidence. 

 16. Defendant 6 then preferred the present revision before this Court. Defendant 6 also preferred First Appeal 195 of 2018 against judgment and decree passed in Title Suit 218 of 2010. 

 17. Mr Md Mozammel Hoque, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of defendant 6 in both revision and appeal takes us through the materials On record and submits that the Courts below committed error of law resulting in an error in such decree occasioning failure of justice in failing to consider the material evidence on record affecting the merit and touching the root of the case. The Court also erred in law in coming to its wrong conclusion without assigning proper reason. The Court failed to appreciate that plaintiff led contradictoty evidence and neither cause of action nor possession followed by dispossession is proved in evidence. He further submits that Court very enthusiastically granted declaration of title in favour of the plaintiff although such prayer was omitted by subsequent amendment, He also submits that the ex-parte decree passed upon evidence of PW 1. Mezbahul Adam was restored but the suit did not start from that stage as before and Abdul Hai deposed as PW. 1 although Mesbahul Alam was alive thus it violates the provision of Order IX, rule 15 of the Code of Civil Procedure. He candidly submits that since the decree passed in Title suit 591 of 2015 is not in conformity with the sketch map of the schedule to the plaint this suit cannot be decreed under section 51(a) read with Order V11, rule 3, Order XX, rule 6(1), Order XXI, rule 11(2)(j)(i) of the Code without a clear description of the property. He submits that the commissioner's report clearly contradicts the case of the plaintiff and reliance upon such wrong report is unwanted and the same causes failure of justice. He then submits that the inclusion of part of the land of defendant 6 in city survey khatians 3504 and 650 made in the name of plaintiff is apparently wrong and any right if granted by way of amicable arrangement is not legally binding upon the grantor. He finally submits that since plaintiff has evidently failed to prove his case in both revision and appeal the impugned judgments may be interfered with. 

 18. Mr A.J Mohammad Ali, learned Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of the plaintiff in both revision and appeal submits that the courts below upon proper appreciation of evidence has correctly passed the judgment and the same may not be subject to interference since there is no misreading and non-consideration of material evidence. Since dispossession done by defendant 6 is proved in Title Suit 591 of 2015 the claim of road by defendant 6 by subsequent Title Suit 218 of 2010 has no basis and such claim is false. He then refers to Order 248 dated 23-4-1969 and submits that despite objection the commissioner's report was accepted upon vivid discussion and no question can be raised against such report and dismissal of Title Suit 218 of 201.0 relying upon the commissioner's report is legal and proper. He submits that since defendant 6 failed to make out a positive and convincing case in both revision and appeal those are liable, to be discharged and dismissed respectively. At this stage he has preferred an application for inclusion of certain words "স্বত্ত্ব সাব্যস্তপূর্বক" in the prayer portion of the plaint and submits that this application is necessary for proper and effective adjudication of the suit. Ile conceded that although declaration of title was prayed in the original suit in 1957 but consequently due to mistaken advice or for reasons unknown the words declaration of title was omitted from the prayer portion although the caption of the plaint remains same as it was before and evidence was also taken in that manner. It appears that the amendment was done at the instance of the plaintiff and now the plaintiff has come before this Court disowning his earlier amendment claiming that by such amendment the nature and character of the suit has been changed. However in order to avoid the new born technicality this prayer is allowed especially because the title of the plaintiff by kabala dated 11-11-1953 (Exhibit 3) is admitted. 

 27. DW 1 Arifa supported the case of defendant 6 and stated that her brother as PW 1 deposed in Title Suit 432 of 2015 wherein documents were exhibited. She deposed as PW 2 in Title Suit 432 of 2015. 

 28. DW 2 Kashein has deposed as PW 3 in Title Suit 432 of 2015. 

 29. P1 1 Rafiqul (in Title Suit 432 of 2015) stated in examination-in-chief 

 32. On 16-1-2014 PW 1 Hye again was recalled and he tendered a kabala 6500 dated 28-10-1952 said to be the document of his mother and the same was marked as Exhibit 5. It appears that this document was introduced in order to make camouflage to validate the alleged road as well as the bigger quantum of land wrongly recorded in their names and the same can be understood from reading of paragraphs 18 (Ma) to (Eno) of the written statement filed in Title Suit 218 of 2010. 

 34. It is admitted case of both parties that they purchased 5(five) katha each from the D block of CS plot 290 by two kabalas dated 11-11-1953 from the common vendor Mir Mahtab Uddin. D block contains 10(ten) katha land. Plaintiff's kabala is Exhibit 3. Exhibit 1 is the kabala of defendant 6. The boundary as mentioned in the 'Kha' schedule to the plaint of Title Suit 591 of 2015 wherein plaintiff wants recovery of possession is that at the north: B marked plot, south: the half portion southern land sold today to Abdul Aziz Khan, east: 20 feet ejmali road, west: the land of Noresh Chandra Sen Master. The boundary of Exhibit 3 is also the same. The boundary of Exhibit 1 is that at the north: the land sold today to Mominullah Saheb, east: 20 feet ejmali road, west: the land of Gonesh Chandra Sen, south: F marked plot. Abdul Aziz Khan (defendant 6) is at the south of Exhibit 3 and simultaneously Mominullah (plaintiff) is at the north of Exhibit I and there is no road intervening such border. Therefore it is clear that plaintiff has got no road at his south according to the boundary of Exhibit 3 and even if there is any road as claimed by plaintiff that must fall within the 5(five) katha boundary of Exhibit 1. Plaintiff also did not make out any case of ouster. Had this most important material evidence on boundaries of both kabolas along with the schedule-Kha with sketch map to the plaint of former suit been considered the result of the case would have been otherwise. 

 35. When Title Suit 591 of 2015 was first filed in 1957 it was stated in paragraph 10 of the plaint that the quantum of disputed land is approximately 3(three) katha but subsequently plaint was amended on 9-2-2016 claiming the disputed land is 5(five) katha and the amendment was done after closing of plaintiff's evidence. There is nothing in the amendment to show how and when and by what manner plaintiff was dispossessed from the rest 2(two) katha land. It has been stated in paragraph 7 of the plaint that defendants 1-5 have dispossessed plaintiff from the place marked as Ka, Kha, Ga, Gha in the sketch map but such marking does not make a rectangle figure or shape. The two sentences before the verification made in the plaint indicating path way through Gha to Uma is also not a rectangle. Therefore the claim of the plaintiff is vague and indefinite. 

 36. Title of each of the parties by Exhibits 1 and 3 is admitted in this case. Exhibits 1 and 3 contains 5 (five) katha each which is equivalent to 825 ajutangsho, Trial Court found that since defendant 6 admitted that because of earlier understanding between the predecessors of both parties the land measuring 285 sq. ft. was left out by Aziz Khan which is now claimed by defendant 6 after long lapse of time. This finding is wrong. Possession on the basis of mutual understanding does not constitute the same adverse against the real owner. Plaintiff also did not make out any case of ouster, SA and RS records were correctly prepared in the name of defendant 6. But in the city survey khatian 456 only 722 ajutangsho of land instead of 825 ajutangsho which is equivalent to Wive) katha was recorded in the name of defendant 6 and the remaining left out 103 ajutangsho equivalent to 285 sq. ft. was wrongly inserted in city survey khatians 3504 and 650 in the name the plaintiff. Therefore we are of the view that defendant 6 is entitled to have corrected the khatian in his name by inserting 103 ajutangsho land which has been wrongly entered in the khatians belonging to plaintiff. 

 37. In the instant case the lower court without assigning any proper reason abruptly relied upon the commissioner's report and accordingly decreed Title Suit 591 of 2015 and dismissed Title Suit 432 of 2015 but failed to appreciate that decision on material issue cannot be left to the report of the commissioner when there is satisfactory evidence already on record. 

 38. From the above made discussion we therefore hold that plaintiff has failed to prove his case. In Title Suit 591 of 2015 and in Title Appeal 38 of 2018 the courts below committed error of law occasioning failure of justice in decreeing the suit upon misreading and non consideration of material evidence affecting the merit of the case. The trial Court also erred in law in dismissing Title Suit 432 of 2015 upon fanciful consideration. The title of defendant 6 is hereby declared in respect of 5(Five) katha land equivalent to 825 ajutangsho and the city survey khan= 456 is hereby corrected by inserting 103 ajutangsho in the name of defendant 6. Plaintiff shall deliver khas possession of 103 ajutangsho of land to defendant 6 as described in the 'Kha' schedule to the plaint within 60(sixty) days otherwise defendant 6 shall recover such possession through Court.

parties:
Mostafa Shahriar -------- Appellant. (in both the appeals)
-Vs.
Mostafa Ahmed and others -------- Respondents. In C.A. No. 284/2010)
Mostafa Ahmed and another ------ Respondents. (In C.A. No. 285/201)
full_judgment:
Krishna Debnath J. That these two civil appeals arise out of leave granted by this court in two civil petitions for Leave to Appeal Nos. 717 and 718 of 2009 are directed against the judgment and order dated the 13th day of January, 2009 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.71 of 2002 with Civil Revision No.87 of 2002 discharging both the Rules thereby affirming those dated 21.10.2001 passed by the Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Sylhet in Title Appeal No.36 of 1999 heard analogously with Title Appeal No.35 of 1999 allowing both the appeals decreeing Title Suit No 67 of 1995 setting aside those dated 30.11.1998 passed by the Assistant Judge, Beani Bazar, Sylhet decreeing Title Suit No.67 of 1995 and dismissing Title Suit No.64 of 1995. 

 2. The facts involved in the case no 67 of 1995, in short are that the suit land originally belonged to Gajendra Kumar Chattarjee; that Gajendra Kumar while in possession intended to sell the same and entered into an agreement with the present proforma respondent no 2, Liakot Ali and Panaullah on 13.09.1963 at an consideration money of Tk.1000.00; that Gajendra received tk.800 from the purchasers and inducted them into possession; that on 09.03.1965 after getting the balance amount of tk. 200 the aforesaid Gajendra executed the sale deed in favour of Panaullah and Liakot Ali ; that therefore a dispute arose between the Panaullah and Liakot regarding the purchased land and Panaullah instituted Title suit no 312 of 1967 against the said Liakot and ultimately the suit was decreed on 23.01.1968 on the basis of a solenama, the present pro-forma respondent no 2 Liakot got the 2nd scheduled land in his share and had been owning and possessing the same; that original owner Gajendra filed Title suit No 386 of 1967 for permanent injunction against Panaullah and Liakot which was ultimately withdrawn by the plaintiff, Gajendra and in that suit Gajendra admitted his earlier sale in favour of Panaullah and Liakot; that the proforma respondent No 2 Liakot had been possessing the 2nd scheduled land of the plaint by constructing house at S.A. Plot No 171 and cultivating paddy on S.A. plot no 125 and had been paying rent regularly and also mutated his name in the record of right in Mutation Case No. 43 of 1968-69; that thereafter the aforesaid Liakot went to Dinajpur for some purposes and had been possessing the suit land through his maternal uncle one Nasiruddin, a retired police officer; that thereafter, Liakot became a member of the local Union Parishad at Dinajpur and had been living there permanently; that at the instance of certain local interested persons the local Vested Property Authority claiming the suit land and some other lands as Vested and Non-resident Property started VP Case no 22 of 1978-79 and served notice upon Liakot and present respondent no 1 Mostafa Ahmed directing them to hand over possession of the same; that on behalf of Liakot, his uncle Nasiruddin filed written objection and Mostafa Ahmed also filed a separate written objection and after hearing VP Case No 22 of 1978-79 was dropped; that in that case Mostafa Ahmed the respondent No 1 filed papers before the Court with Firisti along with aforesaid Nasiruddin the representative of Liakot Ali; that the present proforma respondent no 2 Liakot Ali sold the 2nd scheduled land of the plaint to proforma respondent Nos. 3-7 and one lqbal Hussain and others who purchased 1.33 acres of land out of 1.41 acres through different registered sale deeds dated 12.06.1989 and 18.06.1989 respectively at Tk 4,40,000.00.Thereafter defendant Nos. 2-6 along with lqbal Hussain and others constructed dwelling house and by digging pond and filling earth possessed the same. Thereafter, the said lqbal Hussain and others transferred their shares to Mostafa Shahriar through different sale deeds dated 05.10.1989 and 08.11.1989 respectively and delivered possession to him and since then the petitioner and others have been possessing the 2nd scheduled land. In the month of June, 1989 one Nizamuddin, a relative of Liakot Ali came to know that the respondent no 1, Mostafa Ahmed mutated 2nd scheduled land in his name and accordingly, on enquiry, he further came to know that he has created a forged deed dated 20.04.1983 by way of false personation. On 17.06.1989 the said Nizamuddin filed a complaint before the District Anti-Corruption Department, Sylhet against Mostafa Ahmed. Thereafter, on 08.08.1989 after obtaining the certified copy of the deed dated 20.04.1983 Liakot Ali came to know about the existence of that bainapatra dated 18.10.1973 which was also forged deed and never been executed by Liakot Ali and as such, the plain-tiff filed the suit for declaration that the bainapatra dated 18.10.1973 and the deed of sale dated 20.04.1983 are forged and collusive papers, hence the plaintiffs instituted the suit. 

 3. The defendant No. 1 contested the case by filing written statement contending, inter-alia, that the suit land originally belonged to Gajendra Kumar who executed a bainapatra on 13.09.1963 in favour of one Liakot Ali, son of Rafique Uddin of Khidirpur and Panaullah and he received tk. 800 out of total consideration of tk. 1000 and inducted them into possession; that thereafter, getting the remaining amount of tk. 200 the aforesaid Gajendra executed a sale deed on 09.03.1965 in favour of both Liakot and Panaullah: that Panaullah filed Title suit No. 312 of 1967 for partition in the Court of subordinate judge, 2nd Court, Sylhet and on the basis of solenama the suit was decreed; that as per terms of solenama Panaullah got 42 decimals towards the western side of plot no 171 and 54 decimals towards the southernside of plot no 125 that thereafter, Panaullah and Liakot mutated their names in the record of right vide Mutation Case No. 42 of 1968-69; that Panaullah transferred his share in favour of one Rabeya Khatun, wife of Shoikot Ali by registered deed dated 13.04.1968; that Rabeya Khatun by two registered deed dated 05.12.1972 and 15.12.1972 respectively transferred the same in favour of present defendant no 1 Mostafa Ahmed and inducted him into possession; that after the purchase from Rabeya the owner of other portion namely Liakot Ali intended to transfer his land and the defendant No.1 in order to purchase the same entered into an agreement for sale with Liakot Ali on 18.10.1973 and consideration money was fixed at Tk. 12000.00 and tk. 6000 was paid on that date and defendant no. 1 was inducted into possession of the land; that in spite of repeated requests Liakot Ali delayed the execution of the kabala on different pleas and ultimately on 20.04.1983 after getting the remaining tk. 6000 executed and registered the sale deed in favour of the defendant No. 1 and he has been possessing the suit land as before; that the defendant No. 1 on 31.08.1971 received a notice from the vested property authority directing him to hand over the possession of the land in favour of the government claiming the same as vested and non-resident property; that the defendant No. 1 instituted title suit no 226 of 1982 in the court of subordinate judge 2nd court. Sylhet for a declaration that the land is not a vested and nonresident property and also for a declaration that the plaintiff is the owner in possession of the same on the basis of purchase; that he also filed title suit no 202 of 1984 in the same court for permanent injunction restraining the government from interfering with the plaintiffs' possession and the same was decreed on 25.02.1985; that the government did not prefer any appeal against that decree; that title suit no 226 of 1982 was also decreed on 28.11.1987 declaring the plaintiffs' title and possession over the land mentioned in the plaint; that from the date of bainapatra dated 18.10 1973 the defendant no.1 has been possessing the suit land by constructing house and paying rent regularly; that the defendant no 1 mortgaged entire land of plot no 171 with the local Sonali Bank in the year 1986 and transferred entire land of plot no.125 to Musammat Kamrunnessa Khatun, Badrun Lashker, Luthfur Rahman Chowdhury, Abdus Samad and Abdus Sajjad who mutated their names in the record of right and have been possessing their and by constructing building thereon; that Liakot Ali after his sale left the locality and at present, there is no Liakot Ali at the locality which is evident from the local voter list: that the plaintiffs in order to grab the suit land created some forged deeds presenting a false person as Liakot Ali before the Sub-Registrar: that the plaintiffs have no title and possession over the suit land and the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 4. That in title suit no 64 of 1995 the present respondent no 1 Mostafa Ahmed as the plaintiff stated everything in support of his claim which he stated by filing written statement in Title suit no 67 of 1995. He also stated that the present appellant Mostafa Shahriar in collusion with his alleged nephew defendant No. 1 Shahed Ahmed Chowdhury created a forged deed dated 10.11.1991 alleged to have been executed and registered by plaintiff Mostafa Ahmed in favour of defendant No. 1 Shahed Ahmed and his son has been shown as an attesting witness though he never executed and registered any deed in favour of Shahed Ahmed Chowdhury that he and his son were not present at Sylhet on that date; that the defendant in order to grab the land of the plaintiff created the aforesaid false deed; that on 10.07.1994 when the plaintiff Mostafa Ahmed was in Dhaka, the defendants Shahriar and Shahed with the help of their party men forcibly entered into the house of the plaintiff Mostafa Ahmed and dispossessed him from the house and also from the land; that on return to Sylhet when he asked the defendants about the reason they disclosed that on the basis of purchase they took possession of the same: that after enquiry on 08.08.1994 and after obtaining the certified copy he came to know that defendant No. 1 in collusion with defendant No. 2 created a forged deed dated 10.11.1991 in respect of 60 decimals of land of plot no 171; that on the basis of so-called deed dated 10.11.1991 the defendants have not acquired any title or possession and for declaration of the aforesaid deed as forged and recovery of khas possession after evicting defendant Nos. 1 and 2 from the suit land of the suit he instituted T.S. No 64 of 1995. 

 5. That the present appellant Mostafa Shahriar as defendant No. 2 contested the suit by filing written statement and stated everything which he stated in his plaint of T.S. No. 67 of 1995. He also stated that since their purchase from the Liakot Ali in the year 1989 he and his other sharers have been possessing the land by con-structing house, they also dug a pond and connected their land with electric and gas line, that the so called dispossession of the plaintiff on 10.07.1994 from the suit land is absolutely a false story; that the plaintiff of T.S. No. 64 of 1995 had no title or possession over the suit land: that defendant No 2 is not his nephew and he has no connection with him and he had no knowledge about the so called deed dated 10.11.1991 and as such T.S. No. 64 of 1995 against him is liable to be dismissed with cost. 

 6. The trial court after analogous trial decreed the Title Suit No. 67 of 1995 and dismissed the Title Suit No. 64 of 1995 on 30.11.1998. 

 7. That being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and decree respondent No. 1 filed title appeal Nos. 35 of 1999 and 36 of 1999 and the court of appeal below allowed the appeals by his judgment and decree dated 21.10.2001. 

 10. Mr. Fida M. Kamal learned Senior Advocate with Mr. Zuhurul Islam Mukul, learned Advocate appearing for the appellants in both the appeals submit that Liakot Ali himself as plaintiff No. 1 and along with purchasers from him having instituted the suit and deposed twice as P.W-2 to prove in support of his case and his identity having not being challenged and defendants in his suit having not been able to prove that he is not the real Liakot. Mr. Kamal further submits that in support of his claim Mostafa Ahmed (respondent) having stated that his vendor Liakot Ali left for Chittagong Hill Tracts and he is already dead and Liakot Ali present in Court is not the real person and the trial court having disbelieved his claim and having held that he has not been able to prove the said facts. Lastly, he submits that the Vested Property Authority issued a notice on 31.08.1978 in VP Case No. 22 of 1978-79 claiming the entire land as vested property (possessed by Liakot and Panaullah) and after their representation and production of the necessary papers on 27,09.1987 the said notice having been withdrawn. the Title Suit No. 226 of 1982 filed on 12.07.1982 by respondent Mostafa Ahmed challenging the notice dated 31.08.1978 without impleading Liakot Ali as a party is malafide to show himself as the sole owner of the entire property and the court of appeal below committed an error in not considering the aforesaid facts, in decreeing the instant suit and the High Court Division also committed error in affirming the same. 

 11. On the other hand Mr. A. J. Mohammad Ali, learned Senior Advocate with Mr. M. Khaled Ahmed, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondents of both the appeals submit that the appellant Mostafa Shahriar in no way acquire his title through the disputed deeds upon 1.33 acres of land from Liakot Ali, the identity of the produced Liakot Ali is being disputed. Mr. Ali submits on the contrary Panaullah, one of the admitted owners of the suit land has been examined in the Court and proved the transfer in favour of respondent No. 1 Mostafa Ahmed. Lastly, he supports the judgment and order of the High Court Division as well as the judgment and order of the Court of Appeal and prays for dismissal of the appeals. 

 13. Firstly, it appears that Liakot Ali as plaintiff No. 1 along with purchasers instituted the suit and deposed twice as P.W-2 to prove his case. His identity was not challenged by the defendants at that time. Secondly, Respondent Mostafa as defendant stated that, his vendor Liakot Ali left for Chittagong Hill Tracts and he has already died and Liakot Ali present in the Court is not the real person, trial court dis-believed his claim with cogent reasons. but, the Court of Appeal below without reversing the said findings with its own finding referring the materials on record mechanically and whimsically allowed the appeal and thereby committed serious error as revisional Court in allowing the appeals and the High Court Division com-mitted an error in failing to thresh out the said mistake of affirming the judgment of the Court of appeal below. Thirdly, it appears that the Vested Property Authority issued notice on 31.08.1978 in VP Case No. 22 of 1978-79 claiming the entire land as vested property, but, after production of the necessary papers by the appellants that notice withdrawn. However, the Court of Appeal did not consider these aspects of the case rather, the High Court Division also committed error in failing to find out the said error of the Court of appeal below and thereby committed error in affirming the decision of the Court of appeals Lastly, it appears that the plaintiff appellant filed his suit for declaration of title and for recovery of khas possession, but the Court of appeal below decreed the suit in favour of respondent without arriving at any finding regarding his possession followed by dispossession of the suit land and the High Court Division erred in affirming such an erroneous judgment and decree.

parties:
Ahsanullah (Md) alias Ahlullah being dead his legal heirs:- 1(a) Afia Begum and others ----- Appellants
VS
Mohammad Ali alias Kuti Miah alias Mukund Ali being dead his legal heirs:- 1(a) Musammat Rong Baher Begum and others -------- Respondents
full_judgment:
Md Nuruzzaman, J: This Civil Appeal, by leave, has arisen out of the judgment and order dated 26-11-2006 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.2360 of 1997 making the Rule absolute thereby setting aside the judgment and decree dated 27-4-1997 passed by the Additional District Judge, First Court, Sylhet in Title Appeal No.251 of 1985 and reversing the judgment and decree dated 27-6-1984 decreeing the suit in part passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 1st Additional Court, Sylhet in Title Suit No.33 of 1979. 

 2. Facts leading, to filing of this civil appeal, in short, are that one Md Ahalullah, the predecessor of the petitioners as the plaintiff filed Title Suit No.152 of 1975 before the learned Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), 2nd Court, Sylhet which was transferred to the Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), 1st Additional Court, Sylhet and renumbered as Title Suit No.33 of 1979 for specific performance of contract against the present respondent Nos.4-5 including their mother Renu Bala Das impleading them as defendant Nos.1-3 and including present respondent No.6 as proforma defendant No.4 stating, inter alia, that Kailash Chandra Das, predecessor of the present-respondent Nos.4-5 being the owners and possessors of the suit land, proposed to sell the suit land to the plaintiff for Taka 25,000 and the plaintiff agreed to purchase the same. Thereafter, the aforesaid Kailash Chandra Das executed and registered a Bainapatra dated 27 Sraban, 1379 BS corresponding to .12-8-1972 in favour of the plaintiff on receipt of Taka 2,000 from the plaintiff. Said Kailash Chandra Das executed and registered another Bainapatra on 7-41973 corresponding to 24 Chaitra 1379 in favour of the plaintiff on receiving of Taka 1,000. Thereafter, on the several occasions by installment said Kailash Chandra Das and his son defendant No.2 in total received Taka 10,380 from the plaintiff and his son. Thereafter, the plaintiff came to know that the defendants are trying to sell the suit land to others. The plaintiff asked the defendant Nos.1-3 to execute and register the conveyance in favour of him on acceptance of balance amount from the plaintiff but the defendants refused to do so. Hence, the plaintiff was compelled to institute the suit to get a conveyance executed and registered by the defendant Nos.1-3 in respect of the suit land. During pendency of the suit the plaintiff by way of amendment of the plaint alternative relief was sought that if, the plaintiff could not prove any claim of the suit plots for specific performance of contract, in that case, he will be entitled to get back principal amount with compensation for the amount, he has already paid for the said plot. Thereafter, the plaintiff by filing an application sought to omit the above alternative relief which was allowed by the trial Court but the said order of omitting the alternative prayer was not challenged by the contesting defendants. 

 3. The defendant Nos.1-2 contested the suit by filing written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint contending, inter-alia, that the suit land was originally belonged to Kailash Chandra Das and after the death of the aforesaid Kailash Chandra Das his interest in respect of the suit land developed upon the defendant Nos.l-3 as his legal heirs. The defendant Nos.1-3 sold the Suit Plot Nos.1, 2 and 3 of the plaint schedule to Assoddar Ali by a registered sale deed dated 20-10-1974 for maintenance, educational expenses of the defendant Nos.2 and 3 and for meeting up the expenses of Sraddah of Kailash Chandra Das. The defendant Nos.1-3 sold the land of Plot No.6 of the plaint schedule to Ahmed Ali and Abdul Ali at a consideration of Taka 8,000 by a sale deed dated 15-1-1975 and gave possession of the same in their favour. The defendant Nos.1-3 kept the land of Plot Nos.4 and 5 of the plaint schedule under the care of Ahmed Ali and Abdul Ali. The predecessor of the defendants Kailash Chandra Das did not execute any bainapatra in favour of the plaintiff. The alleged bainapatra are forged, collusive, paper transaction without any consideration and that the defendants never received any amount of money from the plaintiff and, as such, the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 5. Feeling aggrieved, by the judgment and decree of the trial Court, the plaintiff as appellant preferred Title Appeal No.251 of 1985 before the learned District Judge, Sylhet. Eventually, on transfer, the said appeal was heard by the learned Additional District Judge, First Court, Sylhet who by his judgment and decree dated 27-4-1997 allowed the appeal and thereby set-aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court and decreed the suit. 

 7. In due course, a Single Bench of the High court Division upon hearing the parties made the Rule absolute by the impugned judgment and order dated 26-11-2006 and thereby set-aside the judgment and decree dated 27-4-199; passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Sylhet in Title Appeal No.251 of 1985 and thereby affirmed the judgment and decree dated 27-6-1984 passed by the learned Sub-Ordinate Judge, 1st Additional Court, Sylhet in Title Suit No.33 of 1979. 

 9. Mr Khair Ezaz Maswood, the learned Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of the appellants has submitted that the suit schedules contain several plots and khatians and the plaintiff amended the plaint to the effect that the refund of baina money may be allowed if the claim of any of the plot is not proved, but in this case, the plaintiff successfully proved the claim in each and every plot of the suit schedule of the bainapatra by examining the oral and documentary evidences and that the PWs' corroborated each other and that the defendants' side could not extract any contradiction upon cross-examination of the PW's. The DW's as well could not prove the defence case. Moreover, the plaintiff amended the plaint deleting the alternative prayer which was allowed vide order No.91 dated 19-6-1984 but the High Court Division without appreciating the consequence of the withdrawal of the alternative prayer vide order No.91 dated 19-6-1984 passed the impugned judgment and order on the erroneous findings that the plaintiff amended the plaint claiming alternative relief for which he is not entitled to decree of specific performance of contract which is nothing, rather, emerged on the basis of misconceived appreciation about law and facts and, as such, the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division cannot be sustained in law. He has further submitted that as per settled principle of law when the plaintiff's first prayer is for a decree for specific performance of contract and alternatively he prays for refund of the earnest money in the event of refusal of specific performance of contract it cannot be argued that in the facts of an alternative prayer for the refund of the earnest money the plaintiff is not entitled to a decree for specific performance of contract. The High Court Division erred in law and passed the impugned judgment and order against the settled principle of law only considering the alternative prayer of the plaintiff. Moreover, said alternative prayer was amended and thrown-up by the plaintiff on 19-6-1984 vide, order No.91 which was unchallenged, as not challenged by the defendants in the higher Court, thus, such give-up it is meaning that they have conceded order of withdrawal of the alternative prayer and, as such, the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division is liable to be interfered with by this Division. He has finally submitted that the specific case of the defendant Nos.1-3 that the bainapatra was collusive, fraudulent and forged and that there was no case of the defendants that the plaintiff had alternative prayer for refund of bainapatra money with compensation but the High Court Division made the Rule absolute considering the alternative prayer of the plaintiff without rebutting the findings of facts as discussed and found correct by the last Court of facts as Appellate Court and decreed the suit allowing the appeal instead of decree in part passed by the trial Court and, as such, the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division is liable to be set-aside. Hence, the instant appeal may kindly be allowed. 

 10. Per contra, Mr AM Amin Uddin, the learned Senior Counsel appearing on behalf of the respondents has submitted in supports of the impugned judgment of the High Court Division. He has further submitted that the plaintiff filed an application with alternative prayer dated 20-12-1977 for amendment of the plaint for an alternative relief for return of the consideration amount together compensation at the rate of Taka 25% in the event of his failure to get a decree for specific performance of contract, the trial Court decreed the suit on solatium under section 22 of the Specific Relief Act. No error of law or facts has been occurred in granting such decree. He has further submitted that the lower appellate Court wrongly and illegally decreed the suit for execution of sale deed by the defendant Nos.1- 3, the heirs of the original owner of Kailash Chandra Das. The sale deed executed by the defendant Nos.1-3 in favour of defendant Nos.5-7 remains untouched, unaffected. He has also submitted that the defendant Nos.5-7 are transferee for value against consideration in good faith without notice of earlier agreement for sale by Kailash Chandra Das predecessor in interest of the vendor. They are in possession of the suit properties by dint of valid registered documents. The learned Senior counsel finally referring section 27(b) of the Specific Relief Act, 1877 has argued that the suit against the added defendant Nos.5-7 herein respondent Nos.1(a) to 1(i), 2 and 3 is hits by the provisions of that section. Therefore, the petitioners cannot get any relief against them. Hence, the High Court Division rightly made the Rule absolute. Therefore, he prays for dismissal of the appeal. 

 "From the prayer in the plaint it appears that the plaintiff at prayer "Ka" prayed for specific p"rformance of contract in respect of the suit house of the defendant in pursuance of the agreement for sale dated 24-3-73. At prayer "Ga" the plaintiff prayed for refund of earnest money if the decree of specific performance of contract is refused by the Court. So, essentially the first prayer is for specific performance of contract and the prayer at "Ga" as mentioned above is an alternative prayer. Such prayer is ordinarily made, as in the event of refusal of specific performance of contract the plaintiff can get refund of the earnest money. Even without this prayer if a suit for specific performance of contract is dismissed, then the plaintiff is entitled to refund of the earnest money. So from this alternative prayer it cannot be argued that there being an alternative prayer for refund of the earnest money the plaintiff is not entitled to a decree for specific performance of contract." 

 19. On perusal of the judgment of the trial Court it appears that the trial Court opined that "according to law bainapatra exhibits 3 and 3(a) did not create any title of the plaintiff in respect of the suit land. In view of the above discussion and on consideration of oral and documentary evidence on record the Court finds that the defendant Nos.5-7 purchased the lands out of the suit land from the defendant Nos.1-3 by the registered sale deed Exhibit A, A(1) and A(3). Those are for valuable consideration in good faith and without notice of the original contract held in between the plaintiff and Kailash Chandra Das and, as such, specific perfor-mance of contract held in between the plaintiff and Kailash Chandra Das cannot be enforced against the transferees defendant Nos.5-7". 

 b) any other person claiming under him by a title arising subsequently to the contract, except a transferee for value who has paid his money in good faith and without notice of the original' contract; 

 c) any person claiming under a title which, though prior to the contract and known to the plaintiff, might have been displaced by the defendant; 

 28. Gorangha Chandra Das, DW No.1 is a son of Kailash Chandra Das who in his testimonies stated nothing regarding the case of added defendant Nos. 5-7, nor stated that the added defendants purchased the land without the knowledge of the original Bainapatra. This witness straight way denied the Bainanama of his father Kailas Chandra Das although it was not proved concurrently before both the Court below. The High Court Division never tried to discuss the matter in the impugned judgment. 

 31. From those testimonies and discussions, there is no such assertion that they were purchasers of the said property paying the money in good faith and without notice of the original contract. 

 32. Mere denying the facts of original Bainanama in the written statement will not ipso facto acted upon, such, facts must be proved through oral and documentary evidence. Furthermore, to make applicable the provisions of section 27(b) of the Specific Relief Act i.e. bonafide transfer for value without notice, such plea of the subsequent transferee onus lies on him to prove absence of such notice. 

 39. In cross the added defendants did not deny those testimonies of the PW 3-Soleman Hossain. Therefore, the testimony of PW 3 deem to have been admitted by the added defendants from which it is abundantly clear that the added defendants were aware about the original Bainanama of the plaintiffs. Thus, the submissions advanced on behalf of the added defendants by the learned Counsel devoid of merit. 

 40. It is divulged that the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division opined in the impugned judgment to the effect that " The Lower Appellate Court wrongly and illegally decreed the suit for execution of sale deed by the defendants No.1-3 the heirs of the original owner Koilash Chandra Das. The sale deed executed by the defendant Nos.1-3 in favour of the defendants No.5-7 remains untouched, unaffected because no cancellation was sought for in the prayer of the plaint. The contract for sale of immovable property under section 54 of the Transfer of Property Act does not create any right/interest in the property. It is a document merely creating a right to obtain another document. The plaintiff asked for relief in the alternative on a part with each other and after grant of one of such alternative relief he is not an aggrieved person who could carry the matter to this Court, specific performance be a equitable relief which have been refused in due exercise of desecration by the trial Court which is not liable to be interfered by the lower Appellate Court in view of conspicuous absence of any finding that the learned Trial Court excersied its discretion arbitrarily........ " 

 41. The above findings and opinion in the impugned judgment is not only misconceived, rather, the fundamental and inherent error because if the added defendants could not proved that they had bonafide purchasers for value who has paid his money in good faith and without notice of the original contract in that case, there is no necessity to sought any relief against the added defendants and their alleged deeds in question. 

 42. Since, the suit was for specific perfor-mance of contract by dint of registered Bainanama, such registration itself deem to be not only created a right for registration of sale deed, rather, seems to be a notice for purchasing the same property, in such suit, there is no scope to convert the same as a suit for declaration and cancellation against the added defendants. Moreover, the principal defendants got the suit properties by inheritance from their predecessors deceased Kailash Chandra Das who made registered agreement of bainapatra with predecessors of the plaintiff in the 1379 BS and on 1379 BS Corresponding to 1973 AD and received the part payment of the consideration in his life time, before registration of the deeds in question of added defendants. However, added defendants purchased the suit properties after death of the Kailash Chandra Das from his heirs. Therefore, it is the settled maxim of the law that the added defendants ought to prove that they purchased the property without notice to original bainanama. From our discussions as above, we have already found that the added defendants have failed to prove their part. Therefore, the opinion and discussions of the trial Court and the High Court Division are erroneous and without any merit. 

 43. Moreso, the added defendants steps into the shoes of the principal defendants, in such case, the maxim of law has settled many more years ago holding that specific performance of the contract can be enforced against either party or against any other party who claims title under the original party. In the case of Eazher Meah and others vs Shaher Banu and others reported in 49 DLR (AD) 85 wherein this Division held that— 

 "The proper form of decree is to direct specific performance of the contract between the vendor and the plaintiff and direct subsequent transferee to join in the conveyance so as to pass on the title which resides in him to the plaintiff in order to avoid all controversies." 

 "In a suit for specific performance of contract for sale of immovable property plaintiff is entitled to delivery of possession. A trespasser in the suit property is liable to be impleaded in the suit and evicted from the suit property to give effective relief to the plaintiff." 

 "The expression "under him" is referable to clause (a) of section 27 i.e. either party to the contract. As the defendant No.2 had acquired title to the property as regard which defendant No.1 earlier entered into an agreement for sale with the plaintiffs and as defendant No.2 failed to establish that he purchased the property in good faith without notice of the original contract, the Court was correct in decreeing the suit against the defendants and in directing defendant No.2 to execute and register kabala in favour of the plaintiffs." 

 The principal defendants and added defendants are directed to join in the conveyance and register the same in the name of the plaintiffs. If, they failed to do so, within 90 days from the received of the direction of the trial Court, the plaintiffs would be entitled to have the conveyance paying rest of the consideration money through Court in accordance with law.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.541 of 2018
parties:
Md. Atiar Rahman and another ------- Petitioners
-Vs-
Most. Rabeya Khatun and others ------- Respondents
full_judgment:
2. The facts, relevant for disposal of this petition, are that the respondents herein as plaintiffs instituted Other Class Suit No.131 of 2001 in the Additional Court of Assistant Judge, Kushtia for declaration of title in the disputed property stating, inter alia, that the suit land appertaining to Mouza-Mozompur under S.A. Khatian No.259 corresponding to Plot No.369 comprising an area of .37 acre land originally belonged to defendant No.2, Amejan Nessa, in two annas share and defendant No.1, Atiar Rahman in 14 annas share. Defendant No.1 was the minor son of defendant No.2 and for his welfare, for want of money defendant No.2, Amejan Nessa, herself and as natural guardian, mother of the minor son, defendant No.1 on 30.06.1969 A.D. transferred .0825 acre land in favour of the plaintiffs predecessor by a sub-kabala deed dated 30.06.1969 being No.8077. The possession of the transferred land was handed over by the vendor in favour of the purchaser and after purchase, the predecessor of the plaintiffs possessed that land and paid rent after mutation for more than 12 (twelve) years. The predecessor of the plaintiff, Sarwar Hossain's name has been correctly recorded against the suit land in the present RS record. In RS Plot No.4132, the suit land measuring .0831 acre was recorded primarily in the name of Sarwar Hossain, but subsequently defendant No.1 filed Other Class Suit No.69 of 1987 against Sarwar Hossain and others in respect of the entire land of suit of S.A. Khatian challenging the transfer deed in favour of the plaintiffs predecessor, Sarwar Hossain, in the Court of Assistant Judge, Kushtia. The suit was dismissed on contest and against that dis-missal decree, defendant No.1 filed an Other Appeal No.219 of 1987 in the Court of District Judge, Kushtia. After hearing, the appeal was dismissed affirming the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court and in this manner, the right, title, interest and possession of the plaintiffs to the suit land remained intact. The further case of the plaintiffs is that defendant Nos.1 and 2 in collusion with the settlement officials including the suit land measuring .0825 acre along with .37 acre in SA Plot No.369 with other lands pre-pared a collusive RS Khatian in the name of defendant No. 1. On the basis of that wrong collusive RS record, the defendants on 26.01.2001 denied the title of the plain-tiffs' which constrained the plaintiffs to institute the original suit for declaration of their title. 

 3. The contrary case of the contesting defendant No.1 is that defendant No.2, Amejan Nessa, for the welfare of her minor son, defendant No.1, did not execute and register any transfer deed in favour of the predecessor of the plaintiffs on 30.06.1969 in respect of the suit land measuring .0825 acre. The further case of the defendants is that the deed in favour of the plaintiffs' predecessor in respect of the suit land is without consideration, collusive, forged and not acted upon. On the basis of that sub-kabala deed, neither the predecessor of the plaintiffs nor the plain-tiffs acquired any right, title, interest and possession in the suit land. The plaintiffs' suit is barred by limitation and on the basis of false allegations, they have filed the instant suit. 

 5. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree of the trial Court, the plaintiffs filed Title Appeal No.52 of 2013 in the Court of District Judge, Kushtia which was transmitted to the 1st Court of Additional District Judge, Kushtia who after hearing the appeal by the judgment and decree dated 18.01.2015 allowed the same. 

 8. Mr. Md. Nurul Amin, learned Counsel, appearing on behalf of the petitioners, submits that the plaintiffs claimed that defendant No.1 was the minor and during his minority, his land was sold by his mother, defendant No.2. He adds that mother is a de facto guardian, so the transfer made by de facto guardian is void. He further submits that defendant Nos.1 and 2 have been in possession over the suit land and the SA record was correctly prepared in their names on the basis of the possession, so the instant suit for mere declaration of title cannot be maintainable with-out seeking for recovery of possession. But the appellate Court as well as the High Court Division without discussing this vital issue decreed the suit and thereby committed error of law. He further submits that the plaintiff claimed 0.0831 acre land out of 0.037 acre which is unspecified and indefinite. In a suit for declaration of title without specifying the suit land is not maintainable and as such, the appellate Court as well as the High Court Division erred in law in decreeing the suit. He finally submits that the plaintiff in order to succeed must establish his own case to obtain a decree, but in the instant case, the plaintiff failed to prove his case. 9. No one appeared on behalf of the respondents to support of the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division. 

 11. It is admitted by the parties that the suit land as described in the schedule of the plaint originally belongs to defendant No.2, Amejan Nessa to the extent of 2 annas share and defendant No.1, Ataiar Rahman to the extent of 14 annas share. The respondents as plaintiffs have come with allegation that defendant No.1, Atiar Rahman, was a minor son of defendant No.2 who as natural guarding-mother of the minor son for want of money had transfer .0825 acre land in favour of plaintiff-predecessor by Sub-Kabala dated 30.06.1969 being No. 8077 and since then the plaintiff-predecessor has been possessing the same for more than 12 years. It has been further alleged that the suit land was recorded primarily in the name of predecessor of plaintiff, namely, Sarowar Hossain, but subsequently defendant No.1 filed Title Suit No.69 of 1987 against Sarowar Hossain and others challenging the transfer deed in Court of learned Assistant Judge, Kushtia and the suit was dismissed on contest and thereafter, the plaintiff of that suit (defendant No.1) filed Title Appeal No.219 of 1987 which was dismissed subsequently and as a result of which the right title interest of the present plaintiff remained intact. Finally, the plaintiff alleged that defendant Nos.1 and 2 in collusion with the settlement official were able to record their names fraudulently and on the basis of such wrong record, they denied the title of the plaintiff. 

 12. On the other hand, the contesting defendant denied the aforesaid contention of the respondent-plaintiff and counter claimed that the deed in favour of the plaintiffs predecessor in respect of suit land is without consideration, collusive, forged and not-acted upon and on the basis of which neither the plaintiff nor his predecessor acquired any right, title, interest and possession of the suit land and that the suit is barred by limitation. 

 "A minor, whose property has been sold by his mother during his minority need not aside the sale which is void, but he can institute a suit for possession within 12 years from the date of the sale or within three years from the date of his attainment of majority whichever may be the later date. If the suit is not so instituted his title in the property would be extinguished under section 28 of the Limitation Act and the subsequent suit would be barred by limitation". 

 15. Apart from that we find, in respect of the suit of the property, Title Suit No.69 of 1987 was instituted by the defendant-respondents claiming his right, title, interest and possession. In respect of that suit, there is a certified copy of the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No.69 of 1987 which has been marked as Exhibit-8 by the trial Court. That suit was filed by the defendant-respondents in the Court of learned Assistant Judge, Kushtia and after holding trial, the learned trial Court dismissed the suit on finding that there is no right, title, interest and possession of the present respondent-defendants in the suit property. A Title Appeal being No.219 of 1987 was preferred against that judgment and decree of dismissal from the side of the present defendant-respondent-petitioners as it appears from Exhibit-9. That appeal was heard and disposed of by the then Sub-ordinate Judge who disallowed the appeal affirming the judgment and dis-missal decree passed by the trial Court. After disposal of such appeal, none challenged such judgment and decree in the High Court Division in a revisional forum. The learned appellate Court below in the instant case, has rightly held that the judgment and decree passed in Title Appeal being No. 219 of 1987 have got its every binding force upon the parties concerned. 

 16. In this respect, plaintiff No.9 while deposing as PW1 stated that the suit land appertaining to Mouza Mozampur under S.A Khatian No.259 originally belong to defendant Nos.1 and 2 and defendant No.2 is the minor son of defendant No.1 who for the purpose of maintaining his minor son (defendant No.2) sold out the suit property measuring .0825 acre in favour of his father on 30.06.1969. He further depoed that soon after such transfer, his father got possession in such land and paid rent after mutating his name in suit Khatian. PW1 further stated that Title Suit being No.69 of 1987 was filed against their predecessor's title document, i.e. Kabala deed No.8077 dated 30.06.1969 by the defendant, but they lost the same up to Appellate Court. During his course of examination, plaintiff No.9 produced their deed dated 30.06.1969, copy of R.S. Khatian No.330, rent receipt showing payment of rent, the DCR, copy of math porcha, copy of S.A Khatian No.259 along with the certified copy of judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No.69 of 1987 and Title Appeal No.219 of 1987. All those documents were produced and being marked as exhibits in course of his examination. Waliur Rahman, PW2, deposed that he is the contagious land holder of the suit property and the plaintiff is in possession of the suit property for long term by erecting boundary wall. During his course of cross examination the aforementioned testimonies of the PWs were not shaken in any manner. On perusal of those evidence on record, we find that there is no intrinsic weakness and inherent infirmity in those testimonies. Thus, we are not in a position to disbelieve them. 

 19. Having gone through the aforementioned state of affairs, we are also inclined to hold that the learned Judge of the Appellate Court below as final court of fact on preponderance of the evidence on record arrived at a conclusive decision that the present respondent (plaintiff) has got right title interest and possession over the suit land.
