full_judgment:
The instant petitioner, earlier as plaintiff, instituted Title Suit No. 686 of 2009 against one Md. Abu Nayeem and 09 others for specific performance of contract. It was stated in the plaint of that suit, inter alia, that the plaintiff entered into an agreement with the defendant Nos. 2-8 of that suit represented by their Power of Attorney holder namely Sharif Madber, to purchase 1650 ajutangsha/10 Katha of land and made payment of earnest money of Taka 5,00,000/- (five lac) on the basis of a registered Bainapatra dated 31.01.2008; however, when the vendor did not execute and register sal kabala deed in favour of the plaintiff i.e the instant petitioner within time after repeated requests made by the petitioner, the petitioner filed the aforesaid suit. Thereafter, the defendants of that suit appeared in the suit initially but they failed to contest the same afterwards and the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka vide its judgment and decree dated 09.03.2011, decreed the suit for specific performance or contract in favour of the petitioner. Till date, the said judgment and decree subsists since neither the instant opposite party Nos. 3-4 nor did their predecessors file any appeal for setting aside the same. 

 03. Thereafter, the petitioner filed Title Execution Case No. 04 of 2011 for execution of decree and obtained a registered sale deed bearing No. 12897 dated 17.10.2011 by the learned Executing Court. Subsequently, the defendant Nos. 1-7 appeared in the Court and filed Miscellaneous Case No. 23 of 2011 under Order 9 Rule 13 read with Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the ex parte decree and restoration of the original suit. Subsequently, the defendant Nos. 1-7 filed an application praying for staying all further proceedings of the Execution Case No. 04 of 2011 but the same was rejected on 01.08.2011. Thereafter they filed another application of the same nature which was also rejected on 10.10.2011. Lastly, the said rejection order was upheld by the Appellate Division vide its judgment and order dated 04.09.2012 passed in Civil Petition For Leave To Appeal No. 2184 of 2012. Consequently, the Miscellaneous Case No. 23 of 2011 was proceeded by the learned Judge of the Executing Court pursuant to the order dated 04.09.2012 passed by the Appellate Division in the aforesaid Civil Petition For Leave To Appeal. However, on 13.04.2014, the same was dismissed for default and the aforesaid order has never been challenged by anyone till date. 

 date was deferred till 08.04.2019 for further trial, again on 08.04.2019, the case was fixed for further trial, however, since the Jail Authority repeatedly failed to produce the accused person namely Mohammad Hossain in Court, therefore, the learned trial Judge failed to proceed with the trial of the case for non-production of the detained accused person to the Court by the Jail Authority and hence, the learned trial Judge constrained to defer the hearing and fixed the next date on 16.04.2019 for further trial; subsequently, on 16.04.2019, the case was again fixed for further trial, however, on an application for time made. by the learned Public Prosecutor for the opposite party No. 2, the learned trial Judge fixed the next date on 30.04.2019 for trial; it was further stated by the petitioner that since the prosecution failed to produce the witnesses from witness No. 6 onwards despite several orders of Summons and Non Bailable Warrant passed by the learned judge of the trial Court for proper adjudication and early conclusion of trial and hence, it was very much uncertain as to when the trial of the case would be concluded; after obtaining the judgment and decree in .Title Suit No. 686 of 2009, the present petitioner being plaintiff started Execution Case No. 04 of 2011 before the concerned court for execution of the decree and thereafter during the pendency. of the execution proceeding, the defendant Nos. 1-7 of that suit (the predecessor of the opposite party No. 3) appeared in the concerned court and filed Miscellaneous Case No. 23 of 2011 under Order 9 Rule 13 read with Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the ex parte decree and restoration of the original suit in its original file and number;. it was also stated by the petitioner that earlier, one Power Packaging and Printing Ltd. and others filed an application under Section 15 of the Money Laundering Protirodh Ain, 2012 before the learned Metropolitan Special Judge, Special Court, Dhaka for revoking the freezing order so far as it relates to the applicant's different bank accounts which was, on transfer, heard by the learned Special Judge, Court No. 5, Dhaka and after hearing the parties concerned, on 15.01.2017, the learned Special Judge allowed the application allowing the applicant to make transactions from those accounts subject to furnishing a bond onto a non-judicial .stamp of BDT. 300.00 (three hundred) undertaking to furnish the necessary information and any lawful demand of any person or entity as determined by Court in respect of those accounts as and when asked by the learned Judge of the Court. Subsequently, on an application filed by the present petitioner, Destiny-2000 Ltd. represented by its Managing Director and another, were added as opposite party Nos. 3 and 4 vide our order dated 09.07.2019. 

 13. The added opposite party No. 3 Destiny-2000 Ltd. also contested the Rule by filing a counter affidavit denying all the material facts and contending, inter alia, that one Abdul Barek Sarker was the owner of the disputed property and after him, his heirs Abu Nayeem Sarker and others came to the possession of the property and executed a power of attorney in favour of one Md. Shahid Uddin Khan who on behalf of the heirs of Abdul Barek Sarker sold out the property to Proschaya Ltd. Thereafter, Proschaya Ltd. decided to sell the property and published notices to this effect in different newspapers to find out if there is any dispute in connection with the property, however, when there was no objection from any quarter, Proschaya Ltd. sold out the property to Destiny Developers Ltd. which then sold out the same to Destiny-2000 Ltd. It is further contended that Proschaya Ltd. went to the possession of the disputed land on 28.05.2009, Destiny Developers Ltd. on 10.02.2010 and Destiny-2000 Ltd. on 16.03.2011 vide different registered sale deeds but the instant third party petitioner having been fully aware of the possession of the property did not implead Proschaya Ltd. or Destiny Developers Ltd. or Destiny-2000 Ltd. as party to Title Suit No. 686 of 2009. It is further contended that in order to come to a conclusion in this case, it requires extensive scrutiny of facts which can only be done through trial and evidence and such highly contentious and disputed questions of facts being not amenable to adjudication under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure, the instant Rule is not maintainable and liable to be discharged. 

 15. Mr. Zakir Hossain Bhuiyan, learned Advocate for the petitioner further submits that the impugned order dated 20.02.2017 passed by the learned Special Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka in Special Case No. 16 of 2016 rejecting the application filed by the petitioner and thereby refusing to release the schedule property from attachment is violative of sections 3, 48, 52, 53 and 53B of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 in view of the fact that the petitioner acquired valid right, title and interest in the scheduled property on the strength of the judgment and decree dated 09.03.2011 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 686 of 2009 arising out of the registered contract for sale and the said contract for sale being earlier in point of time would prevail over the subsequently executed sale deed within the meaning of Section 47 of the Registration Act and as such the impugned order is patently illegal and liable to be set aside. 

 16. Mr. Bhuiyan further submits that the impugned judgment and order dated 20.02.2017 passed by the learned Special Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka in Special Case No. 16 of 2016 rejecting the application filed by the petitioner and thereby refusing to release the scheduled property from attachment is ex-facie illegal and liable to be set aside in view of the fact that the present petitioner acquired valid right, title and interest in the scheduled property on the strength of the judgment and decree dated 09.03.2011 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 686 of 2009 and accordingly, he became the lawful owner of the scheduled property in question upon execution of a registered sale deed bearing No. 12897 dated 17.10.2011 by the concerned Court i.e., before 01 (one) year 01 (one) month and 04 (four) days of making of the said application for attachment dated 21.11.2012; consequently, at the time of making the application for attachment of the property in question by the opposite party No. 2 (Anti-Corruption Commission), Destiny 2000 Ltd. did not have any right, title or interest in the said property, however, the learned Special Judge miserably failed to appreciate this aspect with reference to the documents submitted by the petitioner and passed the impugned judgment and order without applying his judicial mind to the given set of facts and therefore, the impugned order is liable to be set aside. 

 17. Mr. Bhuiyan next submits that the learned Special Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka failed to understand the. purport and scope of Section 15(3) of the Money Laundering Protirodh Ain, 2009 and on erroneous view rejected the application of the petitioner who is a bona-fide purchaser of the property in question for consideration and he acquired valid right, title and interest in the scheduled property on the strength of the judgment and decree dated 09.03.2011 passed by the learned Court of Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 686 of 2009, therefore, the impugned order passed by the learned Special Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka is patently illegal and hence, the impugned order is liable to be set aside and the property in question be released in his favour of the petitioner being released from the attachment. 

 18. Mr. Bhuiyan also submits that the learned Special Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka failed to understand the purport and scope of Section 15(3) of the Money Laundering Protirodh Ain, 2009 and on erroneous view rejected the application of the petitioner in view of the fact that Destiny 2000 Ltd. purchased the schedule property in question during the pendency of Title Suit No. 686 of 2009 before the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka and the fact of pendency of the said suit was intimated to the Destiny 2000 Ltd. by a Cautionary Notice dated 26.01.2010 and therefore, Destiny 2000 Ltd. should be subjected to the result of the suit in view of the settled proposition of law that a transfer of the land in suit being subject-matter of the pending suit is hit by the doctrine of lis pendens as enshrined in Section 52 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 and accordingly, such a transfer is void in the eye of law pursuant to Section 53B of the said Act, 1982, and accordingly, the impugned order passed by the learned Special Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka is ex-facie illegal and hence, the impugned order is liable to be set aside and the property in question is liable to be released from attachment in favour of the petitioner after releasing it from attachment. 

 20. Mr. Roman next submits that since the schedule property in question has got no minimum connection with the alleged money laundering or any such offence/s and the instant petitioner is in no way directly or indirectly connected with the alleged money laundering or any such offence/s and the petitioner is neither an accused in the Special Case nor he is a nominee or in any way representative of the accused person/s of the said case and Destiny 2000 Ltd. does not have any tight, title or interest in the said property, on the other hand, the petitioner is a bona-fide purchaser of the property in question with value and he acquired valid right, title and interest in the scheduled property on the strength of the judgment and decree dated 09.03.2011 passed by the learned Court of Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 686 of 2009, therefore, the impugned order dated 20.02.2017 passed by the learned Special Judge is liable to be set aside and the property in question should be released in favour of the petitioner. 

 22. Both Mr. Zakir Hossain Bhuiyan and Mr. Mahfujur Rahman Roman next submit in chorus that since the schedule property in question has not any connection with the alleged money laundering or any such offence/s and the petitioner is in no way directly or indirectly connected with the alleged money laundering or any such offence/s and the petitioner is neither any accused of the special case nor he is a nominee or in any way representative of the accused person/s of the said case and Destiny 2000 Ltd. does not have any right, title or interest in the said property; on the other hand, the petitioner is a bona-fide purchaser of the property for value and he has acquired valid right, title and interest in the scheduled property on the strength of the judgment and decree dated 09.03.2011 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 686 of 2009, therefore, the impugned order dated 20.02.2017 passed by the learned Special Judge is liable to be set aside and the property in question is liable to be released in his favour of the petitioner being released from attachment. 

 33. Mr. Mainul further contends that at the time of filing of the Title Suit No. 686 of 2009, the title no longer rests in the vendors since the vendors earlier sold the entire property to Proschaya Ltd. vide a registered sale deed being No. 5198 dated 28.05.2009 long before the filing of the said suit and since the instant opposite party Nos. 3-4 or their predecessor were not made party to that suit, the judgment and decree simply fails. 

 34. It is his further contention that Destiny-2000 Ltd. was a necessary party to that suit for specific performance of contract and since they were not made party to that suit, the suit was not maintainable and the judgment and decree passed in the suit is bad for defect of parties and hence, the Rule issued in the instant case is liable to be discharged. In support of the above submission, the learned Advocate refers to the decision in the case of Ezaher Meah vs. Shaher Banu reported in 49 DLR (AD) 85 wherein it was held that the proper form of decree is to direct specific performance of the contract between the vendor and the plaintiff and direct subsequent transferee to join in the conveyance so as to pass on the title which resides in him to the plaintiff in order to avoid all controversies. The learned Advocate also puts reliance on the decision in the case of Nurul Islam and others vs. Jamila Khatun and others reported in 53 DLR (AD) 45 wherein it was also held that in a suit for specific performance of contract for sale of immovable property plaintiff is entitled to delivery of possession; a trespasser in the suit property is liable to be impleaded in the suit and evicted from the suit property to give effective relief to the plaintiff. In respect of this submission, the learned Advocate has also emphasized on the decisions of the cases of Jahangir Sarker vs. Motaleb and another, reported in 11 BLC 391; Sooraya Rahman vs. Hajee Md. Elias and others, reported in 8 BLC (AD) 7 and Abdul Khaleque Sowdagar and another vs. Mohammad Fazlul Huq and another, reported in 26 DLR 247. 

 35. Mr. Mainul next contends that the opposite party No. 3 is a subsequent transferee for value who had paid his money on good faith without notice of the original contract for sale and he has been possessing the same from the date of purchase and hence, the opposite party No. 3 is a bonafide purchaser of the entire property for consideration/value thereof and as such, his right should not be affected and he is entitled to hold his title against the plaintiff of the suit (the instant petitioner) for specific performance of contract in view of Sections 53 and proviso of 53A of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 read with Section 27 (b) of the Specific Relief Act, 1877. 

 36. Mr. Mainul also contends that since the opposite party No. 3 was a necessary party and in his absence, the judgment and decree for specific performance of contract fails in view of aforesaid provisions of law and hence the title is seriously disputed in between the instant petitioner and the opposite party No. 3 which is a disputed question of facts and unless the registered sale deed executed in favour of the opposite party No. 3 is declared null and void by a competent civil court, the same cannot be adjudicated in the instant case by this Court exercising its jurisdiction under Section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 

 41. In reply to the submission of the learned Advocate for the opposite party No. 3 regarding maintainability of the earlier suit for specific performance of contract and judgment and decree passed therein being bad for defect of parties, Mr Zakir Hossain Bhuiyan and Mr. Mahfujur Rahman Roman, the learned Advocates for the petitioner vehemently contend that in a suit for specific performance of contract only the parties to the contract are necessary parties and addition of 3rd Party without any reason in such a suit would convert it into a suit for determination of title and this is not permissible in law. In support of this submission, the Advocates have placed reliance on several decisions reported in the case of 2Md. Atif Atiq and another represented by their lawful attorney SK. Abdul Hye Bacchu Vs Nurun Nahar Begum and others, reported in 18 MLR (AD) 65 wherein it was held by the Hon'ble Appellate Division that if the property under contract of sale is sold to a third party or remains in possession of third party, the right, title and interest of the person with whom contract was first entered into, shall not, in any way, be affected. In another case of Ibrahim Khalil and others Vs Mujibir Rahman and others, reported in 18 BLC (AD) 23 wherein the Hon'ble Appellate Division held that in a suit for specific performance of contract, the question to be decided whether there had been a valid contract between the parties and whether consideration money was paid as per terms of the contract. Furthermore, in a suit for specific performance of contract, the 3rd Party is not a necessary party to the suit and in this connection, the learned Advocates have referred several decisions including the case of Nurun Nahar Begum vs Abdul Khaleque Choukder, reported in 43 DLR (AD) 107  wherein our Apex Court held that addition of party in a suit for specific performance of contract — the appellants averments in the application for addition of party setting up an independent title to the land disentitle them to be included as parties within the framework of the present suit wherein the real question to be determined is whether the contract for sale between the parties therein was genuine and whether on the basis thereof the plaintiffs are entitled to get a decree. The averments for addition of party will convert the present suit into one for determination of title which is not permissible in law. The similar view was also adopted in several cases of Jamir Ahmed Vs. Siddique Ahmed Sowdagor and others, reported in 14 BL7' (AD) 16, Feroja khatoon vs. brajalal nato & others, reported in 43 DLR 160 and Muzaffor Ali and another vs. Messrs Monwora Hospital and others, reported in 51 DLR 341. 

 42. Refuting the last submission advanced by the learned Advocate for the opposite party No. 3, Mr. Zakir Hossain Bhuiyan and Mr. Mahfiijur Rahman Roman, the learned Advocates for the petitioner, submit that the predecessor of the opposite party No. 3 namely, Proschaya Ltd. got the registered sale deed being No. 5198 on 28.05.2009 when the registered contract for sale executed in favour of the petitioner subsisted and the same was never lawfully rescinded and accordingly, in view of Section 53B of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, the subsequent sale deeds shall be deemed to be .void ab-initio; additionally, at the time of selling the property to the said Proschaya Ltd., the original vendors did not have subsisting interest, right and title over the suit schedule property in view of Section 7 of the said Act since they earlier entered into a registered contract for sale with the instant petitioner and hence, the later executed and registered sale deed/s is/are void ab-initio and the said proposition has been settled by our Apex Court by a series of judicial pronouncements. The learned Advocates for the petitioner further contend that before purchasing the suit scheduled property, the Proschaya Ltd. or the opposite party No. 3 was required to take reasonable care to ascertain that the transferors (the original vendors) had power to make the transfer and/or they have acted in good faith in the transaction in view of Section 41 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, otherwise they cannot take the plea of bona tide purchasers for consideration/value without notice of the original contract for sale; in order to determine the valid right, interest and title of the vendors over the property, the opposite party No. 3 or their predecessors should have checked up the concerned Sub-Registrar's Office what transfers, if any, had been made by the transferor. Since registration of any document constitutes sufficient notice in view of Explanation I to Section 3 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, the opposite party No. 3 cannot take the plea of their being bona fide purchasers for consideration/value without notice of the original contract for sale since the existence of the registered deed of contract for sale executed in favour of the petitioner would be revealed if the opposite party No. 3 or their predecessor would take reasonable care to ascertain the title of their vendor and hence, they cannot be protected by Sections 41, 53 and 53A of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882. In support of this submission, the learned Advocates for the petitioner have placed reliance on a catena of decisions as reported in the case of Abdul Awal and others Vs Narayan Chandra Das, reported in 13 MLR (AD) 71 wherein it was held that where the deeds are void ab-initio the plaintiff is not required to seek declaration or cancellation thereof. In another case of Most. Nazera Bibi and another Vs. Abdul Mazid and others, reported in 12 ALR (2018) (1) (AD) 118 it was held that when the document in question is void one, the question of seeking its cancellation would not be necessary; it is only when a document is a voidable, that is valid until it is declared as void, in that case the question of seeking its cancellation would arise. The similar view was also adopted in the cases of Chitta Ranjan Chakraborty and others Vs. Abdur Rab, reported in 2 MLR (AD) 58, Rabeya Khatun and others Vs. Moniruddin and others re-ported in 8 BLC (AD) 121, Husan Ali and Another Vs. Azmaluddin and Others, reported in 14 DLR 392 Wahidha Begum Vs. Tajul Islam, reported in 8 BLT 238 and Nagendra Chandra Bhattacharjee Vs. Parameswari Ray, reported in 9 DLR 476. 

 44. The case of the present petitioner mainly rests upon four propositions, namely, the consequences of the judgment and decree and subsequent orders passed in favour of the present petitioner by a competent civil court having jurisdiction to pass the same, the fate of the subsequently registered sale deed executed by the original vendors in favour of the predecessors of the instant opposite party No. 3 and the subsequent sale deeds registered in favour of the opposite party No. 3, whether the opposite party No. 3 or his predecessor was necessary party in the Title Suit filed by the present petitioner and whether there is any error of law apparent on the face of the impugned judgment and order dated 20.02.2017 passed by the learned Special Judge, Dhaka. 

 50. In this context we would like to point out that the Supreme Court of Bangladesh with 02 (two) Divisions has been established under Article 94 of the Constitution. Under Article 101 of the Constitution, the High Court Division has been conferred such original, appellate and other jurisdictions and powers by the Constitution or any other law. Under Clause 6 of the Fourth Schedule of the Constitution, all original, appellate and other jurisdiction which was vested in the High Court constituted by the Provisional Constitution of Bangladesh Order 1972 has vested in and is exercised by the High Court Division. Consequently, 

 61. In the present case in hand; the aforesaid judgment and decree dated 09.03.2011 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court and subsequent orders are still in force since neither the opposite party No. 3 nor did their predecessors has filed any appeal for setting aside the same till today. On perusal of the record of the case, we have noticed that the opposite party No. 3 had been intimated about the pendency of the Title Suit No. 686 of 2009 vide an intimation letter attaching a Cautionary 

 62. The next proposition of the case is the fate of the registered sale deed registered by the original vendors in favour of the predecessors of the instant opposite party No. 3 and the subsequent sale deeds registered in favour of the opposite party No. 3 and whether the opposite party No. 3 or his predecessor was a necessary party in the aforesaid title suit filed by the present petitioner. 

 63. In this regard we find force in the arguments advanced by the learned Advocates for the petitioner who have strenuously submitted that the present petitioner first came to learn about the opposite party No. 3 when the petitioner and the Bailiff went to the suit scheduled property to have the delivery of possession in favour of the petitioner pursuant to the order of the Executing Court and also when the opposite party No. 3 filed a written objection before the Special Judge against the application filed by the petitioner. The petitioner only then came to know that during the existence of the registered agreement for sale and during the pendency of the title suit, the vendors transferred the entire property to one Proschaya Ltd. and subsequently to the instant opposite party No. 3 and hence, there arose no question of impleading them in the said suit since by that time the petitioner got the sale deed registered pursuant to the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No. 686 of 2009. Apart from this, neither the opposite party No. 3 nor their predecessor is a necessary party in the suit for specific performance of contract. 

 "In a suit for specific performance of contract, the claim of title of a third party cannot be considered and as such, the plea of the petitioner that having title in the suit property he is required to be impleaded as defendant does not inspired us at all to interfere in the matter." 

 65. The similar view has also been adopted in the case of Md. Atif Atiq and another vs Nurun Nahar Begum and others, reported in 18 MLR (AD) (2013) 65, wherein our Apex Court held that "if the property under contract of sale is sold to a third party or remains in the possession of the third party, the right, title and interest of the person with whom contract was first entered into, shall not, in any way, be affected." 

 This Division even did not approve of addition of party who set up independent title in a suit for specific performance of contract in the case of Golam Kader being dead his heirs: Nurun Nahar Begum vs Abdul Khaleque Choukder, reported in 43 DLR (AD) 107. 

 In the aforesaid case, it has been held that "the appellants' averments in the application for addition of party setting up an independent title to the land disentitle them to be included as parties within the framework of the present suit wherein the real question to be determined is whether the contract for sale between the parties therein was genuine and whether on the basis thereof the plaintiffs are entitled to get a decree. It has further held that the averment for addition of party will convert the present suit into one for determination of title which is not permissible in law (paragraph-14). 

 67. Now, reverting to the case in hand, in so far as it relates to the registered sale deed in favour of the opposite party No. 3 and its predecessors, the learned Advocates for the petitioner emphatically submit that the predecessor of the opposite party No. 3 namely Proschaya Ltd. got the registered sale deed being No. 5198 on 28.05.2009 when the registered contract for sale in favour of the petitioner subsisted and the same was never lawfully rescinded and accordingly, in view of Section 53B of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, the subsequent sale deeds shall be deemed to be void ab-initio. Additionally, at the time of selling the property to the said Proschaya Ltd., the original vendors did not have subsisting interest, right and title over the suit schedule property in view of Section 7 of the said Act since they earlier entered into a registered contract for sale with the instant petitioner and hence, the later executed and registered sale deed/s is/are void ab-initio and the said proposition has been settled by our Apex Court in a catena of judicial precedents including the case of Abdul Awal and others vs Narayan Chandra Das as reported in 13 MLR (AD)  71. wherein our apex court held as under: 

 "Relief against parties and persons claiming under them by subsequent title 

 (b) any other person claiming under him by a title arising subsequently to the contract, except a transferee for value who has paid his money in good faith and without notice of the original contract; 

 77. Having carefully gone through the aforesaid provisions as well as other relevant provisions, we find force in the arguments advanced by the learned Advocates for the petitioner to the effect that before purchasing the suit scheduled property, the Proschaya Ltd. or the opposite party No. 3 was required to take reasonable care to ascertain that the transferors (the original vendors) had power to make the transfer and/or they have acted in good faith in the transaction in view of Section 41 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, otherwise they cannot take the plea of their being bonafide purchasers with consideration/value. In order to determine the valid right, title and interest of the vendors in the property, the opposite party No. 3 or their predecessors should have checked up the Registrar's Office as to what transfers, if any, had been made by the transferor. Since registration of any documents constitutes sufficient notice in view of Explanation I to Section 3 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, and hence, the opposite party No. 3 cannot claim to be a bonafide purchaser for consideration/value without notice since the existence of the registered deed of agreement for sale would be revealed if the opposite party No. 3 or their predecessor would take reasonable care to ascertain the title of their vendor and hence, they cannot be protected by Section 41, 53 and 53A of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 and section 27 (b) of the Specific Relief Act, 1877. 

 78. In this context it may further be stated that in the case of Rabeya Khatun vs Moniruddin and others, reported in 8 BLC (AD) 121 the Apex Court held that "The ratio of judicial pronouncements is that for applicability of section 41 of the Act, 1882 primarily two things must concur, 1) that the person i.e., ostensible owner, who has no real title was clothed with the insignia of ownership with the consent, express or implied, of the real owner; and 2) that the person purchasing for value from the ostensible owner shall take reasonable care to ascertain that his transferor has authority to make the transfer. Because of authoritative of pronouncement of series of cases it is also the settled matter that a person purchasing from a person who is not the real owner can only protect himself by showing that he acted as a prudent man and that if he makes no inquiry into title, such as a prudent purchaser would make, or avoids prosecuting such an inquiry he cannot claim protection and the principle that a man cannot give what he has not must applied." Now, as to making reasonable inquiry by the purchaser, such as a prudent purchaser would make, a Division Bench of the High Court Division in the case of Husan Ali and another vs Azmaluddin and others, reported in 14 DLR 392 has held that "Section 41 of the Transfer of Property Act makes it incumbent upon the transferee to act in good faith and to take reasonable care to ascertain that the transferor had power to make the transfer. It is obvious that the first step which the transferee is expected to take is to search the registration office to ascertain what transfers, if any, had been made by the transferor.  The transferee is not entitled to the benefit of section 41 of the Act, 1882 if he or she fails to do so (para-M (emphasis as laid is ours)." 

 79. In another case a Division Bench of the High Court Division held that "If one wants to be protected under Section 41 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 he is required to prove that he took all reasonable care to ascertain the title of his vendor. He inquired at least in the local sub-registrar's office to know if the land had charge or previous encumbrance or not to establish his bonafide (8 BLT 238). More so, in another case the High Court Division held that "Registration is sufficient notice when the document is compulsorily registrable (9 DLR 476)." 

 80. Accordingly, the contention of the learned Advocate for the opposite party No. 3 as to his claim being bonafide purchaser for consideration without notice of the previous contract for sale does not satisfy us at all. In this regard, in order to effectuate the tight, title and interest of the opposite party No. 3 pursuant to the registered sale deeds executed in his favour, the opposite party No. 3 ought to have filed a separate suit seeking adequate reliefs for protecting its right, title or possession, if any, in the suit property and having failed to do so, their contention cannot be considered in the instant case in view of the fact that the present petitioner relies on his right, title and interest in the property on the strength of the judgment and decree dated 09.03.2011 passed by the learned Judge in Title Suit No. 686 of 2009 and subsequent registered deed of sale dated 17.10.2011 executed by Court and the same being subsisting, is binding on all concerned, whereas, the opposite party No. 3 only relies on the registered deed of sale and the same is void ab-initio in view of Sections 7, 41 and 53B of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882. The plea of subsequent transferee with value and that he had no notice of the previous sale agreement was settled by the Appellate Division in the case cited in 21 DLR (AD) 333, wherein, it was held that "The onus lies on the subsequent transferee to prove absence of such notice and mere denial in the written statement that he had no notice of the previous sale is not sufficient to discharge onus." 

 81. Now again coming to the case in our hand, in dealing with the application for releasing the property from attachment filed by the petitioner, the learned Special Judge ought to have considered that the schedule property in question has not any connection with the alleged money laundering or any such offence/s and the instant petitioner is in no way directly or indirectly connected with the alleged money laundering or any such offence/s and the petitioner is neither any accused of the special case nor is he any nominee or in any way representative of the accused person/s of the said case and the learned Special Judge failed to consider that Destiny 2000 Ltd. did not have any right, title or interest in the said property; on the other hand, the petitioner is a bona-fide purchaser of the property in question with value and he acquired valid right, title and interest in the scheduled property on the strength of the judgment and decree dated 09.03.2011 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 686 of 2009. 

 82. The learned Special Judge further failed to consider that the petitioner acquired valid right, title and interest in the scheduled property and since the judgment and decree dated 09.03.2011 and subsequent orders passed by the learned Joint District Judge and the registered sale deed in favour of the petitioner still subsist and the opposite party No. 3 or their predecessor had never attempted to challenge or set aside the same in spite of having definite and specific knowledge about the said judgment and decree and subsequent orders of a competent civil court, and hence, the petitioner is entitled to have the scheduled property released in his favour from attachment.

Sree Kanailal Boshak
Vs.
Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Naogaon and another
full_judgment:
2. The facts giving rise to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus, the present petitioner as plaintiff instituted the original Other Class Suit No.66 of 1998 in the Court of learned the then Sub-ordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Naogaon against the defendant-opposite party for declaration of title in respect of 'Ka' schedule property contending inter alia that the suit property appertaining to Mouza Hajinagar under Neyamatpur police station of District-Naogaon corresponding to C.S. khatian No.107 and S.A. khatian No.2, 88 and R.S. khatian No.1 in C.S. plot No.733, 212, 176 and present plot No.1145, 82 and 123 comprising an area of 3.60 acres of land originally belonged to Koibara Estate. The Zamindar of the said estate while owning and possessing the suit property transferred 0.18 acres of land out of 2.43 acres of C.S. plot No.733 in favour of one Krishna Mohon Fouzdar and the remaining portion of the 'Ka' schedule land was settled in favour of the plaintiff in the year 1351 B.S. at a 'Najar' of Tk.105/- (one hundred and five). The plaintiff paid rent to the Zamindar and obtained 'dakhila'. Subsequently, while the land vested upon the government the plaintiff paid rent to the government `seresta' and the S.A. 107/5 attested khatian was prepared in the name of plaintiff and thereafter, during R.S. operation the land has been correctly prepared in the name of the plaintiff in field `bujarat' khatian No.632. Subsequently, while the khatian was finally prepared in the name of defendant No.2 the plaintiff filed an Objection Case being No.195/1972, which was allowed on contest on 22.10.1972. The legal heirs of Krishna Mohon Fowjdar by a transfer deed dated 08.04.1997 sold out his 18 decimals of land of 'Ka' schedule in favour of the plaintiff and the sub-kabala was registered in Neyamatpur Sub-registry Office. In this way, the plaintiff after acquiring the entire 'Ka' schedule property use to possess the same and on 09.07.1998 the Union Land Office declined to accept rent from the plaintiff, disclosing that the property-in-dispute has become khash property under the government and the government will settle the land. Thereafter, on 19.08.1998 on getting the certified copy of the khatian, the plaintiff came to know that the suit property has been wrongly recorded in the name of government, which constrained the plaintiff to institute the original suit for declaration of title. 

 3. The contrary case of the government in short is thus, that the suit is not maintainable and barred by limitation and the same is bad for defect of parties. The further case of the government-opposite party is such that during R.S. operation the land has been correctly recorded in the name of government as khash land as the land is under the "Shyrat Mohol" and in the remark column of the khatian, it has been cited that the property is being used by the people of the locality at large from the very beginning, using the water of the suit property for their agricultural purposes and the plaintiff having no manner of right, title, interest and possession in the suit property on the basis of false allegation filed the suit. 

 8. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the learned Appellate Court during disposal of the appeal committed gross illegality and irregularity. The learned Advocate further submits that the learned court of appeal below committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice, by not considering that the plaintiff obtained settlement of the suit land on 27th Magh of 1351 B.S. and the settlement paper has been properly proved by the plaintiff which has been marked as Exhibit-1. The subsequent Vakhilas' were also proved and marked as Exhibits-2-2(Ga). The learned Advocate also submits that the learned Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Naogaon without rebutting the findings of the trial court adverting evidence on records, reversed the judgment and decree passed by the trial court illegally and in passing the impugned judgment and decree there has been misreading and non reading of evidence and non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned counsel argued that the property-in-dispute had been correctly recorded in the name of plaintiff-petitioner in the field `bujarati khatian No.632 during the preparation of R.S. record of right and subsequently, the suit land have been wrongly recorded in the name of defendant No.2 and against that wrong record the plaintiff filed an Objection Case being No.195 of 1972 before the concerned settlement officer and the settlement officer on hearing both the parties allowed the objection Case No.195 of 1972 on 22.01.1972 A.D. vide Exhibit-5 and accordingly the government after acceptance of rents granted rent receipt in favour of the plaintiff vide Exihibit-6 and the learned appellate court was totally misconceived in appreciating the documentary evidences adduced from the plaintiffs side, which has been marked as Exhibits-1-8. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the government admitting the plaintiffs tenancy right to the suit property recognizing the plaintiff a tenant under government, granted rent receipt after accepting rents and the learned trial court after proper evaluation of the evidence on records conclusively held that the plaintiff has successfully discharged his onus of proof, but the defendants have hopelessly failed to disprove the case of the plaintiff and there is no evidence excepting the attested photocopy of the R.S. khatian No.1 marked as Exhibit-'Ka' from the side of the government to justify their case that the property has been vested to the government and the R.S. record of right has been rightly prepared, but the learned appellate court during disposal of the appeal without proper sifting of evidence in its true perspective and without proper appreciation of law, arbitrarily decided the merit of the appeal in favour of the appellant and passed the impugned judgment and decree, which is liable to be set aside. 

 10. In order to appreciate the argument advanced from the sides of the learned counsels for the respective parties, on perusal of the impugned judgment and decree dated 25.08.2011 and the judgment and decree passed by the trial court in Other Class Suit No.66 of 1998, the evidence led from the sides of the respective parties and all other relevant papers including the case records it transpires that, admittedly the disputed property described in schedule `ka' of the plaint originally belonged to `Koibara Estate' and it is the pleading's case of the plaintiff that the Zamindar of the said estate from the C.S. plot No.733 settled 0.18 acres of land out of 2.43 acres of land in favour of one Krishna Mohon Fowjdar and in respect of the remaining land of schedule 'Ka', the Ex-Zamindar settled that land in favour of the plaintiff-petitioner on 27th Magh of 1351 B.S. The Zamindari papers have been produced from the side of the plaintiff, and these documents support the plaintiff's pleadings case and these papers after its formal proof under the Evidence Act, have been marked as Exhibit-1-2(Ka) and 2 (Ga) respectively. From the said Zamindari papers, it transpires that the Zamindar after accepting rent from the plaintiff granted rent receipts of their `Koibara Estate'. I also find from the documentary evidences adduced from the side of the plaintiff that the R.S. attested khatian No.107/5 was prepared in the name of plaintiff marked as Exhibit-3 and the papers relating to Objection Case No.195/1972 (Exhibit-5), the relevant attested khatian No. 632 and 107/5 in the name of the plaintiff-petitioner and the government rent received including the information slip relating to the positive contention of the plaintiff, go to show that the right to the plaintiff-petitioner in respect of the suit property has been accepted by the government-opposite party and all the official papers definitely have a presumptive value under the ambit of section 114(e) of the Evidence Act, 1872. Besides this, it is also apparent from the rent receipt granted in favour of the plaintiff by the government that the government after accepting the rents from the plaintiff in respect of the suit property is now stopped from challenging the plaintiff's tenancy and it appears that, all these papers were properly evaluated by the trial court at the time of disposal of the Other Class Suit No.66 of 1998. 

 12. P.W.1 the plaintiff Kanai Lal in his testimony testified that he is the plaintiff to the suit and at a stage of his testimony he has categorically testified that, initially the draft S.A. khatian was prepared in his name and the S.A. attested khatian No.107/5 was prepared in the name of him and the field 'bujarat' khatian No.632 was also prepared in his name and subsequently while he came to know that the khatian has been finally published in the name of the defendant No.2, he filed an Objection Case being No.195/1972 which was allowed on contest and there has been an order from the office of the settlement officer that a khatian will be opened in his name (the plaintiff). The plaintiff in his deposition categorically testified that the legal heirs of Krishna Mohon Fowjdar after the death of Krishna Mohon transferred the land measuring 18 decimals in favour of the plaintiff-petitioner vide a registered sub-kabala deed dated 08.04.1997, which has been marked as Exhibit-8. During cross-examination from the side of the defendants, P.W.1 replied in a question that the property-in-dispute is never used by the people of the locality as `Shyrat Mohol, rather; the suit property is being used by him since his settlement. With regard to the boundaries of the suit land, P.W.1 Kanai Lal categorically testified about the boundary men, who are in possession in their lands, besides the suit land. 

 16. Vis-à-vis; the one and only witness of the defendant, D.W.1 Md. Abdul Mazid in his testimony testified that he is an Assistant Tahshildar of Hajinagar Union Land Office. He has brought the R.S. record book, wherefrom it appears that the suit property has been entried in khash khatian No.1. He has submitted the attested R.S. khatian which has been marked as Exhibit-'Ka'. During cross-examination D.W.1 in a reply to a question from the side of the plaintiff, testified that he has brought no paper showing that the suit land was ever possessed by the government through lease. D.W. 1, the concerned official witness of the government-opposite party in his testimony frankly admitted that the government rent receipt which has been produced from the side of the plaintiff, was issued by the government.

caseno: F.M.A. No. 157 of 2015 with C. Rule No. 656 (FM)/2011.
parties:
DR. A.K.M. MUZTABA AND OTHERS 
Vs. 
AHSAN HABIB KHAN AND OTHERS
full_judgment:
2. The facts relevant for disposal of the appeal in a nutshell can be stated thus that the present appellants as petitioners filed a Miscellaneous Case being No. 10 of 1998 under section 35(1) of the Waqf Ordinance, 1962 in the Court of learned District Judge, Bagerhat for a declaration that the disputed property is not waqf property contending inter alia that the case land along with other lands originally belonged to one Sayed Ali, Abdul Gafur and Abdul Goni. Hasan Ali the predecessor of the petitioners obtained the case land through settlement for the limited period. Subsequently, Hasan Ali executed a kabuliat in favour of Sayed All and others. The kabuliat was registered on 31.10.1939. The period of settlement although was expired in the year 1950, even then; Hasan Ali was possessing the property-in-dispute by handing over. In this way, a tenancy was created in favour of Hasan Ali by the conduct of Sayed Ali and others. Sayed Ali and others instituted a Rent Suit being No. 1788 of 1958 against Hasan Ali for realization of arrear rents. The further case of the petitioners is such that the case land was not recorded wrongly in the name of Hasan Ali in the S.A. khatian and for that reason Hasan Ali filed a Title Suit being No. 02 of 1972 for declaration of title in the disputed property and that suit was decreed on compromise in terms of "solenama". In this way, the petitioners acquired title in the disputed property and a registered Osiotnama ' was subsequently executed by Hasan Ali in favour of the petitioners. Hasan Ali died in the year 1975. The case land is a homestead property and the petitioners are residing therein after constructing their residential sheds. The petitioners had been owning and possessing the case land by payment of rents, taxes etc. and the case property was not a waqf property in the name and style "Karom Ali Khan Waqf Estate". The further case of the petitioners is such that Karom Ali Khan had no title and interest in the case property and he had no right to declare the property Waqf On 02.04.1978 on behalf of the Deputy Commissioner, Bagerhat the Thana Nirbahi Officer concerned issued a notice for eviction directing the petitioners to handover the vacant possession of the disputed property in favour of the opposite parties which constrained the plaintiffs to file a Title Suit being No.86 of 1997 in the Court of learned Assistant Judge, Bagerhat for permanent injunction against the defendants to that suit. It is also the case of the petitioners that the order of the Administrator of Waqf, Dhaka, Bangladesh vide his office Memo No. 1281/Khu dated 05.01.1997 as well as the order dated 28.05.1998 relating to the eviction of the petitioners treating the case property waqf property are illegal, null and void and without jurisdiction. Challenging the orders of the Waqf Administrator the petitioners filed the miscellaneous case. 

 3. The contrary case of the opposite parties in short is thus that one Karom Ali Khan, son of Nayan Khan was the owner of' the case property and the owner of the property in the name of 'Almighty Allah' declared the property as waqf estate in respect of 327 bighas of land including the case property. A deed of waqf was executed on 29.09.1921 and Karom Ali Khan became the Motowalli of the property. The further case of the opposite parties is such that at the demise of Karom Ali Khan, his two sons namely Syed Ali Khan and Abdul Gafur Khan and grandson Abdul Goni Khan were appointed Motowalli of the waqf estate. They were the Joint Molowallies of the estate which was enrolled as waqf property in the office of the Waqf Administrator under E.C. No. 11050. Subsequently, the case land was recorded in the name of Motowalli. It is the case of the opposite parties that Hasan Ali was the son-in-law of Abdul Gofur Khan who was a lawyer. Out of love and affection Hasan Ali was permitted to reside in the homestead of the case land from his father-in-law Abdul Gofur Khan and as such he was a permissive possessor in the case property. Taking advantage of that, Hasan Ali fraudulently crated a kabuliat showing settlement of the case land in favour of Syed Ali and others. Subsequently, realizing the fault; Hasan Ali gave up his claim over the suit property by executing a 'nadabipatry' on 09.03.1952. A Refit Suit was filed by Wahed Ali against Masan Ali with regard to the estate for arrear rents, in which a fraudulent `solenama' was filed and in that Rent Suit the Waqf Administrator was not made party intentionally. A Title Suit being No. 02 of 1972 was also filed in respect of the case property and in that suit another fraudulent 'solenama' was filed. The Administrator of Waqf was not a party to that suit also. That suit was filed with regard to the S.A. record of right. The opposite parties knowing about the fraudulent 'solenama' informed the Administrator of Waqf who issued a show cause notice upon Saleh Ahmed, the father of the petitioners. An Inspector of Waqf inquired into the matter and submitted his report to the Waqf Administrator and the Administrator of Waqf being satisfied requested the Deputy Commissioner, Bagerhat to evict Saleh Ahmed from the case property vide Memo dated 05.01.1997 and the Deputy Commissioner, Bagerhat directed the concerned Thana Nirbahi Officer to do the needful. Thana Nirbahi Officer accordingly served a notice upon the petitioners for eviction, against which the petitioners out of ill-motive to grab the waqf property filed a suit for permanent injunction being No.86 of 1997 which is pending for disposal. 

 7. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the appellants submits that the learned District Judge, Bagerhat during disposal of the miscellaneous case committed illegality and failed to appreciate that the predecessor-in-interest of the present appellants Md. Hasan Ali obtained the case property through a settlement by the original owners of the property namely Syed Ali Khan, Abdul Gofur Khan and Abdul Goni Khan. The learned District Judge also failed to appreciate that a kabuliat was executed and registered by the settlement holder Hasan Ali -in favour of the Owners of the property on 31.10.1939. Since the settlement was for a limited period, it was expired in the year 1950 A.D. But the fact remains that the predecessor of the appellants, Hasan Ali had been owning and possessing the property by handing over, and accordingly tenancy right was accrued in favour of Hasan Ali by the conduct of the original owners who brought a Rent Suit being No.1788 of 1958 against Hasan Ali for realization of arrear rents. The learned trial court during disposal of the miscellaneous case could not realize that, against the S.A. record of right in respect of the case property Hasan Ali filed a Title Suit being No. 02 of 1972 which was decreed on compromise by way of solenama' and in this way the appellants acquired title and interest in the case property. A registered `osiotnama' was executed and registered by Hasan Ali in favour of the appellants on 09.11.1974 prior to his death in the year 1975 and all these facts has been corroborated from the evidence of P.W.1, but the learned trial court i.e. the District Judge, Bagerhat without proper assessment of evidence and appreciation of law arrived at an erroneous decision that the case property is a wall-estate, which has been declared as waqf property by the original owner of the land Md. Karam Ali Khan. The learned Advocate also submits that the learned District Judge committed an error in law resulting in an error in the decision in not holding that the disputed deed of waqf dated 29.09.1921 is not related to the case property which was in respect of the land appertaining to Bagerhat Police Station. The property showing in the waqf deed relating to Morelgonj police station is different and not identical with the case property. The learned Advocate submits that in fact, Karam Ali Khan was not the owner of the disputed property and he had no authority to declare the case property waqf estate which is not properly evaluated and appraised by the learned trial Judge during disposal of the Miscellaneous Case No. 10 of 1998. The learned Advocate lastly in support of his contention referred some decisions reported in 19 DLR 106 and 2 BLC 517. 

 8. As against the aforesaid submission of the learned counsel for the appellants the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondents opposing the grounds of the appeal memo submits that, the learned District Judge, Bagerhat during disposal of the original miscellaneous case committed no illegality or irregularity. The learned Advocate further submits that the present appellants who were the petitioners of the miscellaneous petition under section 35(1) of the Waqf Ordinance, 1962 failed to prove their respective case by adducing tangible evidence. The oral and documentary evidences led from the sides of the respective parties were properly evaluated and discussed by the learned trial Judge during disposal of the case on merit. The learned Advocate also submits that the learned District Judge, Bagerhat after proper assessment of evidence and appreciation of law arrived at a conclusive decision relying upon the authentic evidence that the property-in-dispute is a waqf property and the Waqf Administrator was totally empowered to pass an order under section 50 of the Waqf Ordinance of 1962 treating the property as waqf property pursuant to E.C. No. 11050. The learned Advocate submits that the Rent Suit which was marked as Exhibit-11 was in fact not tiled by the motowallies or their legal heirs and neither the C.S. recorded tenants nor the heirs of the recorded tenants filed the aforesaid Rent Suit for realization of arrear rents and apart from this; the kabuliat vide Exhibit-'G' allegedly executed by the predecessor of the petitioner-appellants namely Hasan Ali is a created paper, by which no valid title and interest was accrued in favour of Hasan Ali or his successors. Hasan Ali, who is an admitted lawyer of the local Bar, during his life time realizing the fate of his conduct, admitting the case of the respondents executed a `nadabipatra which shows the malafide of the appellants and the learned trial Judge rightly appraised the actual facts of the case. The alleged kabuliat was also not produced from the side of the petitioner-appellants during pendency of the original miscellaneous case while the Gnadabipatra' dated 09.03.1952 was exhibited and marked as Exhibit-GE'. The learned Advocate submits that the S.A. record of right Exhibit-`D' stands recorded in the names of the predecessor-in-interest of the, respondents which have got its presumptive value of correctness and that matter is properly appreciated by the learned court below and it is apparent from the face of the records that the original owner of the property was the predecessor-in-interest of Syed Ali, Abdul Gofur and Abdul Goni Khan namely Karam All Khan. It is a fact that Karam Ali Khan during his life time declared the property as waqf estate by a waqf deed which has been marked as Exhibit-GA' and the positive contention to that effect that Karam Ali Khan in respect of the case property along with other property comprising an area of 327 bighas of land executed the deed of waqf in the year 1321 A.D. and in the waqf deed vide Exhibit-GA' there exist a clear recital that, during the life time of Karam Ali Khan he will remain as Motowalli of the estate and after his death his two sons namely Syed AIi Khan and Abdul Gofur Khan along with his grandson Abdul Goni Khan would be joint motowalli of the estate which has been proved by sufficient cogent evidence before the learned trial Judge. The learned Advocate after filing a supplementary affidavit submitted B.R.S. khatian No. 525 which stands recorded in the name of the present respondents as n2otowalli of the waqf estate namely 'Karam Ali Khan Waqf Estate' and it has been published during pendency of this case. The learned Advocate lastly submits referring some decisions reported in 34 BLD 463 and 2 SCC 642 that a waqf is a permanent dedication of property and once a waqf always a waqf and the learned trial court rightly after proper sifting of evidence in its true perspective arrived at a conclusive decision that the property being waqf cannot be a property a private individual and it is not proved by any cogent evidence that the appellants acquired any valid right, title, interest and possession in the case property, rather; it is on records that the predecessor of the appellants Md. Masan Ali and after his death the appellants are permissive possessors in the case property who in fact have no legal status or character to declare the property a private property or that the property is not a waqf property. 

 10. Having gone through the case records ii transpires that the original ease was instituted by the heirs of Saleh Ahmed against the order dated 28.05.1998 passed by the Waqf Administrator in respect of the case property under section 50 of the Waqf Ordinance, 1962 in E.C. No. 11050, treating the disputed property waqf property. The learned trial court by the impugned judgment and order dated 26.05.2011 disallowed the miscellaneous case and being aggrieved the petitioners to that case have instituted this appeal and it’s connected Civil Rule No. 656(FM) of 2011. 

 12. Consulting the relevant case records I also find that the waqif Karam Ali Khan by virtue of a deed of waqf declared the suit property along with the other properties comprising total area of 327 bighas of land as waqf. It is also within the recital of Exhibit-'A' that in the deed of waqf Karam Ali Khan was the motowalli of the estate and at the demise of Karam Ali Khan his two sons namely Syed Ali Khan, Abdul Gofur Khan and grandson Abdul Goni Khan were appointed motowallies jointly in respect of the above mentioned properties and it is the case of the appellants that from the sons and grandson of Karam Ali Khan who are the successors of Karam Ali Khan, their predecessor Hasan Ali obtained the case land by way of a settlement for a limited period ended in the year 1950 and a kabuliat was executed by Hasan Ali in favour of Syed Ali Khan and others. It is further case of the appellants that after the expiry of the ending year 1950, the possession was continued by their predecessor Hasan Ali by holding over. It was also contended from the side of the petitioner-appellants that Syed Ali Khan and others for recovery of arrear rents filed a Rent Suit being No.1788/58 against Hasan Ali and when the S.A. khatian was prepared in the name of original owners, Hasan Ali filed a Title Suit challenging the entry of the khatians being Title Suit No.02 of 1972 for declaration of title which was decreed on compromise in terms of `solenama’. 

 14. During trial of the original case apart from documentary evidences the parties to the case examined two witnesses from each side. 

 15. P.W.1 A.B.M. Sadique is the co-petitioner to the original case, who is the full brother of the original plaintiffs. This witness in his testimony testified that he is deposing on behalf of all the petitioners. P.W.1 further testified in his testimony that the owners of the property filed the rent suit against his grandfather Hasan Ali and in that Rent Suit No. 1788 of 1958 the owners of the property recognized Hasan Ali as of their tenant. P.W.1 admits in his testimony that they are not in a position to file any paper relating to the Rent Suit No. 1788 of 1958. lie also testified that against the S.A. record of right the Title Suit .No.02 of 1972 was filed by their grandfather Hasan Ali, which was decreed in terms of `solenama' and his grandfather died on 09.11.1978 leaving behind the original petitioners along with he (P.W.1) and during the life time of Hasan Ali he made an `osiotnama transferring the suit land in favour of the petitioners. 

 18. On the contrary, 0.P.W.1 is the opposite party No.2 Khan Mohammad Rezaul Karim. This witness in his testimony testified in support of the written objection filed by them and corroborated their pleading. 0.P.W.1 categorically testified in his deposition that the original owner of the property was Karam Ali Khan, who executed the deed of waqf on 29.09.1921 which was registered on 02.10.1921 being No. 6864. In the said deed of waqf the waqif Karam Ali Khan was the Motowalli. 0.P.W.1 in his testimony also testified that his predecessor in interest late Abdul Goni Khan who was his father along with other Motowallies did not recognize Hasan Ali as of their tenant and they never realized any rent from Hasan Ali and also did not accept the alleged kabuliat from Hasan Ali and there was no tenancy right of the predecessor of the petitioners and he was asked to handover vacant possession of the case property when the predecessors of this witness came to know about the alleged kabuliat. O.P.W.1 denied the `osiotnama' executed by Hasan Ali and testified specifically that they asked the petitioners to leave the case property. With regard to the `nadabipatra' of Hasan Ali 0.P.W. 1 testified that they have filed the 4nadabipatra' in which Hasan Ali admitted the case of the opposite parties. 

 22. The learned trial court with regard to the evidence adduced from the sides of the respective parties after assessment of the same arrived at a decision that in the evidence of the petitioners it has conic to the notice of the court that they have admitted the case of the opposite parties as to the permissive possession of the petitioners in the case property. I find on meticulous assessment of the evidence on record that the learned District Judge was justified and rightly held that, despite from the side of the petitioners there exist series of rent receipts since 1372 B.S., but inasmuch as they are in possession over the case land as permissive possessors of the opposite parties, the series of rent receipts have got no presumptive value of their title and possession in the case property. 

 23. Having gone through the relevant papers it also appears that the case property has been made waqf property by the Waqif Karam Ali Khan by a registered deed of Waqf in the year 1921 A.D. and within the relevant list of Waqf Administrator of the year 1946 A.D. the suit property has been enlisted. Admittedly the S.A. record of right stands recorded in the names of the legal heirs of Waqif Karam Ali Khan and the heirs of the wag if according to the deed of waqf became motuwallies jointly to look after the property. The learned court below in his observation and findings evaluating the connected documents, conclusively held that the kabuliat as alleged from the side of the petitioners and the filing of so called Rent Suit No.1788 of 1958 and the subsequent sole decree obtained in Title Suit No. 02 of 1972, which are under challenge have got no legal footings, inasmuch as; by way of registered waqf deed of the year 1921 the property has became waqf property and in this context; the learned Advocate on behalf of the opposite parties rightly cited the decision reported in 2 SCC 642. In the Case of Sayyed Ali and others —vs.- A.P. wakf Board, Hyderabad and others, their lordships held that, "a waqf is a permanent dedication of property for purposes recognized by Muslim law as pious, religious or charitable and property having been found as waqf would always retain its character as a waqf In other words, once a waqf always a waqf and the grant of patta in favour of Mokhasadar under the Mums Act does not, in any mariner, nullify the earlier dedication made of the property constituting the same as wave; After a waqf has been created, it continues to be so for all time to come and further continues to be governed by the provisions of the waqf Act and a grant of patta in favour of Mokhasadar does not affect the original character of the waqf property. " 

 25. Therefore, this documentary evidence itself shows that the appellants frankly admitted that the case property is a waqf property under Karam Ali Khan waqf estate. Furthermore, the above mentioned Rent Suit was not filed by all the Moluwallies or their successors-in-interest. Besides this; the Rent Suit was instituted admittedly after the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. It further appears from the case records that the specific case of the present respondents as to the nature and character of the case land there lies a document. The predecessor-in-interest of the present appellants Md. Hasan Ali executed a 'nadabipatra' on 09.03.1952 vide Exhibit-`E, in which Hasan Ali acknowledged that he has got no right, title, interest in the case property and he was allowed to stay in the case land temporarily. The witness in whose presence, Hasan Ali executed the nadabipatra' has been examined from the side of the respondents as O.P.W.2, who was a witness of that deed (Exhibit-`E'). This witness in his testimony identified his signature as well as the `nadabipatra'. 

 28. On perusal of the deed of waqf vide Exhibit-'A' dated 29.09.1921 it is noticed that within the contents of the deed there is a clear mention from the side of the Waqif Karam Ali Khan that the Motuwallies are not entitled to change any of the terms and conditions of the said deed and according to the terms and conditions of the deed of waqf, the purported kabuliat dated 31.10.1939 (Exhibit-`G') cannot create any right or title in favour of Hasan Ali. From the plain reading of the contents of Exhibit-`A' it is evident that, nobody is empowered to change the nature and character of the property which has made waqf through the waqif by this registered instrument. The learned court below with regard to this rightly observed in the impugned judgment and order that the nature and character of the property remain as before and because of that, the Waqif Administrator consulting the connected documents rightly issued the Notice-in-dispute with regard to the eviction of the petitioner-appellants from the case property. 

 29. The fact remains in view of the schedule Condition No .3 of the deed of waqf and section 56 & 80 of the Waqf Ordinance, 1962 that the case land being a waqf property cannot be transferred or alienated by any means and the alleged act of compromise in the Title Suit No.02 of 1972 cannot be treated legal and proper. It is found that the motowallies are also without jurisdiction without prior approval of the waqf Administrator to enter into any compromise in respect of the case property. The connected S.A. Khatian vide Exhibit-'D' which stands recorded in the names of the predecessor-in-interest of the respondents have got a presumptive value of correctness as it is not rebutted by any' tangible evidence and that there is nothing on record to hold that the khatian was prepared wrongly. From the record of Waqf Administrator with regard to the nature and character of the case land it transpires that an enquiry was held and there is a report to that effect dated 17.12.1996 and from the contents of that report it is crystal clear that the enquiry officer during his local enquiry clearly observed that the suit property' is a waqf property and there is no existence of any valid document showing transfer of the case property in favour of 3rd party. Furthermore, under section 56(1) of the Waqf Ordinance, 1962 there is no such approval or permission by which the alleged transfer or alienation was done.

Versus
Haider Ali being dead his heirs;

full_judgment:
3. Facts necessary to dispose this petition are that the predecessor-in-interest of respondent Nos.l-4 as the plaintiff filed Title Suit No.21 of 1989, in the Court of the then Subordinate Judge (now- the joint Distract judge), 2nd Court, Dhaka for declaration that the exparte decree dated 18.12.1986 passed in Title Suit No.208 of 1986 of the Court of Assistant Judge, Additional Court, Dhaka was illegal, fraudulent, collusive without any legal effect and not applicable to him and for partition of the suit land. The plaintiff claimed saham to the extent of .52 acre land. 

 4. The suit was contested by defendant Nos.1, 3-11, 16-32 and 51-54 by filing separate sets of written statement. This suit (Title Suit No.21 of 1989) was heard analogously with Title Suit No.467 of 1990 (original numbers were 87 of 1984 and 208 of 1986) filed by Momin Mia. 

 6. The learned Joint District Judge by his judgment and decree dated 24.02.2004 decreed, Title Suit No.21 of 1989 in preliminary form giving saham to the plaintiff to the extent of .52 acre land but dismissed Title Suit No.467 of 1990. 

 7. Against the judgment and decree of the learned Joint District Judge passed in Title Suit No.21 of 1989, the defendants filed Title Appeal No.132 of 2004 befdre the District Judge, Dhaka and the plaintiff of Title Suit No.467 of 1990, filed Title Appeal No.133 of 2004. Both the appeals were heard analogously by the learned Additional District Judge, Sixth Court, Dhaka and he by a common judgment dated 04.06.2006 (separate decrees were drawn and signed) dismissed Title Appeal No.133 of 2004 and allowed Title Appeal No.132 of 2004 and modified the decree of the trial Court. The Appellate Court maintained the saham given by the trial Court and at the same time gave separate saham to the contesting defendants to the extent of 681/2 decimals land with the direction that saham shall be given to the parties on the basis of the priority of the deeds and maintaining their possession (in Bangla it has been stated as “দলিল সমূহ অগ্রাধিকারের ভিত্তিতে স্বত্ব দখল বজায় রেখে পক্ষগন ছাহাম প্রাপক হবে।”) 

 9. Heard Mr. Md. Osman Ghani, learned Advocate for the petitioners and Mr. Mahbubey Alam, learned Advocate who entered caveat on behalf of respondent Nos.l-4 (they are the legal heirs of the original plaintiff), perused the judgments and decrees of the Courts below and the impugned judgment and order.

parties:
Bank Asia Limited ----- Appellant
Vs. 
Industrial Promotion and Development Company of Bangladesh (IPDC) ----- Respondent
full_judgment:
28. The IPDC in their written objection in paragraph no.30 admitted that "in breach of the loan agreement and the undertaking the opposite party No.2 failed to execute/or produce the following security documents (a) a joint and several equitable mortgage in favour of the opposite party No.1 (IPDC) ranking pari passu over the opposite party No.2's immovable property by the deposit of the title deeds, the relative memorandum of deposit, a right to call for a legal mortgage" and after such admission the instant miscellaneous case No.20 of 2013 ought to have been allowed straight way but the learned court below without taking such admission into consideration rejected the miscellaneous case most illegally and arbitrarily. 

 29. It is stated that 16.50 decimals of land out of 24 decimals of attached land was under registered mortgage in favour of the appellant Bank by dint of Mortgage deed No.8036 dated 19.06.2003, that a registered power of attorney deed No.8037 dated 19.06.2003 was also executed in favour of the appellant bank and all the documents of title was also deposited and is still under the custody of the instant appellant and there is no security sharing or pari passu agreement between Bank Asia Ltd. and IPDC and the respondent No.2 did not execute any registered or equitable mortgage in favour of IPDC and therefore for all practical purposes the appellant has paramount right over their mortgaged property which cannot be circumvent in any manner. 

 30. It is stated that the reference of the title deed being No.22297 dated 15 February, 1968 which respondent No.1 IPDC has given in their plaint is not the title deed of respondent No.2 rather the vendor of the said deed is Bilkis Begum. 

 37. The learned Advocate for the appellant next submits that while passing the impugned judgment and order the learned court failed to consider that Bank Asia Ltd. i.e. the present appellant is also a decree holder against the same set of judgment debtors and said Bank Asia Ltd. have in their favour registered mortgage deed and power of attorney deed over 16.50 decimals of land out of 24 decimals of attached land and the original documents of title are still kept at the disposal of the appellant, that Bank Asia Ltd. obtained the judgment and decree on 31.05.2009 (decree singed on 03.06.2009) from Judge, Artha Rin Adalat No.2, Dhaka, whereas IPDC i.e. (opposite party) respondent No.1 subsequently obtained decree in their favour on 15.07.2010 (decree signed on 18.07.2010) from Artha Rin Adalat No.3, Dhaka without disturbing the decree of Artha Rin Suit No.75 of 2005 and therefore the right of the petitioner appellant over the mortgaged land cannot be curtailed at the instance of another decree holder who has no valid charge over the said property. 

 38. The learned Advocate for the appellant also submits that in support of their so called claim of equitable mortgage IPDC i.e. respondent No.1 failed to produce the title deeds of the land in question or any memorandum of deposit of title deeds and therefore the observation of the learned Court below in the judgment of the Artha Rin Suit No.78 of 2010, treating the land in question as under equitable mortgage in favour of IPDC is based on no evidence and the said observation is without jurisdiction which can not stand on the way of granting relief to the appellant. 

 a). A joint and several equitable mortgages in favour of the IPDC ranking pari-passu over the BGFL's immovable property by the deposit of the title deeds, the relative memorandum of deposit, a right to call for legal mortgage. 

 80. IPDC failed to show any registered or equitable mortgage in its favour; moreover, the documents of title was not in their custody. In para-30 of their plaint they have admitted that there is no equitable mortgage and they do not have the title documents. 

 83. Even in its application for attachment IPDC gave wrong description of the title deed of the property to be attached. 

 96. In the case of Subha Karam and others Vs. State Bank of Pak. and ors. Transfer of Property Act (IV of 1882) Sec.58(f) "Equitable mortgage by deposit of title deeds—Ingredients which have to be established—No such mortgage is created with mere deposit of title deeds for advances to be made in future." 

 103. Impugned judgment and order dated 15.04.2014 passed by the learned Judge, Artha Rin Adalat No.3, Dhaka in Miscellaneous Case No.20 of 2013 arising out of Artha Execution Case No.156 of 2010 in disallowing the miscellaneous Case filed under Order XXI Rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure read with section 32 and 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 is hereby set aside. Consequently Miscellaneous Case No.20 of 2003 arising out of Artha Execution Case No. 156 of 2010 read with section 32 and 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 is hereby allowed. The connected Civil Rule 594(FM) of 2014 is hereby made absolute. The schedule property of the appellant to the extent of 16.50 decimals of land which includes all the structures standing thereon mentioned in their application filed under Order 21 Rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure be excluded from the schedule No.1 of the Title Execution Case No.156 of 2010 pending before the Artha Rin Adalat, 3rd Court, Dhaka filed by the respondent IPDC. The Execution Case shall proceed as usual in respect of other properties mentioned in the schedule of the said execution case.

parties:
Fatema Khatun ----- Defendant-Petitioner
VS
Maszid-E-Fattah (Tablig Markas Maszid) ----- Plaintiff-Opposite-Party
full_judgment:
