3. The sole defendant contested the suit by filing written statement denying the material allegations contending, inter-alia, that the suit is not maintainable in its present form and manner. The suit is barred by limitation and bad for defect of the parties. Further case of the defendant is that she is a tenant under Mohammad Modasser Hossain. Initial rent of the premises was Taka 35 and thereafter it was enhanced to Taka 200. The defendant has been depositing rent before the Court of Premises Rent Controller since 1989 and Mohammad Modasser Hossain has been withdrawing the same regularly. The landlord illegally tried to evict the defendant and then the defendant filed Title Suit No. 28 of 1991 for permanent injunction which was decreed ex parte. The defendant is not a defaulter and she did not receive any notice under section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act. The plaintiff has no bonafide requirement of the suit premises. At the request of the landlord, defendant constructed safety tank and tin shed toilet in the suit land and made some repair of the structures therein by expending Taka 2 lacs but the plaintiff did not adjust the same in spite of promise. Defendant has been residing in the suit land since 1965. Plaintiff's suit is false and manufactured one, as such, liable to be dismissed with cost. 

 7. Mr Mustaq Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party submits that the petitioner was inducted in the suit premises by the original owner Mohammad Modasser Hossain. The petitioner had been paying rent to the said original owner of the property but at a point of time she started depositing rent in the Court of Rent Controller by filing a House Rent Control Case No. 127 of 1989. The said Mohammad Modasser Hossain and his two daughters namely, Taslima Banu and Selima Banu by a deed of waqf dated 25-8-2002 transferred the property to the Maszid-E-Fattah, Khulna. After execution and registration of the waqf deed the said Mohammad Modasser Hossain as well as the Maszid Committee informed the petitioner about the waqf and advised him to pay the rent to the Maszid Committee but the petitioner instead of making payment of rent to the opposite party continued to deposit the same with the rent Controller in the name of Mohammd Modasser Hosain and thereafter, in the name of his three daughters. 

 13. Now the question has come whether by depositing the rent with the Rent Controller in favour of original owner the petitioner can safe herself from the definition and or disrepute of defaulter. It appears that the petitioner was informed about the change of the ownership of the property by way of oral communication, thereafter, by a suit filed earlier in the year 2008 by the opposite party and finally by notice to quit but in spite of knowing fully well about transfer of ownership the petitioner continued to deposit the rent in the name of original owner who had no title in the property. To appreciate the knowledge of the petitioner about the transfer of the property to the opposite party the relevant portion of reply made by DW 1 in his cross-examination may be looked into which runs thus: 

 14. From the above statement, it is established that the petitioner had knowledge about the transfer of the property to the opposite party. Apart from this the petitioner also had knowledge from the plaint in Title Suit No. 1563 of 2008 and, thereafter, from the notice under section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act. In the situation, the petitioner was under obligation to make payment of rent to the opposite party but instead of doing so the petitioner purposely continued to deposit the rent with the Rent Controller in the name of original owner making herself a worst type of defaulter. There is no earthly reason to believe from the aforesaid circumstances that the petitioner was not informed about the transfer of the property to the opposite party. 

 15. The present defendant-petitioner was a monthly tenant under the original owner Mohammed Modasser Hossain who is not legally competent to receive the rent after execution of deed of waqf. Whenever a notice under section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act is served upon the tenant to vacate the premises, the tenant only has protection of law if she is not a defaulter. In the present case, apart from bonafide requirement of the premises by the opposite party, the petitioner is a defaulter. A defaulter tenant cannot seek protection of law under the premises Rent Control Act. The petitioner having failed to pay the rent to the opposite party after transfer of the property by the original landlord, she has become a defaulter and, as such, the judgment and decree passed by the trial court decreeing the suit for eviction of the petitioner calls no interference of this Court.

parties:
Md. Nachir Uddin and others
Vs.
Deputy Commissioner, Tangail and other
full_judgment:
Md. Rais Uddin, J: This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party No.1 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 18.9.2008 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Tangail in Title Appeal No.22 of 2006 dismissed the appeal and affirmed those dated 23.2.2006 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Madhupur, Tangail in O.C. Suit No.111 of 2002 dismissed the suit, should not be set-aside. 

 2. The relevant fact giving rise to this Rule, in short, is that the petitioners as plaintiffs instituted a suit praying for permanent injunction contending, inter-alia, that the original owner of suit land was Ananta Baishnabi, Kedernath Karmakar and Loknath Karmakar who sold the suit land to Join Uddin Q Joinal Abedin and handedover the possession of the suit land to Joyenuddin and thereafter several transfers were made through kabala deeds and ultimately the predecessors of plaintiff No.1-3 Nurul Islam became the owner of the suit land who died leaving behind plaintiff Nos.1-3 as his heirs. One Mokter Hossain became the owner of the 9 decimals of suit land died leaving behind plaintiff No.4-8 as his heirs and thereby the plaintiffs filed the suit praying for permanent injunction against the defendants who are given threat to disposes the present petitioners from the suit land wherein the present petitioners have been possessing the suit land by constructing dwelling but and living there in and some houses have been possessing by giving rent to the tenants. 

 3. The defendants contested the suit by filing joint written statements denying material allegations made in the plaint contending, inter-alia, that the suit land was acquired by the Road and High ways in the year 1940 and it was published in Gazette and prepared L.A. map. The suit land had no possession, right, title of any others except the Road and High ways. The defendants further slated that no notice was served upon the plaintiffs for demolitions their establishment and on 2.11.2002 there was announcement through mike from the authority of Road and High ways to demolish of illegal establishment from the Government land. 

 7. Mr. Mohammad Ali, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners has placed the Revisional Application, pleadings, evidence, judgment and decree of the courts below and other materials on record before this court and submits that the trial court failed to discuss the evidence of the plaintiffs and the defendants, moreover in his finding found the possession of the plaintiffs. He submits that the appellate court on discussion of the evidence both oral and documentary in his finding found the possession and prima facie title of the plaintiffs but dismissed the appeal on misconception of law, fact and circumstances of the case on the ground that the suit land is not specified by mentioning boundary in the schedule of the plaint which is not sustainable in law. He lastly submits that finding and observation of the courts below are not based on evidence and materials on record and as such judgment and decree of the courts below are not sustainable in law and he prayed for to make the rule absolute and set aside the judgment and decree of the courts below. 

 9. Mr. Swapan Kumar Das, the learned Assistant Attorney-General appearing for the Opposite-parties opposed the rule and submits that the plaintiffs failed to prove their title by producing original deed. He submits that in the Suit there are 8 plaintiffs with separate holding has not been mentioned in the plaint. He submits that plaintiffs filed S.A. Khatian but failed to submit any deed in support of their, Khatian which is not acceptable and sustainable in law. He submits that in the plaint there is no specification of the boundary under Order VII rule 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure. He further submits that the plaintiffs failed to make any statement in the plaint about the original via deed. He lastly submits that concurrent finding of facts reached by the courts below and there is no misreading and non-consideration of the evidence and as such there is no reason to interfere by this court in revision and he prayed for discharged the rule. 

 17. In a suit for permanent injunction the plaintiffs shall have to prove their exclusive possession in the suit land in order to get decree. The court may incidentally enquired into prima facie title of the parties and the court need not enter into disputed title unless the possession of the plaintiffs is clearly established by evidences of the plaintiffs. The courts below have dealt mainly on the point of title of the plaintiffs which should not have been the consideration in a suit for permanent injunction. The findings of the courts as to possession of the suit land on the basis of evidence on record. 

 18. In the instant case both the courts below concurrently found exclusive possession of the plaintiffs but the trial court observed that the plaintiffs failed to prove their title in the suit land. The learned Judge of the appellate court found possession as well as prima facie title of the plaintiffs with the finding- 

 "The suit for permanent injunction is essentially a suit for possession. Though the title may be incidentally gone into but in a suit for permanent injunction the Court need not enter into disputed question of title except to the extent as it would help in finding which of the parties have possession. The plaintiff could not bring home their possession in the suit land for a decree for a permanent injunction." 

 "All the Courts below have considered the legality or otherwise of the award by which the plaintiffs claim title to the suit land but without considering the evidence on record as to possession both the trial court and the Court and the Court of appeal below decreed the suit for permanent injunction. The High Court Division as well without considering the evidence as to possession dismissed the suit for permanent injunction. The suit being a suit for permanent injunction in which the question of title may be gone into incidentally but decision of title in a suit for permanent injunction ought not to have been the guiding principle. The Court cannot disentitle the plaintiff of a decree for permanent injunction if he can prove possession and in thin view the plaintiff could not be evicted with force if continues to be in possession unless in due process of law and could exercise his right of possession restraining everybody including the real owners. In a suit for permanent injunction the Court need not enter into disputed title except to the extent that it would help the Court in finding which of the parties have prima facie title and exclusive possession. 

 "Although the S.A. Khatian stood in the name of Hasina Jamil but the S.A. Khatian cannot confer any title in respect of any landed property to anybody. The learned Judge Found that the suit property as per schedule of the plaint is 1.29 acres of land which appertains to plot No.38 of C.S. Khatian No. 179 but unfortunately, the said property was not found in C.S. Khatian No. 179. The learned Judge also found from Ext. I the sale deed normally registered on 30.3.1939 and he purchased the property of C.S. plot No.28 and not C.S. Plot No.38 of S.A. Khatian No.179. Accordingly the learned Judge dismissed the suit and affirmed the judgment and decree of the trial court, upon a reading of C.S. Khatian Ext. 3(a) not Ext. 3 as the learned Judge referred the C.S. Khatian No.179 and the hal khatian No. 422, dag As stated as 38 but quantity of land measured 1.29 acres of land was sold. The learned Judge termed the discrepancy as simple anomaly." 

 28. In the instant case both the courts below found the possession of the plaintiffs and the appellate court also found the prima facie title of the plaintiffs but dismissed the appeal on the ground that the suit land is not specified in the boundary which is misinterpretation and misconception of law as stated above. The plaintiffs having complied with the mandatory requirement of law in giving description by numbers and boundaries is quite identifiable and not vague and as such suit property can be identified by boundaries and numbers. The appellate court on misconception of law and misinterpretation of the schedule of the plaint arrived at the wrong decision which are not sustainable.

parties:
Md. Nazimuddin Majhi ----- Defendant-Pre-emptee appellant-Petitioner
Versus
Md. Taizul Huq and another ----- Plaintiff-Pre-emptor-respondent Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
Mr. Soumendra Sarker, J:- The Rule issued calling upon the Opposite Party No. to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 21.01.2007 passed by the learned Joint District Judge,' Additional court, Gazipur in Title Appeal No. 108 of 2002 disallowing the appeal affirming the judgment and decree dated 29.07.2002 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, 3"I Court, Gazipur in Title Suit No.36 of 2001 should not be set-aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus, the present opposite party No. I instituted the original suit before 3d Court of learned Assistant Judge, Gazipur for preemption (Wu) under Mahomedan Law contending inter Witt that the case land originally belonged to one Akter uddin and the corresponding S.A. and R.S. khatian was prepared in his name. Akter Uddin died leaving behind two sons namely Md. Taizul Haq who is the plaintiff of the suit and one Abdul Miah. Akter Uddin had also a daughter namely Jahanara Begum and all of them inherited the property. The plaintiff and the defendant no.2 Jahanara Begum are step brother and sister. On 01.08.2001 the -defendant No.1 coming to the suit land started to demarcate the some by survey. Finding that; the plaintiff asked him the cause of such demarcation and from the reply of the defendant No.1 the plaintiff came to learn that he (defendant No.1) has purchased 4(four) decimals of land from the defendant No.2. The plaintiff made a protest and resisted the defendants and observed the formalities of "sufa "(pre-emption). After citing the certified copy of the kabla on 10.05.2001 the plaintiff filed the original suit for getting the suit land pre-empted under Mahomedan Law. The case of the plaintiff is such that he has observed "Man-E-Ishad " and "Talab-E-Muashabotl. The -purchaser defendant No.1 is a stranger to the suit land and he has no adjacent land. 

 3. The contrary case of the contesting defendant No. I in short is thus that the defendant No.1 is a co-sharer of the suit land and while the defendant No.2 proposed to sell the land within the knowledge of all the defendant No.1 agreed and thereafter purchased the property on 07.01.2001 by a registered kabla deed being No.188 within the knowledge of the plaintiff. After purchasing the land the purchaser-defendant No.1 developed the land at a cost of Taka 3,000/- by cutting earth and at a cost of Taka 2,500/- for making a canal. The further case of the defendant No.1 is such that the plaintiff before filing of the suit not at all complied with the mandatory provisions of law which is "Talab-E-Ishad " and "Taint,- E-Muashabad" and as a result of that he is not entitled to get the land pre-empted. 

 4. The learned trial court during trial after examining the witnesses decreed the suit on contest by his judgment and decree dated 29.07.2002 and 04.08.2002 respectively. Being aggrieved the defendant No.1 preferred an appeal being Title Appeal No.1 08 of 2002 in the Court of learned District Judge. Gazipur which was heard and disposed of by the learned Joint District Judge, Additional Court, Gazipur. The learned appellate court by the impugned judgment and decree dated 21.01.2007 and 27.01.2007 respectively disallowed the appeal affirming the judgment and decree passed by the trial court. 

 7. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the trial court as well as the appellate court committed gross illegality and irregularity in passing the judgment and decree in favour of the plaintiff-opposite party. The learned Advocate further submits that neither the trial court, nor the appellate court properly assessed the evidence on record in its true perspective and failed to arrive at a correct decision as to the merit of the case. In fact; the plaintiff-opposite party during trial was hopelessly failed to prove the required formalities of getting pre-emption under Mahomedan Law. There is no cogent evidence to prove the formalities which are required to be observed strictly. The learned Advocate also submits that the witnesses adduced from the side of the plaintiffs not at all proved the case of the plaintiff-opposite parties and the required number of witnesses as contemplated in section 236 of Mahomedan Law is totally absent at the time of alleged formalities. Without strict compliance of "Talab-E-Lshad"and Milab-E7Mlitishabad" no body is entitled to get an order of pre-emption under the ambit of Mahomedan Law. The learned Advocate submits that in the plaint the plaintiff also failed to state about the number of witnesses and the fact of observance of the mandatory formalities. The learned courts below are totally misconceived in appreciating the 

 actual position of law and there has been gross misreading and non-reading of evidence as well as non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The witnesses No. 2 and 3 who are examined from the side of the plaintiff in support of his case are quite silent about the date of alleged "Talab-E-Ishad". From the testimony of these two witnesses it would be clear that they were only present at the time of first formality of the date on 08.01.2001 but they were not present at the time of second formality of 10.05.2001. Therefore, obviously the mandatory formalities not proved. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the courts below on surmise and conjecture without proper analysis of evidence arrived at an erroneous view that the formalities were duly observed which is an illegality on the face of the record. Besides this; in the pleadings of the plaintiff there is nd mention of the name of any witness those who were allegedly present at the time of "Talb-E-lshad " and "Talab-E-Muashabad". The learned Advocate in support of his argument referred three decisions or this sub-continent and relying upon the decisions in consultation with the evidence on records argued that in order to get decree for pre-emption (sofa) under the Mahomedan Law as because the mandatory formalities were not observed properly the plaintiff is not entitled, to get the relief as prayed for. Furthermore; the relief is barred by the law of limitation. The duration of observance of the two formalities as provided in section 236 of the Mahomedan Law inasmuch as not complied with, due to that long laps of time between "Talab-E-Ishad " and "Talab-E-Muashabad " the suit is time barred, but the learned trial court as well as the appellate court by-passing the said duration decreed the suit illegally. 

 8. As against the aforesaid submissions the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite party opposing the Rule submits that the trial court as well as the appellate court during disposal of the original suit and its subsequent appeal committed no illegality or irregularity. 'Admittedly; the petitioner is a co-sharer by inheritance in the suit land and knowing about the purchase of suit land by the purchaser-defendant No.1 from the defendant No.2 who is the step-sister of the plaintiff, the plaintiff specifically expressed his desire to pre-empt the case land. Subsequently, without any delay getting certified copy of the case kabla the plaintiff has complied with the mandatory formally of "Talab-E-Ishad ". The learned Advocate further submits that the courts below during disposal of the suit and its subsequent appeal rightly assessed the evidence on records and arrived at a correct view that the legal formalities as required under law has been duly complied with by the plaintiff and there is no legal embargo in getting the land pre-empted under the purview of Mahomedan Law under section 236. The learned Advocate further submits that in the suit there is no limitation as within. one year which is prescribed in the relevant law from the date of case kabla the plaintiff instituted the original suit. The learned Advocate lastly submits that in support of the plaintiffs case plaintiff examined three witnesses and all the witnesses corroborated the pleadings of the plaintiff which is properly appreciated by the courts below concurrently. Both the courts in their judgment and decree held that the plaintiff-opposite party proved his case by sufficient credible evidence and the requirement of law has been fulfilled. There is nothing to interfere with the impugned judgment and decree for want of misreading and non-reading of evidence and non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. 

 10. On perusal of the case record it transpires that the plaintiff to the suit in order to get the case land pre-empted instituted the original suit being Title Suit No. 36 of 2001 under the ambit of Mahomedan Law. It has been contended from the side of the plaintiff that he is a co-sharer by inheritance in the suit jote and the defendant No.1 who is the kabla purchaser, purchased the case land behind the back of the plaintiff. For the first time the plaintiff came to learn on 08.01.2001 while the defendant No.1 coming to the suit land tried to demarcate the land by surveyor. The plaintiff knowing about that purchase instantly observed the first formality - "Talab-E-Muashabad" as required under Mahomedan Law on the very date in presence of several persons. Within the pleadings of the plaintiff it was further contended that subsequent to that knowledge the plaintiff coming to Kapasia Sub-registry office on 18.05.2001 obtained the certified copy of the case kabla dated 07.01.2001. Thereafter, taking _ the certified copy the plaintiff observed the second formality "Talab-Elshad" as provided in section 236 of the Muslim Law. 

 11. Vis-a-vis; the contention given from the side of the defendant No. I in his pleadings is such that the purchaser defendant No. 1 is also a co-sharer in the suit land and within the knowledge of the plaintiff he 'purchased the land on 07.01.2001. Prior to that the vendor defendant No.2 proposed the plaintiff to purchase the land but at his refusal the defendant No.1 purchased. The further case as it appears from the pleadings of the contesting defendant-petitioner is such that the plaintiff before filing of the original suit; not at all complied with the mandatory, formalities of law in presence of required number of witnesses. 

 12. The learned appellate court with regard r to the respective cases of the parties arrived at a decision in the impugned judgment and decree that the plaintiff during trial of the original suit was able to discharge his onus in proving his case and the learned trial court assessing the evidence on records rightly held that the legal requirements inasmuch as were fulfilled by the plaintiff he is entitled to have a decree for getting the land pre-empted under Mahomedan Law. 

 13. Having gone through the impugned judgment and decree I have come across that the learned lower appellate court in disallowing the appeal and affirming the, judgment and decree passed by the trial court did not analyze the evidence led from the sides of the respective parties. Relying upon the discussions and findings of the trial court the appellate court decided that the plaintiff is entitled to get the relief oh prayed for since he has proved his case by corroborative evidence. In this context; the argument advanced from the side of the learned counsel for the petitioner is required to be adjudicated in consultation with the evidence on records. 

 "236. Demands for pre-emption:- No person is entitled to the right of pre-emption unless- 

 15. Having regard to the facts, circumstance and evidence adduced from the sides of the respective parties I have the reason to inclined such a view that the learned appellate court below without compliance of the mandatory provisions of law as contemplated in Order XLI Rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure disallowed the appeal affirming the judgment and decree passed by the trial court. Furthermore; as I have already discussed earlier that the mandatory formalities and observance of those as required under law inasmuch as not proved at all the right of pre-emption under Mahomedan Law cannot be exercised. In order to get a decree of pre-emption under the Mahomedan Law at the very outset the mandatory formalities is required to be strictly followed. Therefore; it is apparent from the face of the records that the proposition of law is not properly appreciated as well as followed by the courts below during disposal of the original suit and its subsequent appeal. 

 17. In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs. The impugned judgment and decree dated 21.01.2007 passed by the learned Joint District Judge. Additional court, Gazipur in Title Appeal No.108 of 2002 disallowing the appeal affirming the judgment and decree dated 29.07.2002 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, 3rd  Court, Gazipur in Title Suit No.36 of 2001 is hereby set aside. 

 18. The original suit be also dismissed on contest as not proved.

parties:
Sadhan Bala Dey ------ Plaintiff-Appellant-Petitioner
vs
Ratri Bala Dey and other ------ Defendant- Respondent-Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
The Rule issued calling upon the opposite party Nos. 1-4 to show cause as to why the Order No. 12 dated 11-1-2011 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Noakhali, in Title Appeal No. 104 of 2009 rejecting the application for amendment of the plaint under Order VI, rule 17 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure should not be set aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus, the present petitioner as plaintiff instituted the original declaratory Suit being Title Suit No. 158 of 2006 in the Court of learned Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Noakhali for a declaration that the registered deed of gift being No. 13681 dated 12-8-1985 executed by one Ashwini Kumar Dey, the predecessor of the defendant Nos. 1-4 in favour of the defendant No. 1 Ratri Bala Dey is false, fraudulent, inoperative and not binding upon the plaintiff in respect of the land described in schedule-'ka' of the plaint. The learned trial court during trial after taking evidence from the sides of the respective parties dismissed the suit on contest by its judgment and decree dated 30-9-2009 and 7-10-2009 respectively. 

 3. Being aggrieved the plaintiff preferred an appeal being Title Appeal No. 104 of 2009 in the court of learned District Judge, Noakhali. The appeal was transmitted to the 2'd Court of learned Additional District Judge, Noakhali and the lower appellate court while fixed a date for hearing of the appeal the plaintiff-appellant on 11-1-2011 filed an application for amendment of the plaint under Order VI, rule 17 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The learned lower appellate court hearing the application for amendment of the plaint rejected the same by the impugned order dated 11-1-2011. 

 8. On perusal of the papers it transpires that the learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Noakhali after getting the application for amendment of the plaint on 11-1-2011 which was fixed for hearing of the Title Appeal being No. 104 of 2009 held that the proposed amendment will change the nature and character of the suit and as a result of that he rejected the application filed under Order VI, rule 17 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 11. In the facts and circumstance of the case having gone through the application for amendment of the plaint I find that the plaintiff-appellant within the contents of the application spelt out some reasonable as well as bonafide reasons as to why he could not bring such amendment earlier. Furthermore, it is clearly inserted within the body of the application that during pendency of the suit the plaintiff have been dispossessed from some portion of the suit land by the defendant No. 1 and as a result of which an additional relief with regard to declaration of title and recovery of khash possession (as sought for by the plaintiff-petitioner) is necessary. The plaintiff had no other alternative but to amend his plaint. Obviously, the application for amendment is exhaustive and there is a detail description of the deeds which has been challenged from the side of the plaintiff and the fact remains that the said amendment in no way change the nature and character of the original suit rather; in absence of this amendment determination on the real question in controversy between the parties would be difficult. 

 14. In the result, the Rule is made absolute with a cost of Taka 1,000 (one thousand) only payable in favour of the contesting defendants. The impugned Order No. 12 dated 11-1-2011 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Noakhali, in Title Appeal No. 104 of 2009 is hereby set-aside.

parties:
Badsha Mollah being dead his heirs: 1(a) Meher Banu, wife of late Badsha Mollah and others
Vs.
The Chairman, First Court of Settlement, Segunbagicha, Police Station- Ramna, District- Dhaka & another
full_judgment:
2. Facts in short, are that, the original Petitioner Badsha Mollah entered into an agreement on 2.5.1976 for purchase of house No. 122, Mohammadpur Colony, Block-D, Shershah Suri Road, Mohammadpur House Estate, Police Station-Tejgoan, at present Mohammadpur, District Dhaka with its owner Md. Ishaque, son of Late Gasit Khalifa who acquired the ownership of the said house on the basis of the allotment as per Memo. No. 490 (150)- Relf/1, dated 30.01.1957 issued by the Additional District Magistrate, Dhaka on 31.01.1957. The original allotment letter having been lost the Petitioner obtained an attested copy of the same from the Ministry of Works. It was stipulated in the Deed of Agreement dated 2.5.1976 executed in between the Petitioner and Md. Ishaque that he would deliver physical possession of the house in question to the Petitioner on the date of agreement on payment of Taka 10,000.00 (Taka ten thousand) as advance out of total consideration of Taka 15,000.00 (Taka fifteen thousand) and the remaining balance of Taka 5,000.00 (Taka five thousand) of the consideration would be paid at the time of execution of the Sale Deed by Md. Ishaque in favour of the Petitioner within a period of three months from the date of knowledge of the procurement of the necessary papers by the owner Md. Ishaque. It is also stated that the original deed of agreement was filed before the Deputy Commissioner, Settlement, Ministry of Works as per Memo. No. 4440/DCS, dated 18.6.1976 issued by the Assistant Commissioner, Settlement. According to the terms of the deed of agreement for sale (Annexure-C), the Petitioner paid Taka 10,000.00 (Taka ten thousand) to the said Md. Ishaque on 2.5.1976 and obtained physical possession of the house in question from him and since then the Petitioner has been living in the said house with the members of his family without any objection from any quarter. Md. Ishaque was an employee of the Pubali Bank Limited till his death on 24.11.1988. The said Md. Ishaque approached the Petitioner for further advance of the consideration money to meet the expenses for procuring the necessary papers required for registration of the Sale Deed in question and the Petitioner gave a sum of Taka 4,400/- (Taka four thousand and four hundred) to said Md. Ishaque who received the said money by granting a separate receipt on 30.1.1977 and promised that he would complete the sale transaction within the shortest possible time. But Md. Ishaque failed to keep his words and delayed the execution and registration of the sale deed after receiving the balance of the consideration money. The Petitioner was compelled to file Title Suit No. 83 of 1977 against Mohammad Ishaque impleading the Government of Bangladesh represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka and the Secretary, Ministry of Works, Govt. of Bangladesh. The Suit was decreed ex parte on 27.1.1978 against the defendants in favour of the Petitioner as the defendants did not contest the suit. On the basis of the said decree a sale deed was executed and registered in favour of the Petitioner by the Court on 8.6.1978. Thereafter, the Petitioner mutated his name in the record of right and paid all Government dues and Municipal taxes as well. The Petitioner then applied to the Deputy Commissioner, Settlement under Ministry of Works requesting him to mutate the name of the Petitioner enclosing all the relevant documents. Having obtained no response from the Deputy Commissioner, Settlement, the Petitioner apprehending that the property in question might be included in the list of abandoned properties, filed Title Suit No. 1019 of 1981 before the 4th Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka against Government officials and consequently, the same was also deemed ex parte in favour of the Petitioner on 28.2.1983. Subsequently the defendant Nos. 1-3 filed a Miscellaneous Case being No. 50 of 1986 for setting aside the said ex pane decree. In the said case Md. Ishaque, defendant No.4 in the suit, appeared and filed written objection stating that he has no interest in the property as the Petitioner got Sale Deed executed and registered through court. The said Miscellaneous Case was dismissed and after a long lapse of time the Petitioner came to know that the property in question has been enlisted in the "Ka" List in the Gazette published on 28.4.1986 as abandoned property. Thereafter, the said gazette notification was cancelled and a new Gazette was published on 23.9.1986. Thereafter the Petitioner filed Case No. 87 of 1988 before the Court of Settlement in which one Shafi Ahmed filed an application disclosing that the property in question was sold out by Md. Ishaque to one Shamsul Arefin in the year 1966 and subsequently the said Md. Ishaque entered into an Agreement for Sale with the Petitioner on 2.5.1976. Thereafter, the Court of Settlement called for the particulars of the said sale by its order dated 16.11.1992 from the office of the District Registrar, Dhaka. The District Registrar informed that Md. Ishaque executed a Sale Deed in favour of one Mahirunnessa on 9.6.1966 being Sale Deed No. 9336. Against the said order dated 16.11.1992 the Petitioner filed Writ Petition No. 494 of 1992 but that was rejected summarily. Thereafter, the learned Court of Settlement fixed 12.10.1993 for hearing of the case on which date the Petitioner filed an application stating that on thorough enquiry he came to learn that the alleged deed of 1966 was a forged one and the vendor Md. Ishaque did not execute the same and the Petitioner filed another Title Suit being no. 273 of 1993 before the First Court of Assistant Judge praying for declaration that the alleged Deed of Sale No. 9336 dated 9.6.1966 was forged, null and void and also prayed for keeping the proceedings of the case in abeyance till disposal of the aforesaid Suit. Refusing such prayer, the learned Court fixed 13.10.1993 for Judgment. On the date fixed the Court of Settlement delivered the judgment dismissing the case. At this juncture the Petitioner filed this Writ Petition challenging the judgment and Order dated 13.10.1993 and obtained the present Rule and stay. 

 3. The Respondent Government has contested the Rule by filing an Affidavit-in-Opposition denying all the materials facts made in the application contending inter alia that the case property originally belonged to Md. Ishaque who sold it to one Mahirunnessa wife of Shamsul Arefin by a registered, Sale Deed being No. 9336 dated 9.6.1966. It is asserted that since such purchase, she had been possessing the same till 1971 and that she left the property and this country during the War of Independence for unknown destination and her whereabouts are unknown to the Government as such the property in question has been declared as abandoned property under The Bangladesh Abandoned Property (Control, Management and Disposal) Order 1972 (P.O. No.16 of 1972). The Respondent's contention is that since Md. Ishaque had no subsisting or saleable interest in the property in the year 1976 to transfer to the Petitioner, the Petitioner in fact has purchased the Case Property from a person who had no right, title and interest in the said property and by the purchase the Petitioner acquired no right, title and possession in the property. 

 4. Mr. Md. Alim Hossain, the learned Advocate appearing for the Petitioners (heirs of the original Petitioner Badsha Mollah, now deceased) submits that the original lessee Md. Ishaque was in possession, control and management of the property in question and he never left this country at any time and he was all along present in Bangladesh as a Bangladeshi national and was an employee of Pubali Bank till his death. While the said Md. Ishaque was in possession of the property he entered into an Agreement on 2.5.1976 for Sale with the deceased Petitioner Badsha Mollah for a consideration of Tk. 15,000/- out of which he paid Tk.10,000/- as earnest money. Mr. Hossain also submits that the original owner Md. [Masque refused to execute and register the Sale Deed demanding more money. Finding no alternative Badsha Mollah filed Title Suit No. 83 of 1977 for a decree of specific performance of contract against Md. Ishaque and making the Government as defendant in the Suit. The said Title Suit was decreed ex paste on 27.1.1978. Thereafter, the Petitioner got the Sale Deed registered through the Court on 8.6.1978 by filing Title Execution Case No. 16 of 1978. It is also argued that pursuant to Article 7 of P.O. 16 of 1972 and Section 5(1)(a) of the Abandoned Buildings (supplementary provisions) Ordinance, 1985 ("Ordinance") no notice was served upon the original Petitioner and the Government could not show any paper to the effect that the property had on any material date been taken possession of as an abandoned property and as such the listing of the case property in the "Ka" List is ex facie illegal and without lawful authority. It is also argued that the Petitioners claim to be in possession of the case property on the basis of an Agreement for Sale of 1976 and by virtue of a decree passed by the Civil Court in Title Suit No. 83 of 1976 and as such the possession of the Petitioner cannot be said to be unlawful. Mr. Hossain further submits that the Petitioner got the registered Sale Deed through Court by way of execution of a decree passed in Title Suit No. 83 of 1976 against the Government and as such the Government is legally estopped from raising the claim that the case property is an abandoned property. It follows, Mr. Hossain submits, that in view of the said decree the Government cannot claim that the property is an abandoned one and the Court of Settlement's judgment and order is submitted to be a perverse one and liable to be declared illegal and passed without lawful authority. It is also argued that the Petitioner filed another Title Suit being No. 1019 of 1981 against the Government for a decree of a declaration of title of the Petitioner in the case property which was decreed ex- parte on 28.2.1983. To set the said decree aside the Government filed Miscellaneous Case No. 50 of 1986 wherein the original lessee Md. Ishahque appeared and filed written objection denying the claim of the Government and admitting title and possession of the Petitioner. The said Miscellaneous Case was dismissed on contest on 16.11.1988 and no further step was taken by the Government against dismissal of the Miscellaneous Case. In these circumstances, the Petitioners submit, the property cannot be declared as on abandoned property and the very enlistment of the property in the abandoned buildings list as "Ka" List property is illegal and without lawful authority. It is also argued that the lessee Md. Ishaque claiming the property as not abandoned property filed an application before the S.D.O. South, Dhaka being Miscellaneous Petition No. 78 of 1974. In that proceeding the Officer-in-charge, Abandoned Property decided that the property in question is not an abandoned property and recommended a release of the some by his order dated 12.10.1974. In support of his submissions Mr. Hossain has referred to the cases of Bangladesh Vs. Md. Shahjahan reported in 2 ADC, P-411, Abdur Rashid Mollah-vs-Bangladesh and another reported in 2 ADC, 245, Bangladesh Vs. Chairman, Court of Settlement and others reported in 50 DLR (AD), 93, Feroz Ahmed Vs. Bangladesh reported in 13 BLD, 160. Facts of those cases are, however, found by this Court to be different and distinguishable from the case at band. 

 5. Mr. Shahidul Islam, learned Deputy Attorney General and Mr. Sukumar Biswas learned Assistant Attorney General appearing on behalf of the Government have submitted extensively on the facts and issues raised in the Affidavit-in-Opposition. They argued that the case property was legally enlisted in the "Ka" List of abandoned buildings under the relevant provisions of the Ordinance. They submit that the case property was originally allotted to Md. Ishaque on 31.1.1957. The said Md. Ishaque subsequently transferred the case property to one Mohirunnessa, wife of Shamsul Arefin by a registered Deed of Sale being No. 9336 dated 9.6.1966. The said Mohirunnessa left this country during the War of Independence leaving the case property uncared for. Resultantly, the case property was declared abandoned under the relevant provisions of law and the property vested in the Government under P.O. 16 of 1972. Consequentially, the said Md. Ishaque has had no right, title and interest in the said property to transfer to the Petitioner after 1966. It is also argued that the Agreement for Sale and the subsequent different proceedings in different cases and the decree thereof are collusive and created by the Petitioner only for the purpose of grabbing the property of the Government. For that reason the Petitioner has not acquired any interest, right, title and possession in the property. 

 6. Both the learned Deputy Attorney General and Assistant Attorney General also submit that the Suit for specific performance of contract remained barred under section 6 of the Ordinance and the Government is not bound by the said decree because it does not reflect a substantive determination of any issue regarding the abandoned character of the property. In this regard the ratio decidendi of the judgment in CQMH Md. Ayub Ali Vs. Bangladesh and others reported in 47 DLR(AD)71 and Bangladesh Vs. A.T.M. Mannan and others reported in 1 BLC(AD) 8 are relied upon. It is also argued that the onus is on the claimant to prove that the property is not an abandoned property. The Government has no obligation to deny the fact alleged by the claimant or to disclose the basis of listing the property as abandoned property merely because the claimant disputed the same. Mr. Shahidul Islam also argued that, admittedly the possession of the case property was not delivered either by Md. Ishaque or by the Court to the Petitioner, therefore, the claim of the Petitioner to be in possession of the case property on the basis of bainanama and the registered Deed obtained through Court is absolutely false and unbelievable. It is also argued that enlistment of any property under Section 5(1) of the Ordinance is conclusive proof of fact that the property has been legally enlisted as an abandoned property in the Gazette and it is from him who claims the property as not an abandoned property to prove that fact and rebut the position taken by the Government treating the property as an abandoned one. It is also argued that the Court of Settlement has rightly observed in its judgment and order that the Petitioner has totally failed to prove his case by submitting relevant documents before it or indeed by otherwise establishing the presence of the original owner in this country on or before P.O. 16 of 1972 came into force and acquisition of title by his alleged vendor. It is further argued that in the absence of title of Md. Ishaque in the case property the Petitioner on the basis of Agreement for Sale and decrees in Title Suit No. 83 of 1977 and Title Suit No. 1019 of 1981 has not acquired any right, title and interest in the property. 

 11. In the present case the Petitioner claims that the original lessee Md. Ishaque was the owner in possession of the property and through the said Md. Ishaque the Petitioner claims his title and possession of the property and also claims that the Petitioner on the basis of an Agreement for Sale entered into the possession of the case property and got the Sale Deed through Court in execution of the decree passed in Title Suit No. 83 of 1978. Thereafter, his title has been again confirmed by a decree passed in Title Suit No. 1019 of 1981. On the other hand, the definite case of the Government is that the property belonged to one Mohirunnessa by purchase from the said Md. Ishaque by a Deed of Sale being No. 9336 dated 9.6.1966 and as such the Petitioner has not acquired any right, title and interest in the property since he claims his title through Md. Ishaque who in fact had no right, title and interest in the property at the time of execution of the agreement in the year 1976. Therefore, he enlistment of the case property as abandoned one in the "Ka" List is legal, valid and lawful. 

 12. In view of the present situation and the question raised by the Government regarding title of said Md. Ishaque and Mohirunnessa, it appears that the Court of Settlement called for the Sale Deed dated 9.6.1966 from the Office of the Sub-Registrar's Record Room and examined one of the Office Assistants of the Record Room. In support of the Deed called for by the Court and upon examination the Court of Settlement found that the original allottee Md. Ishaque sold the case property to one Mohirunnessa in the year 1966 and therefore, he had no subsisting interest thereafter in the case property and observed that Md. Ishaque could neither enter into an agreement for sale of the property to the Petitioner nor have any other person on behalf of him sell the suit property and also observed that the decree for specific performance of contract passed in Title Suit No. 83 of 1977 as well as the decree passed in Title suit No. 1019 of 1981 is void ab initio and by the said decrees no title passed to the Petitioner. It is also observed by the Court of Settlement that the Petitioner was afforded sufficient opportunity to produce documents of the original lessee of the property and to depose before that Court. But the Petitioner repeatedly sought adjournments and utterly failed to produce any document in original to prove his case and also failed to produce Md. Ishaque before the Court. It is also observed that the Petitioner did not file the original allotment letter before the Court of Settlement but he filed an attested copy of the allotment letter instead of original one which led the Court to believe that the original allotment letter was delivered to Mohirunnessa by the original lessee Md. Ishaque. 

 13. Moreover, from a perusal of the decrees passed in Title Suit No. 83 of 1977 and 1019 of 1981 it appears that there is no declaration in either decree that the building is not an abandoned properly or that it has not vested in the Government under P.O. 16 of 1972. Nor, is there any direction upon the Government to return the building to the Petitioner or release it from the List of abandoned buildings. The decrees do not require the Government to do anything. So, the aforesaid decrees do not come within the proviso of Section 5 of the Ordinance which runs thus: 

 15. From a perusal of the Agreement for Sale of 1976 and the decrees passed in Title Suit No. 83 of 1977 and 1019 of 1981 nowhere is it found that the possession was delivered to the Petitioner by Md. Ishaque or he got the possession through Court. The preamble of the Gazette published on 23.9.86 shows that the declaration by its own express terms permits of construction to the effect that the properties listed in the Notification have already been taken control of by the Government and that the Notification is predicated on that essential fact of control assumed over such property . Furthermore, this has to be read with Section 114, illustration (e) of the Evidence Act, 1872 that permits of a presumption of regularity to be attached to all governmental function discharged in due course. Furthermore, the Petitioner could not satisfy the Court of Settlement by producing any evidence that the vendor Md. Ishaque was in possession of the property in question at the time of execution of the alleged bainanama in the year 1976 or indeed before or after the P.O. 16 of 1972 came into force. From this it is to be deduced that the Notification as above records not only the listing of certain properties as abandoned properties but more importantly the fact of these having passed into the control, supervision and management of the Government at the material date in due course. 

 16. We have gone through the judgment and order of the Court of Settlement and this Court finds that the Court of Settlement considered all the crucial questions raised before it and the Court of Settlement rightly decided the questions considering all the papers and evidences placed before it on the very day of the delivery of judgment. It is also this Court's view that subsequent to the judgment of the Court of Settlement the Petitioner obtained a decree in Title Suit No. 273 of 1993 filed against the said Mohirunnessa and the Government simply to forestall the judgment of the Court of Settlement. It is also found that the Petitioner on different dates by Supplementary Affidavits submitted some documents which were not produced before the Court of Settlement at the time of hearing of the case. Therefore, the Court of Settlement on the basis of the documents available before it considered the case as on the date of delivery of the judgment.

parties:
Md. Shetaur Rahman ------ Petitioner.
Vs.
The Government of Bangladesh represented by the Deputy Commissioner, 
Chapai Nawabganj and others ------ Opposite parties.
full_judgment:
The Rule issued in this Civil Revision under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (shortly the Code, 1908) is about sustainability of the judgment and order dated 22-07-2003 by which the learned Joint District Judge, Chapai Nawabganj dismissed Title Appeal No. 142 of 2001 and thereby affirmed the judgment of dismissal dated 16-10-2001 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Chapai Nawabganj in Other Class Suit No. 187 of 1997. 

 The plaintiff claims that the original owner being the C.S. recorded tenant Panchu Halder sold the suit land to one Saad Imani Mondal by kabala dated 09-4-1946. Plaintiff’s grand father Abdus Sattar purchased the suit land by kabala dated 21-04-1975 from the said Saad Imani Mondal and subsequently transferred the same to the plaintiff by a registered deed of heba-bil-ewaj dated 05-08-1997. Since before the said hiba-bil-ewaj, plaintiff with the consent of his grandfather, has been running his business of motor repairing by constructing a garage on the suit land. But on 21-8-1997 the local Tahshilder refused to accept the rent from the plaintiff on the ground that the suit land is a khas land of the Government recorded in Khaktian No. 1. Hence the suit. 

 The defendants deny plaintiffs title and possession as stated in the plaint. They claim that the suit land was the excess land of the C.S. recorded Zaminder and that it has been correctly recorded in the S.A. and R. S. khatian in the name of the Government. The local people have been running a school on the suit plot named Nawabganj Zilla School since 1996. However a portion of the plot measuring 3.02 decimal is a vacant land which is under process of lease to a private individual named Jarjis. 

 The trial Court framed five issues, namely on (1) maintainability of the suit, (2) limitation, (3) defect of party, (4) title and possession of the plaintiff, and (5) the relief prayed for. 

 The trial Court decided issue Nos. 1-3 with regard to maintainability, limitation and defect of party in favor of the plaintiff. But the trial Court decided issue No. 4 against the plaintiff upon recording a finding that the plaintiff failed to prove his title and possession. Accordingly the trial court dismissed the suit. 

 At the hearing, of this Revision, Mr. Tushar Kanti Roy, the learned Advocate for the plaintiff (petitioner), submits that the courts below failed to consider the material evidence on record about plaintiff’s title and possession namely the original copy of the kabala dated 09-4-1946 (Exhibit-2) executed by the C.S. tenant Panchu Halder in favour of Saad Imani Mondaol and the original copy of kabala dated 21-04-1975 executed by the said purchaser Saad Imani Mondal in favour of plaintiff’s grand father and the deed of Heba-bil-Ewaz dated 05-08-1997 Exhibit-2(a) executed by the grandfather in favour of the plaintiff. 

 In reply Mr. Jabber, the learned Assistant Attorney General (AAG) submits that the courts below recorded concurrent findings on the relevant questions of fact with regard to the title and possession and therefore no interference is necessary in this Revision. 

 Mr. Jaber, the learned AAG next submits that the total quantum of the land as recorded in the 4(four) R.S. khatians filed in this court is about 40 decimals which exceeds the total quantum of the original C.S. plot measuring 27 decimals and therefore the story presented by the plaintiff about the remaining 15 decimals of the suit plot is not at all credible. . 

 The trial Court considered other evidence on record and recorded finding that plaintiff totally failed to prove his title and possession. 

 The appellate Court with reference to contents of the original kabala dated 09-04-1946 executed by C.S. tenant Panchu Haldar in favour of he said Saad Imani Mondal recorded a finding to the effect that the kabala is not credible evidence. Because it contains overwriting on the signature of the executant and there are clear marks of erasing and some writing with different ink. The appellate Court recorded a further finding that seal of the Sub-registry office was not as old as of 1946 but clearly indicates that it was recently affixed.

parties:
Bodrul Ahsan (Md) ----- Petitioner
Vs.
Janata Bank Ltd and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
The respondent No. 1 Janata Bank as plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 307 of 2000 in the Court of Artha Rin Adalat, Court No. 1, Dhaka against the Respondent Nos. 2 and 3 impleading them as defendant No. 1 and 2 respectively and Md Abdul Hadi (father of the petitioner) as defendants No. 3 for realization of Taka 4,45,865 as on 30-11-2000. The suit was decreed ex-parte in the preliminary form on 11-10-2001. After that, the preliminary decree was made final on 14-5-2002. 

 4. According to the reports of the process server dated 6-2-2001 and 6-6-2001 summons were issued upon the defendant No. 3 Md Abdul Hadi, but the same were returned unserved, and on that ground Artha Rin Adalat allowed the Miscellaneous Case No. 52 of 2007 on 4-6-2008 by setting aside the aforementioned ex-parte judgment and decree and restored the suit to its original number and file and also stayed the operation of the certificate issued under sub-section (5) of section 33 of the Artha Rin Adalat AM, 2003 and recalled the same and further directed the defendant No. 3 Md Abdul Hadi to file his written statement on 4-7-2008. 

 7. After that, the defendant No. 3 paid the entire decretal amount through pay orders which were accepted by the Adalat on 12-8-2009, 7-10-2009 and 4-1-2010. After complying with the Court's direction, the defendant No. 3 filed an application on 4-1-2010 under section 57 of the Ain for redemption of the mortgaged property and to return all his title deeds and documents. After hearing the said application, the Artha Rin Adalat, Court No. 1, Dhaka rejected the said application on 16-6-2010. 

 9. The respondent No. 1 by filling affidavit-in-opposition opposes the Rule and contends that the respondent No. 2-3 failed to pay the loan within time. Then, the respondent No. 1 bank filed Title Suit No. 307 of 2000 in the Court of Sub-Judge, Dhaka for realization of Taka 4,45,065 as on 30-11-2000. The suit was decreed ex-parte in the preliminary form on 11-10-2001 and the same was made final on 14-5-2002. In the decree, the defendants were directed to pay the decretal amount by 90 days. But the defendants failed to do so. Therefore, the respondent No. 1 bank filed Title Execution Case No. 52 of 2003. Thereafter, the Court fixed date for auction sale of the mortgaged property on 28-9-2004, but no bidder participated and the next date was fixed on 10-2-2005. On that date, 3 (three) bidders took part and one of whom Md Nazir Uddin became the highest bidder. Since the bid money was not sufficient, the court refused to accept the same by its order dated 27-2-2005. Thereafter, the respondent No. 1 Bank filed an application under section 33(5) of the Artha Rin Ain, 2003. After hearing the said application, the Adalat on 20-8-2005 issued certificate. Thereafter, the respondent No. 1 bank invited tender for auction sale of the mortgaged property. The tender was published on 23-11-2005 and 25-11-2005 in the Daily Sangbad and Daily Amardesh. M/s River View Limited got the property at Taka 10,50,000 vide sale deed No. 3261 dated 27-2-2006. After adjusting the bank debt of Taka 9,75,289.75, the rest of Taka 89,410.27 was kept for the mortgagor petitioner as per provision of section 33(5) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 and accordingly as per provision of section 33(9) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, the said Title Execution Case was finally disposed of. 

 10. Mr Jamir Uddin Sirker, the learned Advocate appearing with Mr Garib-E-Newaz, the learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that the title suit No. 307 of 2000 was initially decreed exparte without serving summons upon the defendant No. 3 Md Abdul Hadi (father of the petitioner) and thereafter, upon application filed by the defendant No. 3 under sub-section (2) of section 19 of the Artha Rin, 2003, the Artha Rin Adalat, Court No. 1, Dhaka restored the aforesaid title suit to its original number and file on 4-6-2008 and after that the said title suit was renumbered as Artha Rin Suit No. 377 of 2008 of First Artha Rin Adalat, Dhaka and thereafter the said suit was decreed on contest on 26-4-2009. He further submits that as per decree, the defendant No. 3 paid the entire dues of the respondent bank duly, thereafter, the defendant No. 3 is legally entitled to get release of his mortgaged land. 

 11. He further submits that since the decree dated 26-4-2009 is still in force, therefore, there is no scope to say that the order of installment to pay the dues of the bank is not proper and the order for payment of money by the defendant No. 3 is not entertain able. He also submits that after variation or reversal of the decree, law entails to restore everything to its previous position and place the parties in the original position, as such there is no scope to say that the dues of the bank has been adjusted before passing the decree on 26-4-2009. 

 17. In this case, the admitted position is that the Title Suit No. 307 of 2000 was decreed ex-parte in the preliminary from on 11-10-2001 and was made final on 14-5-2002. Then, the defendant No. 3 (father of the writ petitioner) filed Miscellaneous Case No. 52 of 2007 under section 19(2) of Artha Rin Adalat for setting aside the aforesaid ex-parte judgment and decree, which was allowed on 4-6-2008. Further it is admitted that the suit was renumbered as Artha Rin Suit No. 377 of 2008 and the same was decreed on contest on 26-4-2009. It is also admitted that neither the respondent No. 1 bank nor the auction purchaser challenged the said decree dated 26-4-2009. 

 30. In this case, the Artha Rin Adalat was functus officio after it handed down its decision. Its function was completed when it rendered its final award. The fact that the original decision was wrong or made without jurisdiction is irrelevant to the issue of functus officio. 

 37. In light of the aforesaid fact and law, we are of the view that the Rule should be made absolute. Accordingly, we set aside the order dated 16-6-2010 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat, Court No. 1, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 377 of 2008 and remit the matter to the Court below to be dealt with in accordance with law.

parties:
Mina Begum and others ------ Plaintiff-Petitioners
Vs.
Joj Miah ------- Defendant-Opposite Party
full_judgment:
This Rule, on an application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure (in short, the CPC) at the instance of the plaintiff-petitioners was issued calling upon the opposite party No. 1 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 29-5-2012 and 4-6-2012 respectively passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Brahmanbaria, in Title Appeal No. 62 of 2009 affirming the judgment and decree dated 14-7-2009 and 20-7-2009 respectively passed by the learned Assistant Judge (in-charge) Akhaura, Brahmanbaria in Title Suit No. 69 of 2007 dismissing the suit should not be set-aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule, in short, is that the late plaintiff Mohammad Ali, now being dead, instituted the above suit for declaration of his title into the suit land by adverse possession averring, inter-alia, that 0.15 acres of land appertains to settlement plot No. 209 corresponding to BS plot No. 575 of settlement khatian No. 60 of Noorpur mouza under Akhaura Police Station of Brahamanbaria district originally belonged to the defendant No. 1 who purchased the same from others on 25-6-1975. 

 7. The further case of the defendant is that he had purchased the suit land from his uncle Ali Akbar by a registered deed on 25-6-1975. At the time of preparation of the recent record of right, the defendant handed over the original deed of the suit land to the plaintiff to get his (defendant) name recorded and accordingly the hal record of right has been prepared in the name of the defendant. The plaintiffs taking the advantage of his possession into the suit land on behalf of the defendant and also using the original deed have been claiming the suit land on some false plea. The claim of title of the plaintiff into the suit land is false and frivolous. The defendant did never sell the suit land to the plaintiff a consideration of Taka 20,000. So, the suit is liable to be dismissed with costs. 

 8. Upon the above pleadings, the trial Court framed as many as 4 issues to dispose of the suit. The plaintiff examined 6 witnesses and submitted some papers which were duly marked as exhibits in the suit while the defendant examined 4 witnesses but did not adduce any documentary evidence. The trial Court on consideration of the evidence on record dismissed the suit and as against the said judgment of the trial Court, the plaintiff preferred Title Appeal No. 62 of 2009 in the Court of District Judge, Brahmanbaria and the appeal was ultimately heard by the Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Brahmanbaria who by his impugned judgment and decree affirmed the judgment of the trial Court. The petitioners being the substituted heirs of late original plaintiff moved this Court and obtained the present Rule. The Rule is resisted by the sole defendant-opposite party. 

 9. Mr Mohammad Mobarak Hossain, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners supports the Rule. He submits that though the petitioners have come in this Court against the judgment and decree of affirmance but if the very basis of the concurrent findings of the two Courts below appears to be as misconception or based on no evidence, such concurrent findings cannot claim any immunity from this Court. He also submits that the plaintiff filed the original suit for declaration of his title by way of adverse possession asserting his uninterrupted and continuous possession in to the suit land from 1981 till filing of the suit in 2007. But the Courts below did not at all consider the possession of the plaintiff into the suit land. 

 10. He further submits that the plaintiff very successfully proved his possession into the suit land and since the suit was for declaration of title by way of adverse possession, the Courts below should have considered the continuous possession of the plaintiff. He taking me through exhibit-3 submits that the defendant filing a petition before the Upazilla Nirbahi Officer, Akhaura, Brahmanbaria had admitted the forcible possession of the plaintiff into the suit land and this admission of the defendant is very much consistent with the case of the plaintiff that the plaintiff has been possessing the suit land forcibly denying the title of the defendant into the suit land. But both the Courts below overlooking the exhibit-3 dismissed the suit and this kind of non-consideration of material evidence by the Courts below is an error of law and when there is error of law in taking decision by the Appellate Court below this Court can interfere into the decision of the appellate Court below. 

 12. The learned Advocate also submits that since the suit was for declaration of title by way of adverse possession the prime consideration of the Courts below should have been whether the plaintiff has been possessing the suit land adversely from 1981 till filing of the suit and though the plaintiff had proved the said facts successfully by the local witnesses but even then the Courts below without considering such evidence very arbitrarily and capriciously dismissed the suit. So, the impugned judgment and decree of the Appellate Court below is liable to be set-aside decreeing the suit in favour of the plaintiff. 

 13. On the other hand, Mr Mohammad Abul Kashem Bhuiyan the learned Advocate appearing for the sole defendant-opposite party opposing the Rule very strenuously contends that the plaintiff filed the suit for declaration of his title by way of adverse possession but the plaint itself discloses that he was admitting the title of the defendant into the suit land till 13-8-2006 and 28-11-2006. In order to succeed in a suit like this, the plaintiff is to prove his adverse possession into the suit land for more than 12 years but if the adverse possession of the plaintiff is counted in this particular suit from 13-8-2006 of 28-11-2006 his such possession appears to be hostile for one year only as against the defendant as the suit was filed in 2007. 

 14. He very categorically submits that there is no date of any sale and also as to when the plaintiff was inducted into the possession pursuant to his alleged purchase from the defendant. Then the plaint shows that the plaintiff admitting the title of the defendant till 2006 demanded the kabala from him (defendant). So, if it is conceded for a moment that the plaintiff had purchased the suit land in 1981 from the defendant but his (plaintiff) possession from 1981 to 2006 was never a hostile possession against the real owner, the defendant as he had admitted the ownership of the defendant during those period of time. 

 16. He also submits that in 1990, the field survey for the recent record of right was going on in the locality, as such the defendant handed over the original kabala of the suit land to the plaintiff in the normal course of family business to get his name recorded and accordingly the plaintiff did the same. Had there been any fact of sale in 1981, the plaintiff must not have allowed the defendant to record his name in 1990. So, all these facts reveal that in fact before 1990 there was no any event of sale between the parties. But whenever the plaintiff got the original kabala from his brother for the preparation of the record of right he being misguided unethically claimed his ownership using the said original deed into the suit kind. 

 19. In this Rule, it is admitted that the defendant was the owner of the suit land in question and he had purchased it from his uncle on 25-6-1975. The case of the plaintiff is that he had purchased the suit land from his step brother, the defendant and pursuant to the said purchase he has possessed the suit land from 1981. But interestingly it is important to note here that neither in the plaint nor in the evidence of the plaintiff there is any definite date as to when he (plaintiff) was inducted into the possession of the suit land. In the plaint it was averred among other that in presence of the common relations and the witnesses, the plaintiff had purchased the suit land. The plaintiff examined as many as 6 witnesses in the suit but none of them is the witness of the sale in question and both the Courts below considered this fact of the suit in a very right way. In this regard, the learned Advocate for the petitioner argued that since the plaintiff claims title by way of adverse possession, the evidence in order to prove the purchase of the land and the date of possession thereof is immaterial. But I find it difficult to have any substance in this argument. The defendant denied the adverse possession of the plaintiff into the suit land. So, there should have been a definite date from when the plaintiff started to possess the suit land. In the case of Sheikh Farid (Md) and others vs Abdul Wadud Sikdar and others reported in 58 DLR (AD) 248 the appellate division did not rely upon the plea of adverse possession simply for the want of any date of starting time of possession. The Appellate Division observed the said fact in the following manner: 

 "The plaintiff was required to establish from what particular point of time he started to possess the land in assertion of his title upon denying the title of the real owner i.e. Karuna Moyee Dasi. The evidence from plaintiff's side is totally lacking for establishing the fact that from a particular point of time he started to possess the land asserting his title upon denying the title of the real owner to his knowledge as well as to the knowledge of the others and since that date he was possessing the land for more than 12 years. In our view, there is no evidence that at any particular point of time the plaintiff claimed title in the land in suit on the basis of adverse possession or, -in other words, claimed his title in the land upon denying the title of the real owner." (para 10 of the judgment) 

 21. Adverse possession means possession of a person in hostility and adversely against the real owner with the knowledge of the real owner and others and same must be very open and notorious against the real owner also. But surprisingly in the suit I find that the plaintiff had requested the defendant although till 2006 for having a kabala from him and it is in the admission of the plaintiff that on 30-8-2006 on his request the defendant denied to execute and register a kabala in his favour. This fact means and includes that the plaintiff has been possessing the suit land admitting the right and title of the defendant till 30-8-2006. So, if it is conceded for a moment that the plaintiff was in possession of the suit land from 1981 to 2006 how this sort of possession can be considered as adverse possession against the real owner. The possession of the plaintiff can be at best hostile and adverse after 30-8-2006 only when the defendant denied to execute the kabala in favour of the plaintiff. The trial Court and the appellate Court below considering all these facts and circumstances came to a sound conclusion that the possession of the plaintiff was never a hostile and adverse into the suit land against the defendant The Courts below also found that since he was living in the native village of the defendant, he used to look after the joint property of the plaintiff and the defendant including the suit land. I find no illegality in the finding and decisions of the Court below based on proper appreciation of the evidence and other materials on record. 

 22. In my consideration, the plaint of the plaintiff is sufficient to hold that his possession was never hostile from 1981 to 2006 as within this period he was requesting the defendant to execute and register a kabala admitting his title. The hostile and adverse possession of the plaintiff was started in fact from 30-8-2006 when the defendant denied to execute and register a kabala and within one year of 2006 the suit was filed. So the said one year is not sufficient to consider the claim adverse possession of the plaintiff. 

 23. Whenever the plaintiff claims title by adverse possession he is under duty bound to prove that his possession was adverse and hostile against the real owner for more that 12 years within the knowledge of the real owner and others. But in this particular case, the plaintiff could not prove that his possession was hostile for more than 12 years against the defendant.

parties:
Md. Akther Hasan
Vs.
Md. Ruhul Amin Moral and another
full_judgment:
2. Material facts of the case as necessary for disposal of the Rule are that the present petitioner as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 31 of 2002 in the Court of Assistant Judge, 2nd Court, Narayangonj which was subsequently re-numbered on transfer as Title Suit No.279 of 2006. During the pendency of the suit for peremptory hearing the plaintiff petitioner could not attend before the Court on 31.7.2007 as a result of which the suit was dismissed for default. The plaintiff thereupon, filed Misc. Case No.12 of 2007 in the Court of Bandar Assistant Judge, Narayangonj for restoration of Title Suit No. 279 of 2006 after recalling the order of dismissal dated 31.7.2007. The learned Assistant Judge by his order dated 29.10.2007 rejected the Misc. Case. 

 4. Mr. Md. Khalilur Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff-petitioner submits that both the Courts below erred in law in rejecting the prayer for restoration of Title Suit No.279 of 2006 without properly considering the facts of the case and the case made out by the petitioner and the same has occasioned failure of justice. 

 9. On perusal of the record, it appears that the petitioner filed Misc. Case tinder Order IX, Rule 9 CPC for restoration of Title Suit No.279 of 2006 stating the ground that the plaintiff-petitioner was bedridden from 27.7.2007 to 12.09.2007 for the disease of hepatitis and thus he could not be present before the trial Court along with witnesses on 31.07.2007. 

 11. On scrutiny of the impugned judgment and order dated 9.12.2007 together with the order of the trial Court dated 29.10.2007 passed in Misc. Case No.12 of 2007 and order dated 31.7.2007 passed in Title Suit No. 279 of 2006, it appears that the Title Suit No.279 of 2006 was dismissed for default due to non-payment of C.P. cost of Tk.300/- rejecting the application for time and thereafter, the Misc. Case was disallowed on the ground that the plaintiff-petitioner took a different plea for restoring the Misc. Case. 

 13. Furthermore at the far end of the hearing the learned Advocate for the petitioner upon placing an application for undertaking filed by the petitioner on 29.05 submits that the plaintiff-petitioner is now ready to pay Tk. 25,000/- as cost, if the suit being Title Suit No. 279 of 2006 is restored to its original file and number on recalling the order dated 31.7.2007 dismissing the suit. 

 14. In view of all the facts noticed above I am of the view that the plaintiff petitioner has a reasonable claim for restoring the suit being Title Suit No.279 of 2006 and both the Courts below committed illegality in not setting aside the dismissal order dated 31.7.2007. The impugned order as well as order of the trial Court below dated 29.19.2007 and 31.7.2017 are totally unsatisfactory and the same calls for interference. 

 15. In the result, the Rule is made absolute. The impugned order dated 9.12.2007 passed in Misc. Appeal No.102 of 2007 is set-aside and consequently. Misc. Case No.12 of 2007 is allowed and the suit being Title Suit No.279 of 2006 is restored to its original file and number on condition that the plaintiff-petitioner shall deposit a sum of Tk. 25,000/- (twenty five thousand) as cost within 1 (one) month from the date of receipt of this order before the trial Court as prayed for.

parties:
Shamir Chandra Sajwal and others ------ Plaintiff-Respondent-Petitioners.
Vs.
Government of Bangladesh ------ Defendant- Appellant- Opposite-Party
full_judgment:
The Rule issued on an application filed under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure at the instance of the plaintiff-respondent-petitioners calling upon the Opposite-Party to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 3-11-2010 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 3rd Court, Barisal in Title Appeal No. 114 of 2009 allowing the appeal and setting-aside those dated 19-4-2009 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Muladi, Barisal in Title Suit No. 106 of 2005 should not be set-aside and/or pass such other order or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus, the land measuring 1.92 acres appertaining to CS Khatian No. 3 in plot No. 272 of Mouza-Shaheber Char, under police station Goumadi at present Muladi, District-Barisal originally belonged to one Avoy Sajwal, Kanu Sajwal and Gopal Sajwal in equal shares. 1.59 acres of land of entire CS plot No. 273 of CS Khatian No. 4 of the said Mouza belonged to one Harachandra, Durgacharan and Sreecharan Sajwal in equal share. 2.13 acres of land of plot No. 274 in CS Khatian No. 35 of the said Mouza belonged to one Kukuri Sajwal, Bhagaban Sajwal, Brindaban Sajwal and Prosannya Sajwal in equal share. 9.49 acres of land of plot Nos. 173, 174, 175, 176, 177, 178, 179 & 180 of CS Khatian No. 66 originally belonged to one Dasharath Sajwal in 3 annas 4 gandas share, Hari Charan Sajwal in 9 annas 12 gandas share and Mohonbashi, Golak Bashi Sajwal in 1 arena 12 gandas share each.
